issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
🤖 An agent literature survey for the Mochi post-training recipe found two Nemotron-sourced changes for train/inference mismatch in async MoE RL. Mochi RL already uses one of them (router replay). The other, an FP32 LM head, has not been tested by us. Nothing here was measured empirically on Mochi: this is a pointer for the RL team, not a result.

**What Nemotron reports**
- The [Nemotron 3.5 Super/Lightning technical report](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-and-Lightning-Technical-Report.pdf) (RL section) says router replay plus an FP32 LM head "reduce the KL error between the training and inference engines by more than an order of magnitude". The two are reported together, so the report does not say how much each one contributes.
- Aside: the [HF MoE handbook](https://huggingface-moe-blogpost.hf.space/) says the NeMo-RL recipes for Nemotron 3 Super/Ultra freeze the router matrix in async RL and keep the load-balancing bias live, and that "whether replay pays off in reward is still contested". Router freezing is an alternative or a complement to replay.

**Where Mochi stands (from existing work, not new measurements)**
- Router replay: Mochi (Hero) RL already uses captured-route replay, and it passed the recorded 4K RL gate in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10388. Its measured replay result is batch-order sensitivity of the gradient: 71.96% → 1.37% at PP48, with +5.3% scoring-plus-update time. That is not a serve-vs-trainer logprob gap, and the same issue notes that serving–trainer differences persist.
- Bit-identical numerics: the stack beginning with https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10634 was closed in favour of score centering with TIS (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11066, open), with probes in https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10658 (open). The Mochi RL launcher is https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11321 (draft).
- FP32 LM head, serving side: the pinned vLLM fork (`0ac9dcb`) already supports it. `vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py` reads `--hf-overrides '{"head_dtype": "float32"}'` and accumulates the head GEMM into FP32. Its comment says this is "required for RL training-inference consistency". The Mochi serve config (`experiments/evaluation/mochi/model-mochi-sft-step400407.yaml`) does not set it, so served logits are BF16.
- FP32 LM head, trainer side: SkyRL's Megatron wrapper calls the model with `fp32_output=False` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py`), so trainer logits are BF16 too. Matching vLLM would need a Megatron-side FP32 output projection, which is not checked here.
- Related Snowball evidence, not RL and not Mochi: in an Oct 25 Levanter-vs-vLLM scoring check on Snowball, silent MoE token drops and BF16 combine weights were each separate numerics boundaries. Fixing them one at a time cut the p99 per-token logprob gap from 3.96 to 0.60 nats.

**What we did not do:** no empirical study on Mochi of the FP32 head, router freezing, or replay versus no replay. The survey proposed a 1 h arm; it moves off our list and into this issue.

Done when: the RL team decides whether to test an FP32 LM head on both engines (vLLM `head_dtype` plus a Megatron FP32 output projection) on Mochi, measured as the serve-vs-trainer logprob or KL gap on fixed responses with replay on, and records the decision here. Router freezing is optional, as a separate arm.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The draft [Mochi RL recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9/experiments/post_training/mochi_rl/recipe.yaml#L78-L82) enables router replay but has no head-precision override. The [Megatron wrapper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/82cee32cfd5bd479aa0670ba1a92a9c0f96ec4bf/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py#L351-L360) passes `fp32_output=False`; [Megatron's implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/7c0fac795b76180c26e363fa292c1ce2c025c4df/megatron/core/transformer/module.py#L593-L635) shows that changing this flag only casts outputs after the model forward. [#10388](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10388#issuecomment-6379516756) reports a remaining serving–trainer logprob gap with replay, but no Mochi FP32-head result. The evaluation YAML named above is absent from current `main`; #11321 is the active Mochi recipe.

**Relevant code**
- [Mochi generator config](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/75bf9fba6c8419070e87c9f97ddd0478148a27a9/experiments/post_training/mochi_rl/recipe.yaml#L126-L149) — serving precision insertion point.
- [Megatron wrapper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/82cee32cfd5bd479aa0670ba1a92a9c0f96ec4bf/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_model_wrapper.py#L351-L360) — learner forward path.
- [Pinned vLLM head](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee86ccb447bc717259159c41ad456a/vllm/model_executor/layers/logits_processor.py#L142-L177) — FP32 accumulation path.

# Proposed Fix

This needs a paired numerical experiment before a production change. If the RL team allocates the run, use one immutable Mochi checkpoint and fixed responses, routes, replay setting, weights, and scoring layout. Measure four arms: BF16 on both engines, FP32 serving only, FP32 learner only, and FP32 on both. Wire and verify vLLM `hf_overrides: {head_dtype: float32}` in #11321, and implement a genuine FP32-output Megatron head projection; verify its GEMM output precision and backward path rather than relying on `fp32_output=True`.

For each arm, report chosen-token logprob-gap RMS/p99/max, same-token probability-ratio outliers, scorer/serve throughput, and memory, with run IDs and source revisions. Compute full-distribution KL only if full-vocabulary logits are captured. Record the RL team's go/no-go decision against the measured parity gain and cost here; treat router freezing as a separate arm.

🤖 Draft PR [#11671](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11671) adds an opt-in FP32 LM head for SkyRL's TP1 Megatron policy and reference paths, with the recipe schema and trial settings documented. To try it with the draft [Mochi recipe #11321](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11321), set `trainer.policy.megatron_config.fp32_lm_head: true` and `generator.engine_init_kwargs.hf_overrides: {head_dtype: float32}`.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 On Snowball 10/05, FP32 LM heads on both engines reduced the mean absolute train–serve log-probability gap by **0.000111 nats (0.61%)** versus the pooled BF16 runs. The paired 95% prompt-bootstrap interval for those runs was [0.000007, 0.00022] nats. The BF16 repeat shifted the gap by 0.00010 nats. Against the first BF16 run alone, the interval spans zero. The p99 gap did not improve. These runs show no reduction that repeats across independent serve runs. FP32 should stay opt-in for this Snowball setup.

| vLLM / Megatron head | Mean absolute gap | p99 absolute gap | k3 | Chosen-token binary KL | vLLM scored tok/s | Megatron scored tok/s | Peak sampled GiB/GPU | H100-h |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 / BF16 | 0.01803 | 0.16582 | 0.000840 | 0.000269 | 145,543 | 4,764 | 63.88 | 5.06 |
| BF16 / BF16 repeat | 0.01813 | 0.16818 | 0.000872 | 0.000269 | 139,364 | 4,886 | 63.92 | 11.02 |
| FP32 / BF16 | 0.01798 | 0.16705 | 0.000851 | 0.000263 | 120,898 | 4,674 | 64.47 | 5.52 |
| BF16 / FP32 | 0.01809 | 0.16809 | 0.000852 | 0.000273 | 140,430 | 5,379 | 63.98 | 8.38 |
| FP32 / FP32 | 0.01797 | 0.16718 | 0.000850 | 0.000264 | 129,809 | 5,144 | 64.58 | 7.75 |

vLLM's own repeat gap fell from **0.01287 to 0.00692 nats** per token with FP32 output. Megatron's repeated scores matched exactly at both precisions. vLLM scored about **12% fewer tokens per second** on average with the FP32 head in these runs. The throughput columns count scored loss tokens per scorer wall second and exclude startup. No Megatron slowdown was visible in these passes.

Binary KL combines the chosen token and all other tokens into two events, so it is a lower bound on full-vocabulary KL. All train–serve values were finite. In the vLLM repeats, 15 BF16 positions and 6 FP32 positions rounded to log-probability zero on one read and a tiny negative value on the other, yielding infinite binary KL for those positions. The finite-token means were 0.000186 and 0.000098, respectively.

All runs used Snowball 10/05 export ac60d940, the same 512 responses and 480,150 loss tokens, and the same captured expert sets on 12,483,900 replayed token-layer rows. Megatron ran TP1/PP2/CP1/EP8 on 16 H100s and vLLM ran DP8/EP8 on 8 H100s in 02A. Production uses CP5. The FP32 vLLM head used BF16 operands with FP32 accumulation and output. Megatron cast BF16 operands to FP32 and logged FP32 output with TF32 off. The scoring probe used no optimizer steps. This isolates the LM-head change for this checkpoint and layout. The experiment measured scoring parity. Reward and the combined Nemotron router-replay and FP32-head intervention remain untested here.

The independent audit verified head precision and probe and route identity (all 49.9 million expert IDs matched), and reproduced the metrics.

The five successful runs used **37.74 H100-hours**. Including the first collector attempt, which stopped during sandbox startup before scoring, total allocation was **47.40 H100-hours**. Reproduction code and tests are in [the Snowball head probe draft](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11772).

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The adopted Mochi Micro210 round drops the qualified inference transport settings. At `4eea28939be7d293433b21551af750da67a13c11`, the rendered evaluator has no `NCCL_NET=IB`, `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0`, or `NCCL_IB_HCA=ibp`; `trainer.policy.nccl_buffer_size_bytes` resolves to null. Qualification run 502 used these IB settings and a 262144-byte inference-actor NCCL buffer. This prevents the evaluation launch from preserving its qualified serving setup.

Reproduce:
1. Run `experiments.post_training.long_loop.round_runner --round experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-sft-eval.yaml --through eval --version 2026.11.19.110 --source-revision 4eea28939be7d293433b21551af750da67a13c11 --validation-output /tmp/mochi-eval-preflight` from that clean revision with the documented credentials, without `--run`.
2. Inspect `skyrl.extra_env` and `skyrl.trainer.policy.nccl_buffer_size_bytes` in the emitted launch and compiled YAML.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

We built **Mini840 and Micro210, compact validation versions of [Marin Eval Policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197), for our reinforcement-learning (RL) feedback loop**. The aim is to evaluate checkpoints during RL training more cheaply and frequently, so we can track capability changes and choose which checkpoints deserve a full evaluation.

How to build our mini-subset? We tested a few approaches. The final product retains 21 of 26 benchmarks and chooses stratified random sampling over learned task-selection methods. **840 unique tasks in Mini840, with a nested 210-task Micro210 for cheaper checks**. More complicated selectors did not consistently outperform.

With a fitted ridge predictor, random sampling achieved family-held-out **Spearman rank correlation of 0.794 for Micro210 and 0.818 for Mini840**. On the separate four-checkpoint holdout panel, the corresponding correlations were **0.667 and 0.867**.

The shipped datasets provide task rewards for RL validation; they do not include that fitted predictor. Their simplified execution profile and raw score aggregation still need prospective validation against the full policy. Release candidates should continue to receive the full evaluation.

- [Mini840: TaskCompendium validation dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-840).
- [Micro210: TaskCompendium validation dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210).
- [Original-policy reproduction index](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-Policy-Index).

For execution, use the [tested RNO2A launch and MarinSkyRL integration instructions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/36ce62ecb793ef31def1b87ea7847e643e08691e/experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/README.md) in draft #10817. An independent issue-only smoke verified all 21 paths with real Pi tools and original verifiers; see the [sanitized receipt](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-840/blob/64c24ba39d2a7b54e6b880c5ec5073c2dfc43165/runtime/evidence/execution-path-validation.json). The datasets are model agnostic; the reference test launcher is Qwen-specific.

The released validation profile uses **65,536 total context tokens, 16,384 maximum output tokens per turn, thinking enabled throughout, and Pi 0.87.0 for all agentic tasks**. TruthfulQA uses generated-choice truthful-answer accuracy. The separate index preserves the same task membership under original benchmark settings, including original harnesses and likelihood-based TruthfulQA MC2. The simplified validation profile has not yet been prospectively compared with the full policy.

## Scope and experimental design

The sampling pool and prediction target are the same 21 benchmarks: FinanceBench, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ and SOTOPIA-hard are excluded; TriviaQA is retained. We count unique task IDs, keeping prescribed repetitions attached to each task. Micro210 is a prefix of Mini840. The released draw is seed 0 (source RNG seed 20261030), reference fold 1, used for the Qwen timing comparison; it was not selected by maximizing a held-out score.

The initial aggregate exploration used 42 models × 26 benchmark scores from the tracker. The task-level study froze an 18-model cohort: 12 baselines and six Snowball/Grug models, with 48,825 task identities and 41,706 eligible predictor tasks. Related model families were held out together in four outer folds. Task selection, imputation, predictor fitting and IRT dimension selection excluded the held-out families. A separate panel held out four later Snowball checkpoints.

Historical random-subset quality metrics average three seeds and family-specific task eligibility sets; they are not measurements of the single exported draw across every model. The reported tournament weights benchmarks equally and applies the campaign’s infrastructure-adjusted uncertainty threshold. “Random” refers to task selection; a ridge predictor estimates the full benchmark scores from sampled outcomes.

## Experiments and outcomes

### Aggregate-score exploration

1. **Benchmark redundancy and PCA:** on 42 models and all 26 benchmarks, two PCs explained 50.0% of standardized variation and five explained 73.6%. Parallel analysis against 250 shuffled-column replicates retained three components. After the five exclusions, five PCs explained 79.8% across the retained 21 benchmarks. These are in-sample descriptions, not held-out prediction guarantees.
2. **Eight benchmark-level selectors:** raw variance, mutual information, mRMR, PCA loadings, transformed SVD, an IRT-inspired proxy, Lasso and Extra Trees were compared with random benchmark subsets under cross-validation. Reconstruction gains over random were modest and did not consistently preserve rankings. Lasso’s reconstruction advantage was about 7% with six benchmarks and 4% with twelve; random had better mean rank correlation than Lasso at twelve.
3. **Benchmark-removal diagnostics:** PIQA, WinoGrande and BoolQ jointly accounted for 47.9% of PC2’s squared loading mass. Removing them raised two-PC variance explained from 50.0% to 54.2%; adding FinanceBench to the exclusions raised it to 55.8%. Removing all five yielded 45.2%, 58.3%, 67.6%, 74.4% and 79.8% cumulative variance for one through five PCs. This motivated the retained pool; selection then operated on pooled tasks.

[Aggregate analysis](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-Policy-Index/blob/main/analysis/ANALYSIS.md).

### Task-level selection: final 21-to-21 study

The table lists every task-selector variant tested in the final scope. MAE is the mean absolute error in normalized benchmark scores, in percentage points. Rank correlation compares pooled out-of-fold tournament scores; random values average three seeds. Other selectors use one fixed seed.

| Method | Micro210 MAE (pp) | Mini840 MAE (pp) | Micro210 rank correlation | Mini840 rank correlation | Mini840 decisive agreement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Stratified random + ridge (selected)** | **8.58** | **8.21** | **0.794** | **0.818** | **57.4%** |
| Ridge relevance/diversity heuristic | 9.50 | 9.50 | 0.773 | 0.776 | 48.8% |
| Mutual information + redundancy control | 9.39 | 8.93 | 0.789 | 0.847 | 57.3% |
| Greedy selection with inner family CV | 10.27 | 10.31 | 0.600 | 0.626 | 52.9% |
| Greedy CV, cost-weighted | 12.27 | 12.30 | 0.236 | 0.217 | 36.5% |
| Greedy CV, cost + domain coverage | 12.33 | 11.23 | 0.236 | 0.610 | 47.1% |
| Multidimensional IRT, static | 9.64 | 9.44 | 0.695 | 0.732 | 45.9% |
| Multidimensional IRT, adaptive historical replay | 9.50 | 9.24 | 0.717 | 0.732 | 47.1% |
| Static IRT, cost-weighted | 11.27 | 11.16 | 0.632 | 0.538 | 26.1% |
| Adaptive IRT, cost-weighted | 10.33 | 10.54 | 0.818 | 0.676 | 30.7% |
| Static IRT, cost + domain coverage | 10.83 | 10.87 | 0.600 | 0.601 | 26.8% |
| Adaptive IRT, cost + domain coverage | 10.26 | 10.43 | 0.779 | 0.673 | 31.3% |

Random sampling had the lowest score MAE at both budgets. Mutual-information selection slightly improved Mini840 rank correlation (0.847 versus 0.818), with worse score MAE (8.93 versus 8.21 pp) and similar decisive agreement. Cost weighting generally hurt prediction quality. The tested IRT variants did not justify their added complexity.

Greedy selection used three inner family-grouped folds; its objective combined decisive-comparison error with a small score-MAE penalty. Coverage variants reserved probes across reasoning, coding, instruction/structured answers, long context and interactive agents. IRT selected among one, two, three and five dimensions using training-only masked-response validation. Adaptive IRT results use historical response replay; fresh online adaptive execution was not completed.

### Generalization, uncertainty, cost and diagnostic checks

- **Later checkpoints:** random Mini840 achieved mean rank correlation 0.867 and score MAE 5.31 pp; Micro210 achieved 0.667 and 5.79 pp. Some learned selectors reached correlation 1.0, but the point-ranking test compares only four held-out checkpoints, and decisive agreement remained much lower. This is a narrow panel, not a strict release-date split of all baselines.
- **Task-level PCA/SVD challenger:** an earlier 23-target study fitted equal-benchmark-weighted PCA on training families, chose one/two/three/five dimensions by inner family CV, and used the same seed-0 random probes. Rank correlations were approximately 0.736 at 210 tasks and 0.718 at 840. This was not rerun for the final 21-target scope and is not evidence that all low-rank methods fail.
- **Uncertainty calibration:** nested family calibration and joint-residual interval experiments were run in earlier target scopes. They did not establish deployable uncertainty for this final 21-target setting. Revised 21-target interval calibration remains unestablished.
- **Cost experiments:** matched full/Micro/Mini components were launched on Qwen, Gemma and Antidoom. The completed Qwen MATH500 component used 1.757 H100 task-hours for all 500 tasks, 0.542 for the 10-task Micro slice and 0.645 for the 41-task Mini slice, including startup/setup. These are component savings of 69.1% and 63.3%; whole-suite cost savings were not established. Full matched timing aggregation and fresh adaptive execution were not completed.
- **Prompt and identity parity:** the MATH500 component retained identical prompts and operation inputs for overlapping tasks, and overlapping grades agreed. Source audits resolved selected tasks against canonical source identities and preserved task repetitions.
- **Grading corrections:** the study replayed 90,000 NUPA grades with zero discrepancies against the corrected scorer. A GSM8K audit replayed 23,742 responses across 18 models, identified 15 differing grades across two models, and rebuilt a corrected analysis snapshot; the corrected snapshot replay had zero mismatches. Model generations and the campaign tracker were not changed by that analysis correction.
- **Repetition audit:** no historical task counts exceeded the declared repetition maximum in the audited frozen matrix.
- **Floating-point ties:** accumulating integer half-points before one division removed artificial distinctions from floating-point accumulation. The final 21-target ranking uses that correction.
- **Target-scope correction:** earlier runs sampled 21 benchmarks to predict 23 tournament outcomes. We changed both pool and target to the same 21, refitted selectors and predictors, and archived the old results rather than mixing scopes.

[Full comparison](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-Policy-Index/blob/main/analysis/study-20261030-v6-21x21/report/COST_COMPARISON.md). UMAP was considered as an exploratory visualization, but no completed UMAP experiment is claimed.

### Where random prediction fails

Errors are structured. At 840 tasks, the bottom model-strength group is overestimated by 5.49 pp on average, while the top group is underestimated by 3.70 pp. Mean absolute errors are 9.80 pp for the bottom six models, 6.55 pp for the middle six and 8.27 pp for the top six.

Of the full-reference decisive comparisons, 57.4% retain the correct winner, 33.9% become ties and 8.6% reverse. TriviaQA accounts for 38.4% of outright reversals. TruthfulQA’s decisive reference comparisons all collapse to predicted ties. These diagnostics describe the historical ridge-prediction experiment, including MC2 TruthfulQA; they do not measure the newly generated-choice or uniform Pi execution variants.

[Error analysis and full model/benchmark breakdown](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-Policy-Index/blob/main/analysis/RANDOM_SUBSET_ERROR_ANALYSIS.md).

## What is shipped

- **840/210 unique TaskCompendium rows**, schema 0.28, with exact nesting and stable source IDs.
- **1,626/450 expanded rollout rows** preserving source repetitions; use the `rollouts` dataset config.
- Both `task_spec` and pre-lowered `task_rollout_spec`. Agentic tasks use the existing SkyRL `harbor_trial` integration, preserving original private packages and verifiers while selecting Pi. Answer-only tasks retain source-pinned script graders.
- Canonical validation settings for 65k/16k, thinking on and Pi 0.87.0. SkyRL receives a 49,152 input budget plus 16,384 output; Pi receives 65,536 as its total context window. No cumulative per-episode token cap is substituted for context length.
- The original-policy index, exact source requests/keys/hashes, canonical configurations, policy materializer, grading wheels and exporter code. Both dataset READMEs link to it.

Construction checks every schema and task membership, verifies exact Micro/Mini nesting, round-trips every selected Harbor task without changing file bytes, checks empty responses on all 14 answer benchmarks and known reference responses on 13 (IFBench has no generic reference-response control). No full candidate-model validation run on the new uniform execution profile is claimed.

The datasets do **not** bundle the fitted ridge predictor. For the intended RL validation use, compute raw per-benchmark mean rewards, then an equal-weight mean over the 21 benchmark means if a single summary is needed. The reported 0.818 correlation measures random probes plus ridge prediction, not these raw means. Raw subset aggregation and the new execution profile need their own prospective comparison.

## Decision and remaining validation

Use random Mini840 and Micro210 as provisional compact RL validation sets. Their simpler selection procedure and competitive historical prediction performance motivate that practical choice; do not imply that the proposal’s conservative full-policy replacement gates passed. Those proposed gates were 70% measured GPU-hour savings, 0.95 rank correlation, 95% decisive agreement, top-three winner retention and calibrated 90% intervals. Rank/decisive gates were not met, and whole-suite cost/21-target interval gates remain unestablished.

Run a prospective shadow comparison on genuinely new checkpoints before using this profile as a release-selection replacement. The simplification to Pi, always-on thinking and common context/output limits intentionally changes execution; full release evaluation remains separate.

## Published revisions and construction checks

- [open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-Policy-Index](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-Policy-Index/tree/d5d2f92ce4866c431063bd123ea31a3865530809): `d5d2f92ce4866c431063bd123ea31a3865530809`.
- [open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-840](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Mini-Eval-840/tree/bae388a44fc0ba9ffa551a4c6347fbe03a9fefd7): `bae388a44fc0ba9ffa551a4c6347fbe03a9fefd7`.
- [open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210/tree/4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819): `4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819`.

The RNO2A construction audit validated all 840 TaskSpec/TaskRolloutSpec rows, exact Micro210 nesting, byte-exact Harbor package round-trips, the native Pi context/output settings, and a fresh installation of the published grading wheels. NUPA and GSM8K reference responses received 1.0 and empty responses received 0.0. These are packaging and grading checks, not a prospective full-model quality comparison.

A second RNO2A check, `/benfeuer/mini-policy-public-readback-20261030`, loaded the exact public revisions through Hugging Face Datasets. It verified 840/210 unique rows, 1,626/450 expanded rollout rows, all task schemas, exact nesting, and original-policy subset configs with no changes beyond task selection.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 All four watched historical timing roots have finished: Antidoom full Harbor, Qwen full BixBench, and Qwen full/Mini Harbor. Iris confirms success and terminal attempts; durable result records are present. No additional timing roots were submitted.

Matched Qwen component costs are now available. Values are H100 task-hours, summed over every worker attempt, including setup, retries and restarts:

| Historical component | Full | Mini840 allocation | Micro210 allocation | Observed reduction, Mini / Micro |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BFCL + DS-1000 + TBLite + TB2 | 64.386 | 54.688 | 22.301 | 15.1% / 65.4% |
| BixBench | 216.105 | 45.875 | 6.048 | 78.8% / 97.2% |

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Symptom

When the shared Daytona evaluation account is at its CPU limit, `shellbox`'s Daytona backend fails sandbox creation immediately on the first attempt instead of retrying with backoff. With Harbor configured at `max_retries: 0`, each affected trial aborts at `prepare` before the model produces any output and is recorded as a generic `VerifierRuntimeError` (`"Execution has no final grade"`), hiding the sandbox-capacity cause in downstream evaluation summaries.

## Code path

- `lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py` (`main` at `0b7a1957`, lines 91–116 and 632–648; run pin `6ff68461`, lines 88–113 and 613): `DaytonaBackend.create` calls `_create_sandbox(client, params, timeout=timeout)` inside `async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):`. Inside `_create_sandbox`, only `DaytonaConflictError` (name-recovery path) and `DaytonaRateLimitError` (line 105 on `main`; line 102 at `6ff68461`) are caught and retried with exponential backoff (`initial=1`, `maximum=30`, `factor=2`, `jitter=0.5`).
- A CPU-cap rejection arrives as `DaytonaValidationError` and propagates out of `_create_sandbox` without any retry:
  ```text
  daytona.common.errors.DaytonaValidationError: Failed to create sandbox: Total CPU limit exceeded. Maximum allowed: 2500.
  To increase concurrency limits, upgrade your organization's Tier by visiting https://app.daytona.io/dashboard/limits.
  ```
- Harbor cleanup then raises `RuntimeError: Daytona environment is not running` (`harbor/environments/daytona.py`, line 309, `_download_role_logs`), and SkyRL records `Task <dataset>/<task> interrupted during prepare: VerifierRuntimeError` (`skyrl_train.rollouts.task_worker:_failed_rollout:324`).
- `experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/evaluation.yaml` (line 126 at `6ff68461`) sets `harbor.max_retries: 0` (resolved as `skyrl.generator.terminal_bench_config.harbor.max_retries: 0`), so Harbor does not retry failed `prepare` attempts either. (In the affected runs, line 125 also increased `n_concurrent_trials` from 8 to 16 per rollout worker, which was not the cause of the account cap but increases concurrent sandbox demand.)

## Observed impact (2026-11-20)

- **Excluded trials (per-trial evaluation records):** Two Micro210 evaluation runs lost 85 and 81 Harbor trials (166 total) during `prepare` across the six Harbor-backed sources (`tb2-recovery` 25/27, `ot-tblite-recovery` 28/25, `bfclparity-pi` 8/6, `ds-1000-local` 8/7, `bixbench-pi` 9/10, `swebench-verified` 7/6), all recorded as `VerifierRuntimeError` (`"Execution has no final grade"`, 0 retries, empty model output). The 14 non-Harbor sources had 0 exclusions.
- **Policy worker log checks (possibly incomplete substring queries):** In those two runs, policy logs contained 59 and 61 `"interrupted during prepare"` lines, of which 47 and 53 matched the CPU-cap error. Two subsequent Micro210 runs also logged 56 and 73 `"interrupted during prepare"` lines (45 and 66 CPU-cap errors).
- **Shared evaluation account state:** A read-only account census at 13:08Z found 625 `STARTED` sandboxes holding 2,494 of 2,500 CPU (re-read at 13:12:54Z: 625 `STARTED` sandboxes holding 2,500 of 2,500 CPU). The owner of those sandboxes is not established.

## Requested behavior

1. **Retry CPU-cap creation errors with bounded backoff:** In `lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py` (`_create_sandbox`), treat the Daytona CPU-cap `DaytonaValidationError` (e.g., `"Total CPU limit exceeded"`) as retryable with bounded backoff within the existing creation/startup timeout, similar to `DaytonaRateLimitError`, while leaving genuine non-capacity validation errors fail-fast.
2. **Surface a distinct exclusion reason:** When sandbox creation fails or exhausts its retry budget due to account capacity, raise and propagate a distinct capacity error / exclusion reason so evaluation results report `sandbox capacity` instead of a generic prepare `VerifierRuntimeError` (`"Execution has no final grade"`).

🤖 ## Research

`_create_sandbox` retries Daytona rate limits but lets CPU-cap `DaytonaValidationError` escape. `OwnedMachineFactory.create` wraps that error in `TaskMachineError`; `_failed_rollout` records the wrapper as the trial failure, so Harbor's `max_retries: 0` leaves no capacity-specific exclusion. PR #11762 handles connection resets for non-Harbor tasks and does not overlap this path.

Relevant code: [`machine.py#L91-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L91-L116) — creation retry; [`machines.py#L103-L125`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/machines.py#L103-L125) — error wrapping; [`task_worker.py#L225-L340`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py#L225-L340) — persisted failure type.

## Proposed Fix

Retry only CPU-cap validation errors with exponential backoff under the existing creation deadline, then raise a typed capacity error if the deadline expires while waiting. Add fake-client coverage for recovery, deadline exhaustion, and non-capacity validation errors; test the resulting failure type through the rollout classification path.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** Over a short SFT continuation at 2e-5, typical per-element updates can be smaller than one BF16 step, so a BF16-only policy rounds parameters after every step while the sealed Mochi SFT recipe keeps FP32 parameters on device.
- **Goal:** The long-loop SFT screens are short Snowball runs that test data and recipe changes before they go into the Mochi post-train. This issue checks whether they trained with the right precision, by comparing the BF16-only policy with the FP32 policy bundle (FP32 parameters, gradients and optimizer state; BF16 compute and served weights).
- **Data:** The edit-call screen data: general rows from the 10/05 SFT mix plus 41 edit-call packs.
- **Method:** 15-update runs from 10/05 at learning rates 5e-6 and 2e-5 comparing the BF16 policy against the FP32 policy (one BF16 run per LR; one FP32 run at 5e-6 and three at 2e-5, one of which used a different general-row sample), plus a 15-update zero-LR check on the BF16 path. Each non-zero-LR run was served in BF16 and scored on the edit-call eval (855 graded replies per run).
- **Results:** At 2e-5 the FP32 runs scored 293, 291 and 284 of 855, against 214 for the BF16 run and 224 for 10/05. At 5e-6 FP32 scored 221 against 231 for BF16. The zero-LR BF16 run still changed 8.2% of one expert bank's values, each by one BF16 step.
- **Conclusion:** Bug: the screens stored parameters in BF16, so parameter updates rounded to BF16 after every step. Mochi and 10/05 train with FP32 parameters. The cause is a BF16 parameter line in the long-loop prototype's `sft-smoke.yaml` ([PR 11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120), not on main). It affected 26 finished ablation runs (plus 4 short timing diagnostics), listed in [this comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11687#issuecomment-6999152021). Because the FP32 policy changed parameters, gradients and optimizer state together, this test does not isolate parameter storage alone. Our long-loop SFT run configs now use the FP32 policy. The fix is not yet upstream; [draft PR 11717](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11717) makes the prototype require FP32 parameters.

## Details

### Question and why it matters for the Mochi post-train

Does a short SFT continuation at 2e-5 keep more of each update when the optimizer holds FP32 parameters, FP32 gradients and FP32 optimizer state, rather than the BF16-only policy our arms have used?

The reason to ask is the size of one update relative to BF16 resolution. At 2e-5 a typical per-element move over a short continuation can be smaller than one BF16 code step. A BF16-only policy rounds parameters to BF16 after every update, so part of each update may be discarded before it can accumulate. This motivates comparing the two precision bundles under a matched recipe.

The sealed Mochi source recipe keeps FP32 parameters on device. These Snowball screens inform the next recipe comparison, and transfer to a live Mochi run remains untested.

### What the FP32 policy bundle means

"FP32 policy" here means: FP32 parameters, FP32 gradients into the optimizer, and FP32 optimizer state during training. The mixed-precision policy sets compute and output to BF16. The served weights are BF16, produced by a verified downcast.

The training setting enables pinned-host FP32 master parameters and changes parameter, gradient and optimizer-state dtypes together. The original G5 and G20 comparisons use the same grown E12 data and order as their BF16 comparators, with the same grouping, learning rate and update count. The data-seed-1 arm changes the general sample and order. Because the bundle changes parameters, gradients and optimizer state together, a difference between the two policies is not attributable to any one of those three.

### The zero-learning-rate observation

A same-data 15-update run at learning rate zero on the BF16 path still changed weights. On one expert bank of 21,810,380,800 BF16 values, 1,779,049,111 values changed (8.156892%), and every change was exactly one BF16 code step. At starting magnitude ≥ 1e-3, a population of 19,996,770,120 values, the zero-rate run and the matched 5e-6 run changed the same 1,627,374,248 positions to identical bits. In the smaller population of 1,813,610,680 values, the zero-rate run changed 151,674,863 and the 5e-6 run changed 201,668,362. The symmetric zero-rate versus 5e-6 final-bit disagreement was 53,561,310 values, 0.2456% of the bank, all below starting magnitude 1e-3. The eight plain-Adam leaves and the AdamH output projection stayed bit-identical to the start.

The reviewed reading of that observation is that the observed changes can occur at zero learning rate on this BF16 GPU path. It does not isolate renormalisation as the cause, it does not show that all remaining differences are learning, and it covers one group with one run per condition at endpoints only; attention, shared-expert and 2e-5 extensions were not part of that review.

### Route from an FP32 checkpoint to served BF16 weights

Training ends with FP32 parameters, and serving needs BF16 weights. The initial HF export jobs for both FP32 endpoints were OOMKilled with no retries. The G5 logs place its failure in late parity work. The reviewed split route is below:

1. **Params-only BF16 downcast.** A worker streams FP32 native parameter chunks directly to BF16, checks integer round-to-nearest-even against each write and read-back, rejects nonfinite values, and excludes optimizer slots and the pending quantisation betas. The audit for the 2e-5 run covers 27 parameters and 67,078,882,816 elements, with zero round-to-nearest-even mismatches and zero values below 1.18e-38.
2. **Independent verifier.** A separate job casts the run-specific FP32 endpoint with its own round-to-nearest-even implementation and compares: 22,747,545,600 checked values across eight parameter matrices, zero cast-bit mismatches, and all 16 magnitude-bin changed counts matching the prior FP32 scan. The producer covers all 27 leaves; this bitwise check covers eight matrices, not the entire model.
3. **Standard BF16 export** with the original FP32 optimizer-slot provenance guard. The export audit found 0 changed values, 0 signed-zero flips and 0 nonfinite values between the downcast checkpoint and the exported tensors, across 11 groups and all 67,078,882,816 elements.

The served weights are that BF16 cast. FP32 changes below a BF16 rounding boundary are invisible to serving metrics. Shard payload hashes in the export manifest are producer assertions unless independently rehashed; the receipt review of the storage copy is not a full independent payload rehash.

The same route and the identical independent check were used for the 5e-6 run, the same-seed repeat and the data-seed-1 run, each against its own endpoint and count reference.

### Results: eval-r2 edit-call

eval-r2 is 171 synthetic Pi edit prompts over 11 tasks; the table pools seeds 1 to 5 (855 grades per run). Each continuation used 15 updates on 64 H100. The 10/05 row is the starting checkpoint. All rows are served as BF16 weights, and for the FP32 rows those weights are the verified downcast. "Exact" counts a reply whose applied edit matches the target file exactly after stripping line-end spaces and tabs.

| Run | Seed 0 (of 171) | Greedy (of 171) | Seeds 1–5 (of 171) | Pooled exact (task bootstrap, descriptive) | Strict pooled | BF16-visible change vs the 10/05 BF16 start |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| FP32 policy, 5e-6 (G5-fp32) | 49 | 66 | 44 / 43 / 44 / 50 / 40 | 221/855 = .258 (.192–.303) | 720 | 835,259,286 of 67,078,882,816 values, 1.2452%; 20,312 of 20,392 tensors |
| FP32 policy, 2e-5 (G20-fp32) | 60 | 79 | 58 / 50 / 56 / 72 / 57 | 293/855 = .343 (.280–.406) | 788 | 3,330,528,658 values, 4.9651%; 20,313 tensors |
| FP32 policy, 2e-5, same seed and data order | 61 | 82 | 63 / 52 / 57 / 64 / 55 | 291/855 = .340 (.277–.403) | 780 | 3,327,404,185 values, 4.9604%; 20,313 tensors |
| FP32 policy, 2e-5, different general sample and order | 66 | 80 | 61 / 51 / 54 / 64 / 54 | 284/855 = .332 (.273–.396) | 775 | 3,275,384,396 values, 4.8829%; 20,314 tensors |
| BF16 policy, 5e-6 (G5r2) | 49 | 60 | 49 / 44 / 44 / 51 / 43 | 231/855 = .270 | — | baseline policy |
| BF16 policy, 2e-5 (G20r2) | 53 | 63 | 40 / 46 / 44 / 45 / 39 | 214/855 = .250 | — | baseline policy |
| 10/05 start | 50 | 59 | 47 / 44 / 45 / 48 / 40 | 224/855 = .262 | — | reference |

The change column is an endpoint-versus-start count of the BF16 export against the pinned 10/05 BF16 mirror: the sum of changed values over 67,078,882,816 compared elements. It counts BF16-visible changes, not raw FP32 changes, and differences between runs are differences of baseline-relative counts rather than a direct comparison of the exports.

- At 2e-5, FP32 against its BF16 twin: +79/855 (+9.24 points). Against 10/05: +69/855 (+8.07 points). The two largest task gains account for 31 of 79 and 30 of 69.
- The same-seed repeat and the data-seed-1 run are +77 and +70 of 855 against the BF16 twin (+9.01 and +8.19 points). Each is higher on 10 of 11 tasks and tied on one. Against the original FP32 run they are −2 and −9 of 855; the data-seed-1 run is also −7 against the repeat and +60 against 10/05.
- At 5e-6, FP32 against its BF16 twin: −10/855 (−1.17 points), descriptive, one trained checkpoint per policy at 5e-6.
- Across the three observed G20-fp32 exports the pooled scores were 293, 291 and 284 of 855, each above the 214/855 G20r2 result.
- The CPU data-path audit for the data-seed-1 run found zero shared full-example fingerprints among its 439 general rows, and confirmed the same 41 edit-call packs at the same positions and the same model seed. Multi-host loader execution was unverified.

### Limits

- These are eval-r2 edit-call scores from one checkpoint per training run and BF16 serving weights. Micro210 is the planned broader check on the original export.
- The FP32 policy changed parameter, gradient and optimizer-state dtypes together, so no single dtype is isolated.
- The three G20-fp32 runs at 2e-5 used the same model seed.
- Exact added-row task and file overlap was zero. Exposure through the general mix, including the data-seed-1 run's new general sample, remains unverified, as does task and TMax exposure inherited from the base data.
- The 10/05 seed-0 and greedy results came from an earlier serve. Its pooled seeds 1–5 came from a separate noise-only serve. The G20 and G5 seed-0, greedy and pooled results share a serve within each export. Each checkpoint was served once under its listed setup. The 2e-5 FP32-policy arm has three training runs; the BF16-policy comparator has one.
- The zero-rate observation is endpoint-only, one group, one run per condition.
- Export manifest shard hashes are producer assertions unless independently rehashed.

### What runs next

- The 60-update FP32 pair was cleared at 20:52:44 UTC on 2026-11-18 and both jobs were submitted at 20:53 UTC. The control is general-only; the treatment replaces 164 of 1,920 packed rows with 41 E12-B packs and 123 TMax packs. The schedule holds 2e-5 through update 4,275, including all 60 updates. At 45 seconds per update the fast-path estimate is about 45 minutes of training-step time per arm, with first-step and other overhead extra.
- Micro210 is planned on the original G20-fp32 BF16 export.

### Links

- [Issue 11646](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11646): first expert-MuonH train step stalls on 64 H100s
- [Issue 11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536): Snowball writes malformed JSON in nested Pi edit calls
- [Issue 11539](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11539): Snowball SFT with vs without TMax agent traces
- Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535)

Plan:
1. Run Micro210 on the original G20-fp32 export and compare it with a G20r2 BF16-policy readout under the same task set, harness, serving settings and scoring policy. Report paired task outcomes, assigned/scored/excluded counts, BFCL ×5 and retention alongside the aggregate; obtain a matched G20r2 readout if none exists.

- For context, 10/05 scored 224/855 (.262) on the same set in a separate, noise-only serve. The three 15-update G20-fp32 runs scored 293, 291 and 284 out of 855 in their own serves.

## Training side

| Arm | Train loss, first → last update | Held-out eval loss at 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 |
|---|---|---|
| Control | 0.639367 → 0.521534 | 0.494975 / 0.494503 / 0.494595 / 0.494820 |
| Treatment | 0.610713 → 0.518248 | 0.495105 / 0.494793 / 0.495092 / 0.495328 |

Held-out eval losses were within 0.00051 at each of the four checks. The treatment scored 13.45 percentage points higher on edit-call. The training losses come from different batches.

## Limits

- One checkpoint and one serve per arm.
- The pair tests the combined E12-B and TMax mix. Their individual contributions remain unresolved.
- The CPU row audit counted 465,505,869 supervised target tokens in the treatment versus 472,066,172 in the control, 1.39% fewer.
- Exact added-task overlap with the 11 eval tasks was zero. Added-file overlap is unknown and inherited 10/05 exposure is unverified.
- Micro210 is a pending readout, not a result in this comment. All four coordinator jobs, two per arm, were running with 0 failures and 0 preemptions at the 01:01:57 UTC Nov 19 readback.

## Next: three eight-hour arms

The eight-hour versions are 480 updates per arm, three arms. The reviewed source cache holds 41 E12-B and 129 TMax packs, so eight times the one-hour dose is not available as unseen packs.

🤖 **Snowball SFT line of work (2026-11-17 to 2026-11-19): data, scale against 10/05, recipes, results, and limits.**

## 1. TL;DR

- **One-hour FP32 edit-call:** treatment (`E12-B + TMax`, 60 updates, LR `2e-5`, fresh state) scored `337/855` (`.394`) on `eval-r2` versus `222/855` (`.260`) for its matched general-only control (`+13.45` pp, higher on all 11 tasks; [one-hour edit-call comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11687#issuecomment-6996439113)).
- **One-hour FP32 Micro210:** over two repeats of one export per arm, treatment averaged `39.47%` suite and `14.99%` agent versus `41.59%` suite and `20.00%` agent for control (`−2.13` / `−5.01` pp; missing-outcome bounds `−2.96` to `−1.25` / `−8.45` to `−0.95` pp; control repeats differed by `3.06` / `6.32` pp).
- **BF16 stored-parameter finding:** 26 finished ablation runs and 4 short diagnostics trained with `params=bfloat16` and `master_param_mode=device` ([BF16 inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11687#issuecomment-6999152021)); [draft PR 11717](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11717) enforces FP32 stored parameters.
- **Status at the 04:49Z update on November 19:** `control`, `single`, and `Warm A` were training. Slow `repeat` was cancelled (`04:46:32Z` readback: killed); `repeat-r2` did not launch. `Warm B` was still queued at the latest placement readback (`0/8`). `Warm A control` was cleared under the new rule: continuations from 10/05 carry optimizer state and use the cooled-down LR; fresh state is reserved for starts from the pretrained base.

## 2. Data

| Set | Construction and size | Loss mask and supervised targets |
|---|---|---|
| **General packs** | Rows sampled from the replay of the 10/05 mix, in a fixed order within each frozen row schedule (`262,144` positions/pack; 1,927 text-format components including agentic sources; full 10/05 mix is `79.65%` SFT + `20.35%` pretraining replay; `data_seed=1` changes the general sample and order). | Full-text causal loss (from config, trainer source, and CPU row audit; no prompt mask; S3 general cache weights were not re-read directly). Planned eight-hour control CPU row-proof count: `3,779,290,292` targets over `15,360` packs (`93.86%` of positions, ~`246k`/pack). |
| **E12-B** | Programmatic exercises from TMax train-split code bodies with one to four corrupted regions, with one Pi 0.87 nested `edit` call as the target (`5,536` exercises / `724` tasks / `41` packs; `5,536/5,536` exact Pi 0.87.0 pure-edit matches; `0` overlap with `eval-r1`/`eval-r2` tasks). | **Final edit call only:** `2,176,018` targets over `10,579,547` real positions (`20.6%` of real positions; `20.25%` of `41 × 262,144` padded positions; mean `53,074`/pack). |
| **TMax** | Successful Qwen3.6-27B mini-swe-agent traces from `allenai/tmax-sft` (`9d6ab747`, thinking split). Full train source pool: `4,647` traces / `909` tasks / `129` packs (`900` of those `4,647` source-pool traces were already in 10/05; `507` / `101` held out). Selected for one-hour and eight-hour arms: packs `0–122` (`123` packs, `4,512` traces; packs `123–128` excluded). | **Full-trace causal loss:** within each trace, each position has weight `1` except the final EOS position, which has weight `0`. The weight at position `k` supervises token `k+1`, so this mask excludes the transition to the next trace. Across selected packs `0–122`: `31,605,382` targets of `31,609,894` non-pad positions (`98.02%` of padded positions; mean `256,954`/pack): assistant `47.5%` (`15.01M`), tool outputs `33.4%` (`10.57M`), user `13.9%` (`4.39M`), system + tool schemas `3.9%` (`1.23M`), role headers `1.3%` (`0.41M`). Matches general packs' full-text loss except each TMax trace excludes its transition across final EOS. (Measured on rendered traces and cache audit; independent technical read in progress.) |

Planned-schedule CPU row-proof shares for combined `E12-B + TMax` arms (`164` packs = `41` E12-B + `123` TMax, `33,781,400` targets): one-hour treatment substitutes `164/1,920` rows (`8.54%` of rows, `7.26%` of its `465,505,869` planned targets); eight-hour `single` substitutes `164/15,360` rows (`1.07%` of rows, `0.90%` of planned targets); eight-hour `repeat` substitutes `1,312/15,360` rows (`164 × 8`, `8.54%` of rows, `7.25%` of planned targets). For `Warm A` and queued `Warm B`, `7.25%` is the repeat-schedule projection, not consumed data.

## 3. Scale against 10/05 SFT

Formula: Levanter `lm_flops_per_token` (non-causal full-span attention convention) for Snowball (`hidden=2560`, `intermediate=1280`, `shared=2560`, `layers=26`, `heads=20`, `kv_heads=5`, `vocab=128,256`, `256` experts, top-4, `sliding_window=2048`, `7` full-attention layers per `_long_layer_schedule(26, 4)` — layers 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25 — matching the 10/05 W&B analytic value `23,911,178,240` forward FLOPs/token). Training FLOPs = `3 × 23,911,178,240 × positions` (`7.173353e10` FLOPs/position; `6.02e17` FLOPs per 32-pack update).

| Run scale | Updates | Packs / update | Positions (`× 262,144`) | Training FLOPs (`3×` analytic) | Share of 10/05 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **10/05 SFT** (step `157,000 → 161,750`) | `4,750` | `256` | `318.77B` (`318,767,104,000`) | `2.29e22` | `100%` |
| **15-update arms** (per arm: `C-*`, `G*`) | `15` | `32` | `0.126B` (`125,829,120`) | `9.03e18` | `0.0395%` (`1/2,533`) |
| **One-hour pair** (scheduled per arm) | `60` | `32` | `0.503B` (`503,316,480`) | `3.61e19` | `0.1579%` (`1/633`) |
| **Eight-hour arms** (scheduled per arm) | `480` | `32` | `4.027B` (`4,026,531,840`) | `2.89e20` | `1.2632%` (`1/79.2`) |

## 4. Recipe facts per run family

All 11-17 to 11-19 arms below use `seq=262,144`, `bs=32`, Mochi grouping (`grug_moe_muonh_v1`, `global_grad_norm=1.0`, `weight_decay=0.0`, special-token LR `√32 × LR`), and BF16 compute/output.

**Earlier `2e-5` BF16 runs are confounded:** the earlier E12 pilot control and treatment ([issue 11536](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11536)) scored below 10/05 on Micro210. In the TMax comparison ([issue 11539](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11539)), both continuations scored below their parent on BFCL ×5 under both evaluated serve stacks. These continuations used fresh optimizer state, BF16 stored parameters, and LR `2e-5`, so the results cannot assign the drops to any one of those factors. Earlier pretrained-base screens ([issue 11537](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11537), C150/O150) also used BF16 stored parameters at `2e-5` with fresh state from the pretrained base (so their gaps to 10/05 are not drops from their initializer) and need an FP32 redo.

- **Limits:** (1) Eight-hour readouts are still in progress; current Micro210 results are two repeats of one export per one-hour arm. The one-hour Micro210 direction is lower for treatment on both metrics even under the missing-outcome bounds, while two repeats leave evaluation variability and training-seed effects unresolved. (2) Treatment arms bundle E12-B and TMax together, so their individual contributions are not separated, and TMax uses full-trace loss rather than assistant-only loss. (3) The `G20-fp32` checks include a same-seed rerun and a run with a different general-data seed. All three used the same model seed, so model-seed variation remains unmeasured; all other arms have one training run per condition. (4) The edit-call and Micro210 scores here describe the BF16 exports. For the one-hour edit-call pair, the added rows share `0` of `11` `eval-r2` task IDs, added-file overlap is unknown, and inherited 10/05 exposure is unverified. (5) Harness parity between the four one-hour Micro210 runs (`44652`, `44653`, `44658`, `44659`) and the earlier `10/05` parent runs (`44627–44628`) was not rechecked. (6) Nine known broader-suite import failures remain unresolved and outside the 20-source Micro210 results; they are not counted as passing.

| Line | Parameters | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Snowball 67B-A2B pretraining (10T run, step-39k cooldown) | FP32 | The W&B consumed config of [`moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k`](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep8_bs1024_seq65536_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_cooldown_step39k) records `param_dtype=float32, compute_dtype=bfloat16, output_dtype=bfloat16`. Every launcher at pin `5681efbe3f` (branch `june_tpu_67b_a2b`) sets the same policy: base 10T, resume15k, cooldown and both YaRN variants. |
| Mochi hero pretraining and the 262K extension (`hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`) | FP32 | `hero_recipe.py`: `MasterParamMode.DEVICE` maps to `params=float32,compute=bfloat16,output=bfloat16`. The README states "fp32 on device with bf16 compute". |
| Long-loop Exp3 and Exp4 production SFT | FP32 | `exp3_production.py` builds `p=f32,c=bfloat16`. `exp3_recipe.py:131` rejects any other policy when the recipe is built. |

Not yet checked against W&B: the Snowball 10T run before step 39k, and the 262K extension that produced `snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8`. Both use the same launcher policy.

Probable cause of the bad line: `hero_recipe.py` defines `HERO_MIXED_PRECISION = "params=bfloat16,..."`. That policy is correct only with `MasterParamMode.FP32_PINNED_HOST`, where an FP32 master copy stays on the host. `sft-smoke.yaml` pairs `params=bfloat16` with `master_param_mode: device`. No FP32 copy exists anywhere in that combination, and no check rejects it. Suggested guard, in addition to #11717's one-line fix: make the SFT runtime reject `params=bfloat16` with `master_param_mode: device` when the config is built.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 The values that change at learning rate zero are changed by the hyperball step's own arithmetic, and the counts in this issue follow from the public 10/05 checkpoint.

`_scale_invariant_hyperball_updates` returns `new_param / |new_param| * |param| - param` in the parameter dtype. At rate zero `new_param` is `param`, so each value `x` becomes `bf16(bf16(x / n) * n)`, where `n` is the bfloat16 norm over its layer's 256 experts. In bfloat16 that round trip is not the identity. For `mlp.experts.down_proj` of `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` (`ac60d940`), `n` is 282.0 in all 26 layers:

| | this issue | from the public weights |
|---|---:|---:|
| values at or above 1e-3 | 19,996,770,120 | 19,996,770,120 |
| changed, at or above 1e-3 | 1,627,374,248 | 1,627,374,248 |
| changed, below 1e-3 | 151,674,863 | 151,674,863 |
| changed, total | 1,779,049,111 | 1,779,049,111 |

Every predicted change is one code step, and a second update changes nothing more. The same arithmetic gives 1,779,077,070 for `gate_proj` and 1,779,130,038 for `up_proj`.

- **The rate at or above 1e-3.** A MuonH step there is far below half a code step. On CPU, with random update directions, the function on `main` leaves every such value of seven matrices of the Snowball base with the same bits at rates 0, 5e-6, 2e-5 and 5e-5.
- **Float32 parameters.** At rate zero the same function then changes no value after the bfloat16 cast.
- **Round 1.** `Snowball-LongLoop-Round1-2026.11.12.7` ran this update on bfloat16 parameters for its attention, shared-expert and GatedNorm matrices and its stacked RMSNorm scales. Over all of those tensors, 83% to 85% of the positions the round trip predicts in the matrices hold exactly the predicted value, and they are 44% to 47% of the values that differ from the base. In the stacked RMSNorm scales the round trip accounts for 95% of the changed values.

So on the BF16 path a count of changed values measures this round trip before it measures learning. I wrote my note on #11639 before reading this issue; its point about parameter precision was already made here.

A check that needs no checkpoint (prints 0.0816 and 0.0):

```python
import ml_dtypes, numpy as np
bf16 = ml_dtypes.bfloat16
x = (0.0098 * np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(20_000_000)).astype(bf16)
n = bf16(282.0)
y = ((x / n).astype(bf16) * n).astype(bf16)
print((y != x).mean(), (((y / n).astype(bf16) * n).astype(bf16) != y).mean())
```

I can post the script that reads the three banks by range request (131 GB, nothing stored).

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Summary

- **Motivation:** Before choosing targeted data to add to Mochi's next SFT mix, we needed a trace-backed picture of where Mochi SFT (step 400407) lags peer open-weight models—such as MRCR-65k (26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08%) and IFBench (26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%)—rather than extrapolating from Snowball-only defects.
- **Goal:** Identify Mochi SFT (step 400407)'s clearest benchmark and trace-level weaknesses against peer open-weight models, check mode and SFT-mix coverage gaps, and test targeted SFT data candidates for Mochi's next SFT mix.
- **Data:** 12 completed full-size benchmark runs, BFCL ×5 (issue 11538), a partial SWE-smith screen (469 retained attempts), three controlled thinking-off versus thinking-on probes, the frozen 216-store SFT manifest (968,596 packs), and two synthetic SFT datasets (multi-needle retrieval and cue-balanced tool abstention).
- **Method:** Audit error traces, run matched thinking-off versus thinking-on probes and zero-training inference checks on Mochi, scan all 216 SFT stores for thinking-off tool coverage and placeholder arguments, and evaluate a 1-hour FP32 Snowball continuation with 120 multi-needle retrieval packs (loss weight 30) against a 1-hour general-only control on full 901-item MRCR-65k.
- **Results:** Clear benchmark gaps were MRCR-65k (26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08%), IFBench (26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%), BFCL live-irrelevance (65.5%), and SWE-smith read calls with an extra `command` key (69/469 attempts). At a matched 4,096-token cap, Mochi scored 81.67% (98/120) under thinking-off versus 96.67% (116/120) under thinking-on on deterministic constraints, and over-called on 57/60 missing-argument tool prompts under thinking-off versus 59/59 abstention passes under thinking-on (a system-prompt guard still over-called on 35/60; empty-think prefill still emitted reasoning on 120/120). The 216-store scan found 14,718 thinking-off rows across non-coding tool stores (vs 506,889 thinking-on rows in `agentic_v1/v2` alone) and 2,485 grounding-filtered explicit placeholder calls in `agentic_v1/tool_calling` (7,383 raw across four agentic stores). On Snowball, the 1-hour multi-needle retrieval run scored 21.20% vs 21.44% control (−0.24 pp) under thinking-off and 22.65% vs 21.59% (+1.06 pp) under thinking-on on MRCR-65k, with 175/901 unclosed think spans under thinking-on.
- **Conclusion:** Multi-needle retrieval data did not transfer to headline MRCR-65k in this single 1-hour Snowball run and stays held out of Mochi's SFT mix. Thinking-off tool abstention data, placeholder-argument filtering across the agentic stores, and a matched thinking-mode check on full IFBench remain the leading candidates for Mochi's next SFT mix, while hard-math, knowledge, and major agentic benchmarks remain unmeasured on Mochi.

Parent: [issue 11535](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535).

---

## 1. Benchmark Scorecard (Mochi step 400,407 vs Comparators)

**Comparability, serving, and cohort notes (all cross-model comparisons are descriptive and configuration-dependent):**
- The 12 EvalDash rows for Mochi are single completed full-size runs (`k=1` each) served on H100s (`pp=3, dp=8`, `max_model_len=65536`, `marin-tokenizer-tools` revision `3f6879a`, `tool_call_parser=hermes`, `reasoning_parser=null`, `chat_template_kwargs={}`, PIECEWISE CUDA graphs, generation config from Snowball RLVR Step 92). Note that `reasoning_parser=null` means no reasoning parser was configured on the serve; it does not by itself establish whether thinking was disabled at generation time.
- Snowball 10/05 (`open-athena-Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`) also had `reasoning_parser=null` and `tool_call_parser=hermes` in the checked EvalDash runs, whereas Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (`qwen3`), Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (`gemma4`), and Nemotron-3.5-30B-A3B (`nemotron_v3`) had native reasoning parsers configured.
- Comparator ranges are **observed ranges** `[min–max]` across retained runs in each cohort, showing cohort count `k` and scored count `n`. The audit retains `succeeded` runs with a populated headline and no recorded policy violations. It applies an 80% coverage floor when both scored and benchmark counts are positive, plus per-benchmark scored-count floors when a positive scored count is reported (`>= 100` for `ds-1000-local`/`bfclparity-pi`, `>= 200` for `ifbench`, `>= 500` for `mrcr-65k`, `>= 1000` for `gsm8k-0shot`); coverage filtering does not prove every comparator run was uncapped.

## 2. Trace-Backed Failure Analysis

### 2.1 `mrcr-65k` (26.49%, n=901; all 901 classified, 15 read directly)

Mochi prepends the exact requested 10-character random string on **806/901 (89.46%)** of prompts, and **186/901 (20.6%)** score `> 0.9` on MRCR's graded string-similarity metric. Mean `mrcr_accuracy` declines with needle count and across the four length buckets below 40k (`n_chars // 4`); the single 40k+ item scored 80.78%:

| Slice | n | Mean `mrcr_accuracy` |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 needles | 299 | 36.29% |
| 4 needles | 302 | 28.71% |
| 8 needles | 300 | **14.47%** (graded string similarity) |
| 0–10k (`n_chars // 4`) | 325 | 31.68% |
| 10–20k (`n_chars // 4`) | 283 | 27.15% |
| 20–30k (`n_chars // 4`) | 159 | 20.05% |
| 30–40k (`n_chars // 4`) | 133 | 19.66% |
| 40k+ (`n_chars // 4`) | 1 | 80.78% |

Across the **620** items that hit the exact random prefix with `score <= 0.9`:
- **423 / 620 (68.2%)** matched another same-topic occurrence by a 60-character substring heuristic, with **331** matched occurrences later than the requested one and **92** earlier (measured direction; not opportunity-normalized). Under literal stripped-output equality with the same topic heuristic, **323 / 620 (52.1%)** matched another same-topic occurrence (**275** later, **48** earlier).
- **26 / 620 (4.2%)** matched a different-topic assistant turn under the 60-character substring heuristic.
- **171 / 620 (27.6%)** had no classified alternative-turn match under this heuristic (this residual count does not separate paraphrases from partial or truncated outputs).
- The remaining **95 / 901 (10.5%)** failed the exact-prefix check (`score = 0`).

## 3. Proposed Candidate Target Skills (with Fast-Eval Proposals and Non-Eval Data Ideas)

*Data hygiene rule:* **Eval-side traces and benchmark prompts/outputs are never used as training data.** Every training data proposal below relies exclusively on freshly synthesized or non-eval open templates verified programmatically. Probe runtimes below are rough estimates and not yet measured on Mochi's serve.

### Proposal 1: Long-Context Ordinal Multi-Needle Retrieval and Verbatim Copy
- **Target gap:** Largest observed deficit vs peers (`mrcr-65k` 26.49% vs Qwen3.6 92.08% and Nemotron-3.5-30B 45.75%), with 423/620 prefix-matching low-score items matching a different same-topic occurrence by 60-character substring (323 under literal stripped-output equality), predominantly later than requested.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 100–200 item synthetic multi-needle probe at 8K–64K context (2/4/8 repeated-topic needles, querying the *k*-th 1-indexed occurrence with a random prefix), scored deterministically in Python by exact prefix and string similarity without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically synthesize multi-turn dialogues (8K–64K tokens) mixing filler turns with 2–12 repeated requests on fresh non-MRCR topics, paired with final-turn ordinal retrieval queries distributed uniformly over *k* from 1 to *N* (covering both `/think` counting chains and `/nothink` direct-copy targets).

### Proposal 2: Strict Verifiable Constraint Following and Output Discipline
- **Target gap:** Strict instruction-following gap vs peers (`ifbench` 26.00% strict vs Gemma-4 43.44%, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 40.00%, Nemotron-3.5-120B 38.00%, Qwen3.6 34.57%), with `repeat` (0.00%), `sentence` (3.57%), `words` (11.76%), and `ratio` (15.91%) lowest.
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 200-item held-out synthetic constraint suite covering word/sentence/ratio/repeat/format/no-preamble constraints, scored purely by deterministic Python verifiers without an LLM judge.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Programmatically compose fresh prompts combining 1–3 verifiable lexical/structural constraints (forbidden/required words, exact sentence/word counts, keyword-per-sentence, ratio bounds, strict JSON/markdown structure, no preamble/postscript), generate candidates, and **rejection-sample strictly using deterministic Python verifiers** (keeping only 100%-passing responses across both `/think` and `/nothink` formats).

### Proposal 3: Tool-Schema Adherence and Abstention Across Diverse Tool Contracts
- **Target gap:** Addresses the concrete tool-contract weaknesses observed in BFCL x5 (`simple-java` 53.3%, `parallel` 62.9%, `live-irrelevance` 65.5%) and the extra-`"command"` `read`/malformed-call defects observed in SWE-smith r6 (69/469 attempts with extra `"command"` on parsed `read`; 12/19 readout-`BAD` first-tool `read`; 21/58 exception-free `reward=0` raw `<tool_call>` text).
- **Proposed fast eval (rough estimate: minutes-scale):** A 150–200 item single-turn synthetic tool-calling probe testing: (a) unfamiliar file/code tool schemas deliberately distinct from `str_replace_editor` (checking valid Hermes JSON and zero undeclared keys), (b) irrelevance/abstention prompts requiring an explicit empty tool list or required artifact, and (c) parallel and typed-argument multi-call prompts. Graded deterministically by JSON-schema and AST checks without container spinup.
- **Proposed clean training data:** Synthesize diverse tool definitions (varying parameter names across file readers/editors, SQL/API clients, and typed Java/JS/Python signatures) with programmatically verified trajectories teaching strict adherence to declared JSON schemas, calibrated abstention when no tool applies or required arguments are missing, and parallel call arrays.

## Part Two: Controlled 3-Probe Diagnostic Suite (`nothink` vs `think`)

**Run conditions and comparability labels:**
- **Serve:** `hero-sft-step400407` (**shared endpoint, unpinned serve**; `max_model_len=262,144`; `/v1/models` returned HTTP 200 with identical `id`, `root`, and `max_model_len` at start and end of all 6 invocations).
- **Decoding:** **`greedy, temperature 0.0`** (explicitly set on all 780 requests; `max_tokens=1,024` for `nothink`, `4,096` for `think`; `stop_token_ids=[128009, 128001]`, `skip_special_tokens=false`). Prompts were pre-rendered locally with `marin-community/marin-tokenizer-tools` (`3f6879acdaf3dae7874b2d48c7d11b9d8c6faf09`) toggling `enable_thinking=False` (`Reasoning: /nothink`) vs `enable_thinking=True` (`Reasoning: /think`).
- **Comparability caveat:** **Do not compare these numbers directly with EvalDash scores as if sampling, prompts, or serve configuration matched.** These paired probes compare two prompt-and-budget configurations in sequential batches on the shared serve. The output caps differed (1,024 versus 4,096), so the contrast does not isolate the prompt directive. Wilson 95% intervals below are marginal per-mode summaries.
- **Data segregation:** All 390 probe items and 780 completions are **eval-only (`eval_only=true`, never training data)**. Any future training data targeting these skills must be generated separately with disjoint topics and seeds.
- **Coverage & wall time:** **780 / 780 HTTP 200 (100.0% coverage, 0 retries, 0 skipped)** in ~23 minutes total at concurrency 6.

---

### 2. Per-Probe Breakdown and Key Findings

#### Probe 1: Multi-Needle Ordinal Retrieval (n=120; 3 needle counts × 4 token bands × 10 items; target `k` cycled across the valid ordinals)

- **Higher constraint score under the `/think` configuration (+14.17 pp; 19 think-only passes vs 2 nothink-only):** Every family reached 90–100% under the `/think` configuration, with `lexical_words` moving from 65% to 95% and `compound_discipline` (including all 10 concise-final-integer items) moving from 80% to 100%.
- **Remaining `/think` failures (4/120):** Three of the four `/think` failures (`p2-lex-11`, `p2-ratio-10`, `p2-ratio-13`) hit the 4,096-token cap with an unclosed thinking span. The remaining failure (`p2-sent-14`) had the `sent_1_missing_water` tag. Under `/nothink`, top strict failure tags were `invalid_json` (5), `caps_count` (4), `sent_1_end!` (4), and required-word counts.

#### Probe 3: Tool-Contract Suite (n=150; 3 sub-suites × 50 items)

| Sub-suite (n=50 each) | `/nothink` pass [marginal Wilson 95%] | `/think` pass [marginal Wilson 95%] | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `irrelevance_abstention` | **38.00%** (19/50) [25.86–51.85] | **100.00%** (50/50) [92.87–100.00] | `/nothink` scored **0/25 (0.0%)** on missing-required-argument prompts (`missing_ticket` 0/9, `missing_station_id` 0/8, `missing_repo_slug` 0/8) and **19/25 (76.0%)** on domain-mismatch (31 total over-calls); the `/think` configuration passed all 50 abstention items (25/25 on both) |

The single-turn probe did not reproduce the SWE-smith pattern. Multi-turn context is one candidate to test in a matched follow-up.

---

### 3. Updated Targeting Implications (Read-Only Summary)

1. **Multi-needle ordinal retrieval at high needle count (`8 needles`: 52.5% `/nothink`, 50.0% `/think`)** persists under both configurations, alongside lower `<|start_think|>` emission in longer nominal bands (63.3% at 8k down to 20.0% at 56k) and 10 early-EOT unclosed think spans plus 1 cap hit on Probe 1 `/think`.
