comments.body:
**The forecast of 21 October, scored**

Follow-up to my forecast in this thread (2026-10-21). Target, as registered: the last `eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` of the hero lineage at step 387,000 or later. That is **1.9602** at step 390,250 (`hero-ctx65k-step372k`), with all 16 Paloma subsets present.

| forecast | value | 90 % interval | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: ladder + the hero's own evals | 1.979 | [1.965, 1.994] | 0.019 |
| B: ladder only | 1.935 | [1.915, 1.963] | 0.025 |
| line through the hero's 16K evals (my baseline) | 1.970 | | 0.009 |
| Aug 19 pre-registration | 2.039 | | 0.079 |

Hypotheses fixed in advance:
- A closer than 2.039: yes.
- B closer than 2.039: yes.
- The final value inside A's interval: no, below it by 0.0045.
- A closer than the straight line: no.

The final value is inside B's interval.

**Packing.** 2.039 and B were built on 4K-packed evals, so the comparison above favours them against a training-length eval. Thanks to the 4K re-evaluation (`hero-ctx-evals-4k`), the offset at the last re-evaluated checkpoint is 1.9817 (4K, step 390,000) minus 1.9590 (the run's eval, step 389,999) = 0.0227. That is smaller than the 0.031 measured at step 252K. Against 1.9602 + 0.0227 = 1.983, B is off by 0.048 and 2.039 by 0.056. So both forecasts are still closer after the correction.

The formulas are unsealed now and match the SHA-256 digests posted before the outcome, as does the registration's manifest: https://github.com/mindscanlabs/NAI-track-record/blob/main/forecasts/marin-535b.md

These forecasts were made with version 19 of NAI.
NAI is now at version 25, and I would be glad to join your next experiment with it.

Thanks for logging, re-evaluating and discussing all of this in the open, and to @bethehand for the packing measurements. They made a clean prospective test possible.

Training loss over the last 1,000 steps averaged 0.965, at 65K context. MFU ended near 33%. The 4K row re-evaluates the last 6K checkpoint; the 65K row is the run's own final eval.

**Training loss.** Every step is plotted, against tokens trained. The dashed lines mark the switch to near-dropless EP (ragged all-to-all), the two datamix changes, and the 4K → 16K and 16K → 65K context extensions.
![training loss](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/dab2e6d920808f898f565be6dbf39ad01dbdad12/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_summary_figs/hero_train_loss.png)

**Against the scaling ladder**, by run progress. At 80% the ladder moved to its phase-2 mix and its loss rose; the hero moved to a different phase-2 mix and its loss fell. The 27.7B rung crashed at 81% on a hardware failure and was not resumed.
![hero against the scaling ladder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/dab2e6d920808f898f565be6dbf39ad01dbdad12/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_summary_figs/hero_vs_ladder_train_loss.png)

**Forecast and actual, every eval at 4K context.** The forecast is the per-5% ladder fit posted earlier in this issue. The hero tracks it to about 65%, then pulls ahead after extending to 16K and then 65K context with an improved datamix. From the 16K switch on, the hero points are the 4K re-evaluations of every 6K checkpoint (W&B `hero-evals-at-4k`).
![forecast and actual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/dab2e6d920808f898f565be6dbf39ad01dbdad12/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_summary_figs/hero_evals_vs_forecast.png)

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Weight merging the final hero checkpoints: −0.003 loss at 65K, saved as a resumable checkpoint**

Averaging the final 65K-phase checkpoints lowers loss by about 0.003 on every eval. On the ladder law L = 1.5 + 84.8·C^−0.09 that's worth roughly 7% more training compute, for free.

**Checkpoint:** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251`

- **Weights:** an equal-weight average of 11 checkpoints: 385,500–390,000 every 500 steps, plus the final 390,251. Each weight tensor is rescaled to stay on the hyperball (details below).
- **Training state:** step 390,251, with that checkpoint's full optimizer state and QB betas. It has the hero's checkpoint layout, so it resumes directly with `initialize_from` or loads weights-only for evals and export.
- **`metadata.json`** records the sources, the weights, the merge space and where the training state came from.

All evals are dropless at 65,536 context with `qk_mult` 1.66. Each row is the change versus step 390,000.

| Merge | Clean Paloma | Uncheatable | All evals |
|---|---|---|---|
| step 390,000 (baseline) | 1.7515 | 1.4786 | 1.6953 |
| step 390,251 (final) | −0.0001 | −0.0003 | ±0.0000 |
| average of last 2 | −0.0012 | −0.0011 | −0.0013 |
| average of last 4 | −0.0020 | −0.0020 | −0.0021 |
| EMA, 0.5 per 500 steps (10 ckpts) | −0.0020 | −0.0019 | −0.0021 |
| EMA, 0.8 per 500 steps (10 ckpts) | −0.0028 | −0.0029 | −0.0029 |
| average of 10 (385,500–390,000) | −0.0028 | −0.0031 | −0.0030 |
| average of 10, hyperball | −0.0028 | −0.0031 | −0.0029 |
| **average of 11, hyperball (saved)** | **−0.0030** | **−0.0033** | **−0.0032** |

- **What matters:** how many checkpoints go in, and how evenly they're weighted. The wider and flatter the average, the bigger the gain, and it hadn't levelled off at 11.
- **Hyperball rescaling changes nothing:** the plain average already sits at 0.9995 of the sphere radius.
- **Step-to-step noise is small:** one more stretch of training (390,000 → 390,251) moves the loss by at most 0.0003, an order of magnitude less than the merge.
- **Every eval set improves,** all 23 of them.

**Process**

1. **Choosing eval sets:** the 4K re-evals of the 16K and 65K checkpoints showed which sets don't fall smoothly from step to step. "Clean Paloma" leaves out PTB (contaminated reads), WikiText-103, TwitterAAE and Gab, whose loss rose 7–12 times across those 23 checkpoints. It averages the other 12 sets. "Uncheatable" averages all 7 of its sets.
2. **Merging:** sources load one at a time into a float32 running sum of the fp32 weights. The hero keeps no separate master copy, so these are the master weights.
3. **Hyperball mode:** after averaging, each MuonH/AdamH tensor is rescaled to its sources' mean norm, over the same axes the optimizer holds fixed:
   - 2-D weights: the whole matrix is one ball.
   - Stacked weights: one ball per layer.
   - Routed experts: each layer's whole bank of all 384 experts is one ball (`ALL_EXPERTS`).

   Adam-trained leaves (embeddings, router, norm gains, attention gate) are plain averages.
4. **Saving:** the merged weights are combined with 390,251's step, optimizer state and QB betas, using a template built from the hero's own optimizer config. Before launching, I checked that template against the 390,251 manifest: all 56 optimizer-state arrays and 36 parameter arrays match in shape and dtype.
5. **Verification:** the job reloaded the saved checkpoint and checked the weights bit for bit and the optimizer state by per-leaf checksums. The eval numbers above for the saved row come from that reloaded copy.

Each variant ran as one job on one rack at production priority, logged to W&B in `marin_moe` as `hero-merge-*` (the saved one is `hero-merge-hb-avg11-save`).

**Code:** branch [`larry/hero-ckpt-merge-eval`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/larry/hero-ckpt-merge-eval) at [`dff14a5`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/dff14a54199eaf97a3719d0b6d64a99fb044d47f). The work is in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_checkpoint_eval.py`, using `--merge-source PATH WEIGHT` (repeatable), `--merge-space hyperball` and `--save-merged OUT STATE_FROM`; the CPU tests are in `test_checkpoint_eval.py`. The saved checkpoint was made with:

```
python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_checkpoint_eval --run-id hero-merge-hb-avg11-save \
  --merge-source <ckpts>/step-385500 1 ... --merge-source <ckpts>/step-390000 1 --merge-source <ckpts>/step-390251 1 \
  --merge-qk-mult 1.66 --merge-space hyperball \
  --save-merged s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/checkpoints/step-390251 <ckpts>/step-390251 \
  --seq-len 65536 --version dev --run
```

where `<ckpts>` = `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-ctx65k-step372k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints`.

comments.author: mcwitt-agent
comments.body:
🤖 The 262K extension is decided: two recipes in sequence, from [the merged checkpoint](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6676769570), 3,240 steps or 149.5B tokens each, to step 393491. The learning rate moves linearly from 5% to 1% of peak. First, Global 1.84 (`qk_mult` 1.66, long scale 1.108), from main at `e0bc917ee5`. Second, log floor 65536 squared, from a branch that merges only if it wins.

Seven 100-step arms at 11 racks did not separate the recipes on held-out text: clean macro at 262K spans 0.0004, against jitter of 0.0002 to 0.0007. The merged start's gain on clean macro fell from about 0.003 to 0.0017 in 100 steps, on one seed. Global 1.84 ran in no arm, no rehearsal ran, and no arm was repeated. An arm that held the router bias fixed was not adopted, so the bias keeps updating each step.

Changes to what you may rely on: a checkpoint from the second finalist cannot be exported or served until log-scaling support lands, SFT and RL loading of the merged checkpoint is untested, and at 262K `ptb` and `wikitext_103` write no online eval value. Offline evals still score them.

Results and full evidence: [logbooks #37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37) and its [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2307cd320fb832c022284d6df07858db3b89d5f/logbooks/37-hero-262k/notebook.md). Tracking: #11056.

Against Global 1.84 at step 393491: clean macro at 262K 1.6434 vs 1.6433 (not significant), MRCR full-context NLL 0.0223 vs 0.0252 (−0.0029, Holm p < .001 at all 7 checkpoints), recovery 0.982 vs 0.981 (not significant). comments.body:
🤖 **Findings:** In the [November 17 SkyRL nightly](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44144419792), OPD and CatCount passed. The Grug Megatron H100 lane reached its GPU tests and failed after five passed, in `test_grug_megatron_forward_matches_hf[pp1]`. Its [native log artifact](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44144419792/artifacts/14355009671) shows `MegatronPolicyWorkerBase.init_model()` raising `AssertionError: NVTE_FUSED_ATTN set to 1, but expected 0 for attention backend type flash`. Pytest exited 1, causing the Iris job to fail. This is model initialization, with no evidence of a placement or Iris infrastructure fault in this run.

At the [run revision, the Grug GPU test sets `trainer.flash_attn = False`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4b1a2a4cb4204ebce19b5a1d4626a40bd0511bed/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/tests/gpu/grug_policy_training.py#L15-L24), while [the BF16 Grug worker selects FlashAttention](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4b1a2a4cb4204ebce19b5a1d4626a40bd0511bed/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/workers/megatron/megatron_worker.py#L140-L148). [Ray sets `NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=0` only when that test flag is true](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4b1a2a4cb4204ebce19b5a1d4626a40bd0511bed/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/utils/utils.py#L1037-L1042). The source of the inherited value `1` is not established by the log, but this configuration mismatch explains why Megatron rejects it.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Queries on the Finelog `log` table that filter on `epoch_ms` open every file. The catalog does not record each segment's time range, so the time filter cannot skip any file. Most of the query time goes to reading Parquet footers, not data. That is why day-sized scans exceed the 10-second query deadline. #11087 raises that deadline to 30 seconds as a stopgap. Once time-filtered queries can skip files, the deadline can go back down.

## Evidence

A one-hour `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the `marin` hub (2026-11-08 23:38 UTC). It filtered `epoch_ms` to one hour, plus `LIKE` filters on `key` and `data`. Wall time was 7.1 s. Full query, plan and metrics: https://gist.github.com/karansag/160e31066556f7b00199c6b328d925f5

Table: `log` in namespace `marin`, 10.4 B rows, 324 GB, 1,977 segments. Trigram indexes on `key` and `data`. No sort columns and no partitioning.

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| files pruned by statistics | 1.66 K total, 1.66 K matched: **0 files skipped** |
| row groups pruned by footer stats | 2.49 K total, 6 matched |
| bytes scanned | 5.00 MB |
| `metadata_load_time` | 18.23 s |
| `time_elapsed_opening` | 52.41 s |
| output rows | 9 |

The times are summed across 16 parallel file groups, so they exceed the wall time.

The catalog records each segment's `seq` and `key` ranges, but not `epoch_ms`. So every file's footer is read just to get the `epoch_ms` min and max. After that, the query reads almost nothing: 6 row groups and 5 MB.

Impact: a 60-day pull of `levanter.model_cache` lines in 12-hour windows lost 58% of its windows to `snapshot read deadline exceeded`, even with three retries per window (#9233).

## Possible directions

- Record per-segment `epoch_ms` min and max in the catalog, so time filters drop files before they are opened.
- Sort or cluster segments by time during compaction, so those ranges are narrow.

## Done when

- A one-hour `epoch_ms` query on `log` opens only the segments that overlap that hour.
- The default query deadline can go back to 10 seconds, reverting #11087's increase.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`Store::query_providers` snapshots paths only, and `NamespaceProvider` gives every path to DataFusion before the existing row-group and index pruning runs. Neither the in-memory segment record nor the SQLite catalog carries `epoch_ms` bounds. This matches the issue's one-hour plan: 1,660 files matched file statistics, then only six row groups were read.

**Relevant code**
- [`store.rs#L515-L527`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/store.rs#L515-L527) — snapshots paths for query providers
- [`provider.rs#L112-L182`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/rust/src/query/provider.rs#L112-L182) — registers all paths before scan
- [`catalog.rs#L193-L207`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/catalog.rs#L193-L207) — persisted segment columns
- [`namespace.rs#L735-L759`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/namespace.rs#L735-L759) — flush publishes segment metadata
- [`executor.rs#L318-L334`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/compaction/executor.rs#L318-L334) — compaction creates replacement metadata

# Proposed Fix

1. Measure the min/max `epoch_ms` span of current `log` segments and the overlap count for representative one-hour and one-day windows. The existing L1+ sort is by `(key, seq)`, so wide time spans could leave most files overlapping even after catalog pruning.
2. Add nullable `min_epoch_ms` and `max_epoch_ms` to the segment catalog and in-memory segment metadata. Migrate existing SQLite catalogs; derive bounds for new L0 segments from the sealed batch, carry correct bounds through compaction and level bumps, and backfill old/adopted segments from Parquet footers. A bound is usable only when every row group has complete statistics. Missing or incomplete bounds keep the segment in the scan.
3. Include bounds in the same snapshot as segment paths. For safe conjunctive `epoch_ms` comparisons, intersect the time range with those bounds and pass only overlapping paths to `ListingTable`, before DataFusion footer reads and before trigram/exact pruning. Keep the SQL predicate as a residual filter; do not infer time from `seq` or file creation time.
4. Test results and planned file groups with multiple segments, out-of-order timestamps, an old catalog, missing statistics, restart/adoption, and compaction. Benchmark the same one-hour query after backfill with maintenance quiescent. Record files opened, footer load time, and wall time; lower the raised query deadline only after representative day scans fit under 10 seconds.

No open PR found for segment time pruning. #11086 and #11087 address the deadline only. If step 1 shows most segments overlap each window, time-aware segment layout needs a separate design: changing the current `(key, seq)` layout or seq-contiguous compaction can break existing pruning and segment identity assumptions.

comments.author: HRL9000
comments.body:
🤖 **Design: in-catalog min/max bounds for declared columns, like key bounds**

This matches **proposed fix 2** in the [research comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11172#issuecomment-6773719532): per-segment `epoch_ms` bounds in the catalog, filled at write, carried through compaction and level bumps, and backfilled from footers. A segment without bounds stays in the scan. Two notes on the other fixes there:

- **Fix 1 (measure segment time spans) is done: the measurements are below.** Segments are already narrow in time: across all ~1,940 live `log` files the median spans 0.5 h, p99 8.7 h and the maximum 33 h. Replaying this issue's hour against per-file bounds keeps 2 files out of ~1,660. Details are under Background below.
- **Fix 3 is more general than the snapshot detail.** The general requirement is that the query engine uses the segments' min/max statistics correctly before opening files; carrying bounds with the segment paths is one way to do that. DataFusion can already skip files from per-file statistics it is given; today Finelog gives it none from the catalog, so it has to read every footer to find them.

The design follows. It covers background, proposal, success criteria, approach, rollout, timeframe and alternatives.

### Background and Motivation

A one-hour query on `log` is slow because Finelog opens almost every file in the table to find the few that hold that hour.

- **The query.** An `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of a one-hour `log` search opened about 1,660 files, and the `epoch_ms` filter pruned none of them. After the footers were read, only 6 row groups and 5 MB were scanned. Three hub reports for similar searches show 2,313–2,379 candidate files and 6.8–8.7 s each.
- **Why the `epoch_ms` filter pruned no file.** Before it opens files, Finelog can drop a segment by its key-column bounds, its `seq` bounds or its partition. For `log` the `epoch_ms` filter matches none of these. `log`'s key column is `key` (the log source, a string), so the catalog has no `epoch_ms` bounds, and `log` is not partitioned. The key column does two jobs, sort order and catalog bounds, and `log` chose `key` for fast per-source reads.
- **Pruning by `epoch_ms` min/max would be effective, because each file covers a short time span.** `log` has about 1,940 live files. The median file spans 0.5 h, p99 8.7 h, maximum 33 h. With per-file `epoch_ms` min/max in the catalog, the issue's hour would keep 2 files instead of about 1,660.

### Proposal

Today the catalog keeps min/max bounds for one column per table, the key column (key bounds), and query planning prunes segments by them. This proposal lets a table declare more columns that get the same in-catalog bounds. They become part of the segment list that the server keeps in memory for each table, so planning drops a segment before it opens the file, with no footer read.

- **Opt-in per column.** Bounds on every column would fit (an estimated 12–39 MB on top of about 60 MB of catalog), but most columns do not prune: each file covers nearly their full range.
- **Start with time columns.** About 65 bytes per segment: about 0.7 MB for the whole hub (about 1% of the catalog).

#### Which tables benefit

Files still opened for a window from the lookback start until now, with the share skipped:

| Table | GiB | Files | Time column | 1h | 6h | 1d | 7d | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log` | 302.7 | 1,935 | `epoch_ms` INT64 | 62 (97%) | 69 (96%) | 103 (95%) | 169 (91%) | step 1 |
| `iris.worker` | 27.5 | 233 | `ts` | 51 (78%) | 53 (77%) | 54 (77%) | 62 (73%) | steps 1, 2 |
| `zephyr.worker` | 14.2 | 185 | `ts` | 29 (84%) | 41 (78%) | 60 (68%) | 67 (64%) | steps 1, 2 |
| `iris.task` | 11.0 | 327 | `ts` | 63 (81%) | 80 (76%) | 90 (72%) | 106 (68%) | steps 1, 2 |
| `iris.profile` | 7.7 | 155 | `captured_at` | 17 (89%) | 19 (88%) | 30 (81%) | 34 (78%) | steps 1, 2 |

- **Already pruned by time:** `levanter.metrics`, `telemetry_v1.node_agent`, `telemetry_v1.marinskyrl` and `telemetry_v1.vllm` (332 GiB). Their key is `timestamp_ms`, which is `INT64`, and the Grafana queries filter it with integer literals (`timestamp_ms >= {start_ms}`). Those filters reach the key-bound check today.
- The issue's hour was in the past, so only compacted files overlap it (2). A window ending now also keeps the 30–60 recent files that are not compacted yet, which is why the 1h column shows 62 for `log`. By bytes, the skip is 97% or more through 1d.

### Success

Success is achieved when:

1. On the hub, the issue's one-hour `log` query opens fewer than 100 files instead of about 1,660–2,370.
2. `iris.task` and `iris.worker` show the same kind of drop for one-hour `ts` filters.
3. Query results never change. The first implementation has tests that check this while bounds are absent or partial: a table where no segment has bounds yet, a mix of segments with and without bounds (as during the backfill), and the same after the backfill. Each test asserts that a time-filtered query returns exactly the rows it returns with pruning turned off.

Wall time is measured but is not a gate, because the exact cause of the 7 s is still open.

### Approach

**Step 1: bounds on `log`** (success 1 and 3)

1. Add a `catalog_bounds` column flag to the table spec, and set it on `log`'s `epoch_ms`.
2. Store each flagged column's min and max per segment in the catalog. Fill them when Finelog writes a segment.
3. Add a maintenance task that reads the footers of existing segments once and fills their bounds. Most of `log` is never rewritten, so this is needed.
4. In planning, drop a segment when its bounds do not overlap the filter's range. Always scan a segment with no bounds, so results cannot change.
5. Also read the `extract(epoch from now())` filter form that `lib/finelog/OPS.md` documents. Change `lib/finelog/OPS.md` to integer literals.

**Step 2: timestamp columns** (success 2 and 3)

6. Teach planning to read timestamp literals (`ts >= TIMESTAMP '...'`, `ts > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'`). Planning ignores them today.
7. Set the flag on `iris.task`, `iris.worker`, `iris.profile` and `zephyr.worker`.

### Rollout

Each step deploys to `marin-dev`, then the three CoreWeave servers, then the hub. Each deploy is approved separately. Before the hub deploy, record a baseline of the issue's one-hour query.

### Expected Timeframe

- Step 1: about 1 week to a reviewed PR, then 1–2 days to deploy.
- Step 2: about 3 days to a reviewed PR, then 1 day to deploy.

### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Leave it in place.** Add a `seq` range to time-bounded queries. | Works today, but a user must first find the `seq` range for a time. |
| **Larger footer and index caches.** | The hub reports show 12–36 footer reads for about 2,300 files and about 7,080 index cache hits: the caches were warm and the queries were still slow. A cache also empties at each restart and must grow with the table's history. |
| **Partition `log` by time.** | Finelog has no time transform, partition selection needs exact values (`=`, `IN`), and the query side does not read a table's own partition spec. A `day` column would change every writer and query and need a rewrite of about 325 GB. |
| **Make `epoch_ms` the key column of `log`.** | The `key` bounds make per-source reads (`key = ...`) fast, which is `log`'s main read path. Keeping `key` as the sort order would need an explicit sort setting, which is part of the source layout and so rewrites the table. |

In local tests, turning the flag on for one of these tables was a metadata-only change: registering the flagged schema published a new table spec version that took effect immediately, with no rewrite of existing data. - The evidence is thin: eight records from about 2 hours. A follow-up should keep these records across container recreates, so the next list can rest on a longer window.
- How much time one segment spans is not measured yet. With `seq` as the key, segments follow arrival order, so each should cover a short span. Forwarding lag and merges into the largest level can widen that.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Validate Marin's BioProBench integration against the released prompts and graders, including the LLM judge used for reasoning consistency. The integration is scoped to non-commercial research under the upstream code and data terms.

Reference: [YuyangSunshine/bioprobench at cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/tree/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d).

The release contains 1,200 PQA, 1,161 ORD, 1,200 ERR, and 772 GEN rows. REA-ERR and REA-GEN reuse ERR and GEN inputs. Reference prompt rendering matched all 6,305 mode-specific requests in direct conversion checks; curation-driver publication and live scoring still need validation.

The audit will distinguish task requirements from reference behavior: single-choice QA with a numeric confidence, a permutation of all step indices, a single True/False error judgment, protocol-generation similarity metrics, and agreement between a reasoning response and the supplied error description. Known reference behaviors to measure include accepting ambiguous True/False answers, excluding malformed answers from accuracy denominators, pair-weighting ordering scores, and judging 601 error rows even though three lack an error description.

Done when:

- All six modes publish through the curation driver and reproduce the source prompts.
- The 50-item Qwen3-0.6B smoke and full-population comparison have durable per-item records and complete graded coverage.
- Deterministic graders are compared with upstream on the same saved responses, with every disagreement explained.
- At least 20 real responses per generation mode are inspected, including unparseable outputs; the consistency judge has a frozen sample and independent blinded reviews.
- Grader errors and protocol differences are quantified, and the reviewed implementation links its validation records.

No live model scores or completed judge audit are available yet.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At Marin main commit [a9ebf7c](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/a9ebf7ceb09380b963615ddc3104012faa992285/experiments/evaluation), there is no BioProBench integration; the open PR search found no overlapping work. Marin's evaluation pipeline already has durable run records, but the pinned upstream release separates deterministic scoring from the REA-ERR LLM judge, and its portable evaluator has no REA-GEN alias. Prompt conversion alone therefore does not establish graded coverage or judge validity.

**Relevant code**
- [Marin evaluation pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9ebf7ceb09380b963615ddc3104012faa992285/experiments/evaluation/pipeline.py) — launch and artifact entry point.
- [Marin run records](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9ebf7ceb09380b963615ddc3104012faa992285/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/records.py) — durable run provenance.
- [Upstream evaluator](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/blob/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d/skills/evaluate-protocol-outputs/scripts/evaluate.py) — five graded aliases and error export.
- [Upstream REA-ERR judge](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/blob/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d/Scripts/LLM-as-a-judge_for_REA-ERR.py) — separate model judgment path.
- [Upstream terms](https://github.com/YuyangSunshine/bioprobench/blob/cf00fecd62583b98350cc48e26a29c92d3f21e5d/LICENSE.MD) — non-commercial code and data use.

# Proposed Fix

1. Pin the source revision, input IDs, prompts, grader versions, and non-commercial attribution. Publish all six modes through the curation driver, then compare its 6,305 rendered requests against the pinned source by ID and prompt bytes.
2. Run a 50-item Qwen3-0.6B smoke before the full population. Save each prompt, raw response, parse outcome, grader output or error, model configuration, and source ID in durable artifacts. Check expected counts and graded coverage by mode before reporting aggregate scores.
3. Replay the same saved responses through Marin and upstream deterministic graders. Publish every disagreement with its input, both decisions, and explanation; report malformed-answer counts and denominators separately, including the known True/False, ordering-weight, and missing-description cases.
4. Inspect at least 20 real responses in each generation mode, including unparseable ones. Freeze a REA-ERR judge sample that includes the three missing-description rows, obtain independent blinded reviews, and report agreement with the judge plus its model, prompt, and version. Document how REA-GEN is graded, since the portable upstream evaluator does not expose it.
5. Link the per-item records, comparison table, review rubric and labels, and measured protocol differences from the validation PR. Merge only after the curation, scoring, and judge evidence satisfies the issue's completion criteria.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Serve Snowball (67B-A2B) on TPU with vLLM, using data-parallel replicas and long context. This issue groups the TPU serving work from 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-20. Session routing (vllm-router) is tracked in the sub-issue https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11856.

## Changes

| Change | Status |
|---|---|
| [PR 11780](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11780): single-host data parallelism and the session router on TPU ([sub-issue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11856)) | Draft, CI green |
| [tpu-inference PR 36](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/36): give each data-parallel rank the right chips on v4/v5p | Draft, needs review |
| [vllm-project/tpu-inference PR 4010](https://github.com/vllm-project/tpu-inference/pull/4010): the same fix upstream | Draft |
| [PR 11781](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11781): pin tpu-inference to the fix | Draft; re-pin after fork PR 36 merges |

## Results

- **v4/v5p chip fix:** `get_num_cores_per_chip()` returns 2 on v4/v5p, but JAX exposes one device per chip (Megacore). Each DP rank therefore got half its chips, and TP>1 with DP>1 failed with "Insufficient devices for 2D mesh". With the fix, Snowball v0.1 on v5p-8 with TP=2/DP=2 served 16/16 requests over 8 sessions. Each rank had a 1.9M-token KV cache.
- **Launch settings that work for Snowball:** `--memory 400g --wait-timeout 3600`, and load the tokenizer from the HF repo. With a `gs://` model and DP>1, the API servers rewrite one shared tokenizer folder at the same time.

## Offloading and context

- tpu-inference supports one kind of offload: a host-RAM **KV prefix cache** (`TPUOffloadConnector`). It reloads KV blocks on a prefix hit, but one request's live KV must still fit in HBM, so it does not raise maximum context. Marin has not tried it with Snowball.
- The TPU platform rejects LMCache and the other generic vLLM KV connectors. There is no weight offload (`cpu_offload_gb`, sleep mode).
- Snowball was served on TPU at up to `max_model_len` 73,728 (v6e-8, v5p-8, v4-32). That was an eval-policy choice matching H100, not an HBM limit: v5p-8 had a 6.8M-token KV cache. 131K or 262K has not been tried.

## Related

- [Issue 11216](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11216): completions corrupt when the KV cache fills.
- [Issue 9751](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9751): tpu-inference fork refresh blocked.
- [PR 10854](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10854): sliding-window fix for TPU serving.

## Next

1. Review and merge tpu-inference PR 36, re-pin PR 11781 to the merged SHA, and land PR 11781 after PR 11780.
2. Serve Snowball at 131K and 262K context on v5p-8 on the final pin, and compare a long-context eval against H100.
3. Try `TPUOffloadConnector` on a multi-turn workload, and measure prefix-hit rate and latency.

The reported v5p-8 TP=2/DP=2 Snowball run served 16/16 requests, but 131K/262K context and `TPUOffloadConnector` remain untested.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Run vLLM's session router (vllm-router) in front of TPU vLLM data-parallel replicas, so that requests with the same `X-Session-ID` reach the same engine and reuse its prefix cache. Part of https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11855.

## Change

[PR 11780](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11780) adds `--session-router` and single-host `--data-parallel-size` to TPU vLLM serving (`marin.inference.iris_cli`). It is a draft with green CI.

## Results

- v6e-4, Qwen3-0.6B, DP=4: 97.0% prefix-cache hit rate with sticky session IDs, against 24.6% with random IDs.
- v5p-8, Snowball v0.1, TP=4, DP=1: 98.5% prefix-cache hit rate; streaming works.
- v5p-8, Snowball v0.1, TP=2, DP=2 (needs the v4/v5p chip fix tracked in the parent issue): 16/16 requests over 8 sessions. Each session stayed on one rank, 4 sessions per rank.

## Next

1. Review and land PR 11780.
2. Measure hit rate and latency on a real multi-turn agent workload, not only repeated prompts.

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
Human tokens: Goal here was to see if we can get signal from the loop at whether a small set of new RL envs is good. TL;DR which has been said in meetings is that as of today we can't! Even at init, eval-lite has pretty big variance (bigger than the effect we see from training). Furthermore, decreases aren't really interpretable since the are I.I.D. sampled from the existing training mix.

AI Tokens:

We tested whether replacing 10% of an existing RL training mix with Mark's
**October D01 math tasks** improved the model after a short run in The Loop.
This did not test his newer 4,000-task release.

## Setup

We trained two copies of the same Datakit SFT model (Grug-67B-A2B). The Loop has
the model attempt tasks, grades its responses, then updates the model using those
rewards.

- **Control:** 2,000 tasks from Snowball, the existing mixed-task training pool.
- **TaskForge:** the same pool, replacing 200 OpenScience tasks with 200 D01 tasks.
  The other 1,800 tasks stayed unchanged.

Both runs used the same code, starting model, seed and settings: **25 training
updates**, with up to four model turns per task. We chose a 2,000-task pool so
200 replacements made up 10%, rather than 0.2% of the standard 100,000-task pool.
This change required a fresh matched control.

Before and after training, we scored the same **100 held-out tasks**: 20 each in
calendar, coding, reasoning, STEM multiple choice and structured output. The
score is mean task reward on a 0–1 scale; higher is better.
[Full setup and input versions](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/24f147a3-8426-49cb-87e1-dcd63f8486c3/v/26/?workspace=rl-data-ablation&repo=WillHeld%2Frl-data-ablation-using-the-loop&type=dataset&revision=main#/file/experiments%2Ftaskforge-d01%2Fsetup.md)

## Result

| Training mix | Before training | After 25 updates | Gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Snowball control | 0.1609 | 0.3000 | +0.1391 |
| With 200 D01 replacements | 0.2100 | 0.2702 | +0.0602 |

TaskForge finished **0.0298 below control** and gained **0.0789 less**. Both runs
completed 25 updates, and all four evaluations scored 100/100 tasks. We excluded
the interrupted TaskForge attempt and used only its completed restart.

**What this means:** this pair showed no improvement. Before either run trained,
the starting model scored **0.1609 in the control run and 0.2100 in the TaskForge
run** on the same 100 tasks, despite the same configured model and evaluation
settings. TaskForge training cannot explain a difference that appeared before
training. We have not diagnosed why it happened, so we cannot confidently
attribute the final score difference to the training data.

The panel checks transfer within the existing task curriculum; it does not
establish broader capability gains or TaskForge's general quality.

[Grader checks](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/24f147a3-8426-49cb-87e1-dcd63f8486c3/v/26/?workspace=rl-data-ablation&repo=WillHeld%2Frl-data-ablation-using-the-loop&type=dataset&revision=main#/file/evidence%2Ftaskforge-d01%2FREADME.md) ·
[Scores and exact differences](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/24f147a3-8426-49cb-87e1-dcd63f8486c3/v/26/?workspace=rl-data-ablation&repo=WillHeld%2Frl-data-ablation-using-the-loop&type=dataset&revision=main#/file/experiments%2Ftaskforge-d01%2Fcomparison-result.json) ·
[Reproduce](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/24f147a3-8426-49cb-87e1-dcd63f8486c3/v/26/?workspace=rl-data-ablation&repo=WillHeld%2Frl-data-ablation-using-the-loop&type=dataset&revision=main#/file/experiments%2Ftaskforge-d01%2Freproduce.md) · [Provenance](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/24f147a3-8426-49cb-87e1-dcd63f8486c3/v/26/?workspace=rl-data-ablation&repo=WillHeld%2Frl-data-ablation-using-the-loop&type=dataset&revision=main#/file/experiments%2Ftaskforge-d01%2Fprovenance.json) ·

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## What

We propose the 50 public BiomniBench-DA tasks as a Marin in-distribution (ID) development evaluation. A model analyzes biomedical data and submits a methods report and a final answer. A judge scores them against a task-specific rubric. We used Marin’s evaluation launcher, the selected BixBench Pi harness and MiniMax judge configuration, and Biomni’s one-hour agent limit. This proposal uses external checkpoints only. [Pinned dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/tree/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235) · [Launch code, task recipes and receipts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full)

**How the inputs differ from the release.** We used the original inputs for 45 tasks. For five tasks, the released data files exceeded our Daytona account’s 10 GiB disk limit. The merged [Marin Harbor adapter PR #184](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/184) introduced two optional changes. We enabled both for all three models:

- **Two colorectal cancer tasks** (`da-1-3`, `da-1-4`). We omitted the 19.18 GB expression matrix and retained the clinical and cell metadata. The supplied cell annotations remain available, but they can no longer be rederived from expression in these sandboxes.
- **Three lupus tasks** (`da-17-1`, `da-17-3`, `da-17-5`). We replaced the 12.22 GB single-cell file with a 2.64 GB version that preserves every cell, raw counts and metadata. It omits the normalized expression matrix and embeddings. [Pinned data and conversion recipe](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/biomnibench-da-lupus-raw-counts/tree/60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83)

All five tasks remain in the 50-task score. The open question is whether the retained inputs support every criterion in their original rubrics.

## Why

- **Broader scientific coverage.** One task asks which expanded T-cell receptor clonotypes are shared across patients in a lung cancer cohort, using supplied clonotype annotations. Another explicitly asks for weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to identify groups of genes whose expression varies together in ALS spinal cord. Our review found no close counterpart for either workflow among BixBench’s 205 public questions. [T-cell repertoire task](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/blob/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235/da-4-7/instruction.md) · [Co-expression network task](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA/blob/e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235/da-15-2/instruction.md) · [Task-by-task comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6781595235)
- **An independent source of tasks.** Phylo developed BiomniBench-DA and FutureHouse developed BixBench. Including both gives Marin two independent teams’ choices about which datasets to use, which scientific questions to ask, and what counts as a good answer. [BiomniBench-DA](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BiomniBench-DA) · [BixBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench)
- **Visibility into methodological choices.** Both benchmarks require multi-step analysis. BixBench grades whether the submitted answer matches the reference. BiomniBench-DA also grades the model’s written account of how it reached its conclusion, so reviewers can inspect which reported methods met the rubric. Verifying that the model executed those steps requires a separate audit of its tool use. [BixBench verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/e96b6dcca1513e97e43523eaa971a85c68fcedae/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py#L14-L27) · [BiomniBench-DA verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/pilot/llm_judge.py#L185-L213)

## Validation

**All 150 external-model outcomes are scored.** Both benchmarks rank the three matched checkpoints Qwen, Gemma, then GPT-OSS. Whether the additional workflows help select between nearby training checkpoints remains open. The paper reports results over 100 tasks and three repetitions. Our public-50 evidence covers one pass per model, including operational recoveries. [Paper](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.12.724604v2.full)

### External-model evidence (November 20)

| Checkpoint and task-level scores | Biomni signed mean / 100 | Scored | BixBench solved / scored |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/qwen-reconciled-50.csv) | 49.72 | 50/50 | 73/202 (36.14%) |
| [Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/d411dfa070/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/gemma-reconciled-50.csv) | 21.70 | 50/50 | 62/204 (30.39%) |
| [GPT-OSS-20B](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/gpt-oss-reconciled-50.csv) | 14.74 | 50/50 | 35/205 (17.07%) |

Gemma’s replacement on `da-13-1` earned 12 signed and 17 unsigned points, giving a final unsigned mean of 25.30/100. [Final Gemma reconciliation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/d411dfa070/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/notebook.md#november-20--completed-gemma-scorecard). All five derived-input tasks have scores for every model. Qwen and GPT-OSS had unsigned means of 52.72 and 17.40. Qwen used four frozen-submission grades. GPT-OSS had 23 judged submissions and 27 verified missing submissions scored zero. For GPT-OSS and Gemma, malformed judge output permits up to four total calls on the same submission, stopping at the first valid grade. Exhausted submissions remain unscored. [Interim comparison, subgroup results and recovery history](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/notebook.md#november-20--interim-evidence-for-the-marin-id-decision).

BixBench attempted 205 questions at each matching model revision. The table uses the higher-coverage Gemma run. The other scored 60/190 (31.58%) and gives the same order. BixBench measures questions solved and Biomni measures rubric points. One pass over three external checkpoints leaves the value for choosing between nearby training checkpoints open. [Comparison records and coverage](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/bixbench-comparison-records.json).

### Inspect runs in EvalDash

The only verified BiomniBench-DA dashboard link for these baselines is the [Qwen control on da-4-6](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261113-170958-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-74446197bd5c4ddd8e5c7c5e0e596e5b-control-2d398d772a4753f281a924f06e1a3df9) (one graded task, 28/100 signed). Marina login is required.

The EvalDash API returned 404 for the Qwen, Gemma and GPT-OSS first-pass run IDs and their checked continuation or replacement IDs on November 20. For the public-50 results, use the task-level scorecards in the table above: all three now cover 50/50 scored tasks.

<details>
<summary>Protocol, input modifications and scoring rules</summary>

### Proposed protocol

| Component | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Population | All 50 public tasks; no exclusions based on model performance. Report the aggregate and separate 45 unchanged-input / five derived-input summaries. |
| Sandbox | Daytona; preserve each task's native CPU/GPU allocation (2 CPUs, no GPU); RAM = min(native, 8 GiB), disk = min(native, 10 GiB). The release requests 16/20 GiB for 48 tasks and 4/10 GiB for two. |
| Time limits | 3,600 seconds for the agent; 900 seconds for the verifier. Setup and serving startup are separate. |
| Harness | Pi through Marin's standard launcher and vendored Harbor. Pilot pin: Pi 0.87.0. The selected BixBench YAML does not pin Pi; the final baseline version still needs agreement. |
| Context/output | BixBench policy's 65,536 context / 16,384 per-response output settings, with its compaction behavior and model-specific reasoning settings. Verify effective requests. |
| Judge | MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, revision `c5454eb03678d8710e54a4e0fc681b9f3b4a3dba`, using the selected BixBench campaign's dedicated-server configuration. Preserve Biomni's rubric and grading prompt. |
| Judge request | Pilot candidate: temperature 0, 8,192 output tokens, 120-second request timeout, no SDK retries; outer verifier limit 900 seconds. These are explicit Biomni pilot settings, not a claim of identical BixBench request settings. |
| Baselines | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B first, then Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and GPT-OSS-20B. Use pinned campaign configurations and record effective reasoning settings. No Marin/Snowball models. |
| Attempts | Pilot: one attempt, no automatic trial retries. Proposed full baseline: three independent solver repetitions per task, subject to protocol and compute-budget agreement. Agree on uncertainty estimation and invalid-output/timeout/recovery rules before launch. Operational retries and judge-only recovery are not independent repetitions; do not take a best-of score. |
| Concurrency | One trial for the initial control; two proposed for the four-case pilot. Concurrency is an operational setting. |
| Evidence | Preserve per-task submissions, trajectories, judge responses, rubric decisions, failures and provenance; validate continuous-score reporting through EvalDash. |

The pilot uses Marin commit `246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7`, with local adapter/preparation files and a bundle-inclusion change. It is not an unchanged main-only execution. Freeze the complete source, image and input manifests for baseline runs. The copied Qwen configuration pins model revision `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`; the [external-model pins](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/external-model-pins.json) record all three baseline revisions.

### Changes from the release

Live create requests against the Daytona eval account rejected 16 GiB RAM and 20 GiB disk with explicit per-sandbox maxima of 8 GiB and 10 GiB. These are verified account constraints, not universal Daytona limits. The current choice is the closest supported allocation on this account without requesting a limit increase.

| IDs | Change | Reason and validation required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M01–M02 | For `da-1-3` and `da-1-4`, omit the approximately 19.18 GB expression matrix `GSE236581_counts.mtx`; retain clinical and cell metadata. | The matrix exceeds the disk limit. Verify that retained data supports every rubric requirement; expression-based annotations can no longer be rederived. |
| M03–M05 | For `da-17-1`, `da-17-3` and `da-17-5`, replace the approximately 12.22 GB lupus H5AD with the pinned 2.64 GB raw-count derivative. | Preserve all cells and required metadata within the disk limit. Validate gene/cell/donor alignment and task-specific feasibility; normalized expression and embeddings are absent. |
| M06–M07 | Disclose the five input changes in task instructions and remove copies of deliberately omitted files from image recipes. | Prevent assumptions about unavailable data; retain exact prompt/recipe diffs and file hashes. |
| M08 | Existing adapter normalizes `da-20-3`'s 72 JSON-form Docker `COPY` entries to a directory copy. | Historical workaround for Daytona Dockerfile parsing. Apply only if needed by the prepared-image path; verify identical paths and bytes with no extra files. |
| M09 | Cap RAM/disk at 8/10 GiB; preserve smaller native requests and native CPU/GPU. | The confirmed account ceilings reduce the computational budget. Record requested/enforced resources and OOM/disk failures; input fit alone does not prove analysis feasibility. |
| M10 | Replace the release's judge provider implementation with the selected MiniMax judge through Marin's verifier connection. | Align judge model/serving with the selected BixBench campaign. This can change grading decisions and requires auditing. |
| M11 | Apply signed rubric penalties; retain an unsigned comparison score from the same decisions. | The written rubric includes negative points that the released parser drops. This is an intentional scoring change. |
| M12 | Require complete, unique criterion judgments with valid levels/reasons; reject malformed or truncated judge responses. | Treat grader failures as unscored, rather than silently accepting incomplete grades. Error and recovery rates can differ from the release. |
| M13 | Prepare digest-pinned images with Pi/verifier dependencies; adapt verifier connection variables and export continuous `reward`. | Required by the current Marin path. The control image needed a separate data layer to restore its original input at its original path; runtime checksum validation passed. Preserve build recipes, package versions and hashes. |

If any modified task cannot support a required rubric criterion, that blocks the full-50 protocol. Restore sufficient inputs/resources or seek review of a revised protocol before running full baselines; do not count input-induced impossibility as model failure or silently exclude the task.

<details>
<summary>Lupus derivative construction and provenance</summary>

The lupus derivative retains `obs`, `raw` and `uns`, rebuilds `var` from `raw.var`, and links root `X` to `raw.X`. It retains all cells; it is not cell subsampling. Both `X` and `raw.X` contain raw counts. Other root groups, including the original normalized matrix and embeddings, are omitted. The original container filename is retained.

- [Pinned derivative](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/biomnibench-da-lupus-raw-counts/tree/60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83): revision `60044fab4ca09e55041729670deb55b4e6205c83`, file `lupus-raw-counts.h5ad`, 2,642,705,030 bytes.
- Derived SHA-256: `33179d1cf993091dc0bd41372629534f6b7da1ce1114d74c36110ffbee375d53`.
- Original SHA-256: `7ba85edbdc033a9aeeecabe7a1cfcb0660282cc24b04f49fb52dd3825052c620`.
- These values come from the existing adapter. Rehash downloaded bytes before use; preserve the conversion recipe, source attribution and license. Record the CRC matrix's source hash and all prepared-file hashes in the final manifest.

</details>

### Scoring and failure handling

Preserve `/app/trace.md`, `/app/answer.txt` and the source rubrics. The judge reads agent-authored reports; it does not independently verify every reported action. Audit sampled judgments against the captured tool trajectory.

For each task, sum signed rubric points, retain the raw total, and clamp to `[0, 100]`. Average the clamped per-task scores. Thus a raw −5 is reported as zero, and a reliability penalty of −10 reduces otherwise perfect work from 100 to 90. The released parser's unsigned calculation would yield 100 in the latter case. Neither calculation is established as the one used for the paper's results.

Export `reward = score / 100` for Marin's continuous metric path, preserving the 0–100 score, raw signed total and unsigned comparison in the evidence. Verify EvalDash's displayed scale; report mean rubric score, not accuracy.

The selected runner does not yet guarantee this failure contract: with no exception and a present `verifier_result`, `_read_trial` marks the trial scored even when `rewards.reward` is missing, defaulting its value to zero ([source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L207-L233)). This is confirmed by code inspection, not an end-to-end control. Add missing, nonnumeric and nonfinite reward controls alongside a valid zero; verify scored coverage as well as the aggregate. Resolve any demonstrated adapter/shared-runner defect in a scoped PR before full baselines.

Proposed failure handling:

- Confirmed empty submissions receive zero; grade partial submissions and flag them. Confirm emptiness only after successful inspection of the stopped agent's output location and successful collection. Missing files in an incomplete archive do not establish emptiness. Distinguish confirmed empty output from collection failure in result metadata before full baselines.
- Setup, collection and judge failures remain unscored. Failure to collect a report is not evidence that the report was empty.
- On agent timeout, establish that the agent stopped before capturing and grading its submission. This behavior still needs live validation for the selected runtime.
- Judge-only recovery reuses the same saved submission, rubric and judge settings; retain both original and recovery records. Record any solver rerun separately.
- Report graded coverage and all failures. An incomplete scored-task mean is not a complete 50-task score. Resolve retry/invalid-output rules before full baselines: the paper specifies a retry for invalid/missing output and then zero, which differs from the current pilot's zero retries and proposed unscored infrastructure failures.

Preserve the source instructions' paper-lookup restrictions. Record network access and installed packages; the current environment permits runtime installation and does not fully pin transitive dependencies. The unchanged-input group still shares resource, harness, judge and scorer changes; its score is not native-protocol parity.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Control checks, adoption checklist and supporting links</summary>

Initial control checks (November 13):

| Check | Result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Resource limits | Live requests confirmed the eval account's 8 GiB RAM / 10 GiB disk ceilings. |
| Scorer replay | Local controls reproduce signed 100/95/90 versus unsigned 100/100/100 for reliability levels A/B/C. These are synthetic judgments, not model scores. |
| Empty submission | An intentionally empty local submission directory emits zero and makes no judge call. The current `missing_submission` label does not itself distinguish confirmed emptiness from failed collection; this control does not validate remote collection-failure handling. |
| Control environment (`da-4-6`) | Remote validation passed for Pi, Python/R, verifier dependencies, the original input checksum and sandbox closure. This does not validate the other 49 tasks or live judging. |
| Standard launcher | Qwen control completed: 28/100 signed, 38/100 unsigned, both reports preserved, verifier status `graded`, 1/1 scored and no recorded trial errors. EvalDash API readback agrees (reward 0.28, continuous metric); this is one control task, not a benchmark-wide score. |

<details>
<summary>Preparation failures and repairs</summary>

Early image preparation failed on an interactive package-install prompt and then on a missing input file; both were repaired before the control evaluation was submitted. A local transport check timed out; the remote worker check subsequently passed. Preserve these negative records in the evidence package. They are not solver failures or zero scores. Historical Luna/GLM diagnostic scores use different settings and will not be pooled into the proposed baselines.

</details>

Before requesting ID adoption:

- [ ] Freeze the final protocol and a 50-row task manifest recording original/derived input hashes, image digests, rubric feasibility, requested/enforced resources and model/Pi/judge revisions. Agree on the proposed three independent solver repetitions and compute budget separately from infrastructure retries and judge recovery. Proposed reporting: mean each task across repetitions, then average tasks equally; report per-repetition means and a task-cluster bootstrap interval, preserving repetitions within each resampled task. Label this as task-sampling uncertainty, not a complete estimate of solver or judge variability.
- [ ] Verify transformed inputs and rubric feasibility for all five affected tasks; validate packaging, enforced resources and task-specific disk/memory use.
- [ ] Exercise good, wrong, partial, confirmed-empty, malformed-judge, missing/invalid-reward and collection-failure controls, plus timeout capture and judge-only recovery; verify coverage and continuous-score display, and audit live judgments against tool traces.
- [ ] Complete external-model public-50 baselines with per-task scores, coverage, 45/five subgroup summaries, failure rates and the agreed uncertainty analysis.
- [ ] Attach the exact pilot patch, preparation recipes and compact validation records; the linked base commit alone does not reproduce the locally modified pilot.
- [ ] Verify archived results and EvalDash ingestion/display; attach reviewable evidence links. The published task-level files above cover all 150 outcomes. Full-pass dashboard visibility remains open.
- [ ] Report wall time, startup/queue time, tokens, sandbox/GPU use, retries, cleanup and measured cost where available. Separate estimates from measurements.
- [ ] Assess incremental coverage beyond BixBench using matched external-model results and documented protocol differences. Reuse suitable existing BixBench evidence where available; additional runs require a separate agreed plan. Three model rankings alone are limited evidence and do not establish checkpoint-selection value. Resolve implementation placement and ownership with evaluation maintainers before the policy decision.

### Links

- [Evaluation launchers, task recipes, grading code and submission receipts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full) on the research branch. The receipts identify the source revision used for each submission. [Reproduction instructions](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/README.md).

- [Biology evaluation tracking #9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258).
- [Existing adapter PR #184](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/184) and [adapter source at inspected revision](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/95a4b88b54cae602ade6e79d9536a2c766657301/adapters/biomnibench-da/src/biomnibench_da).
- [Selected BixBench policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/harbor-configs/bixbench-pi.yaml) and [MiniMax judge configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/judge-model-configs/MiniMaxAI-MiniMax-M3-MXFP8.yaml).
- [External-baseline evidence precedent #11063](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11063).
- [Graded Qwen control in EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261113-170958-Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-74446197bd5c4ddd8e5c7c5e0e596e5b-control-2d398d772a4753f281a924f06e1a3df9). Scorer investigation and complete pilot provenance package: pending attachment before an adoption request.

</details>

## Cost

In the first Qwen pass, 33 trials reported 26,451,485 input tokens and 886,903 output tokens. Median solver time across those trials was 8 minutes 19 seconds. Median verifier time was 7.41 seconds across the 32 trials with verifier timestamps. These measurements exclude queueing and serving startup. The pinned MiniMax judge requests eight H100s. Total GPU-hours, judge token usage and dollar cost for the three-model comparison remain unmeasured. [Resource accounting](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/5f04629165/logbooks/45-biomnibench-da-id/full/first-pass-resource-accounting.json)

## Decision requested

**Does this coverage justify maintaining BiomniBench-DA as a Marin ID eval? If another check would change your decision, which one?** In particular, we’d like feedback on the five modified inputs, the signed rubric penalties and whether further independent repetitions are needed. If maintainers support adoption, the next step is to agree on TaskCompendium placement and ownership, then open a focused implementation and policy-registration PR. Marin checkpoints remain held out until the policy decision.

🤖 # Research

`marin.scaling_laws` has IsoFLOP fitting but no hinted-accuracy fitter. The [paper's released code](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/tree/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30) supplies per-problem outcomes, model FLOPs, a bounded multi-start joint fit, and both unhinted and two-stage baselines; its two-stage baseline uses BPB on GSM8K reference solutions, whereas this issue asks for Paloma BPB. [#11866](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11866) will produce Marin hint records, and [#11870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11870) will apply these forecasts to the hero ladder; no open PR overlaps the fitter.

**Relevant code**
- [`isoflop_analysis.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/scaling_laws/isoflop_analysis.py#L71-L99) — existing typed scaling records and Paloma metric.
- [`plot.py`](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/experiments/forecasting/plot.py#L179-L256) — joint law, optimizer, sigmoid baseline.
- [`two_stage.py`](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/experiments/forecasting/two_stage.py#L58-L93) — BPB power law and accuracy fit.
- [`data/results/README.md`](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/data/results/README.md) — released per-problem data and seed rules.

# Proposed Fix

1. Add a pure `marin.scaling_laws.hinted_accuracy` module with typed per-problem outcomes (`model`, `seed`, `problem_id`, `method`, `hint`, `rollout`, `passed`, training FLOPs) and a separate per-model BPB input; reject incomplete or mismatched model/hint grids before fitting.
2. Fit one bounded six-parameter law per hint method with multi-start least squares on equally weighted model/hint accuracy cells, using `C = log10(training FLOPs)` and `H = 0` for forecasts; return masking, truncation, and their arithmetic-mean ensemble forecasts alongside the two-parameter unhinted sigmoid and the FLOPs → Paloma BPB → accuracy baseline. Center `C` for optimization and convert the intercept back before comparing published parameters.
3. Bootstrap problem IDs as paired units across models, seeds, hint levels, and methods, retaining all rollouts within each sampled problem; return fixed-seed percentile intervals for each forecast and baseline difference, plus the number of failed or degenerate refits.
4. Add behavior tests for known synthetic parameters, held-out forecasts, paired bootstrap intervals, and degenerate grids; reproduce the paper's Delphi parameters and forecasts from its pinned released outcomes, then test the Paloma baseline separately because its BPB input differs from the paper's reference-solution BPB. Wire the #11866 records into this module only after their schema lands; #11870 owns hero-ladder fitting and the go/no-go decision.

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
Part of #9541. Hinted scaling laws ([arXiv 2611.02270](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02270)) score base models with part of a reference solution prefilled as a hint. We need this protocol in the curated eval catalog to run it on Delphi and on the hero ladder checkpoints.

Add hinted variants of two base-model completion evals:
- GSM8K 5-shot on `openai/gsm8k@740312ad`, first 256 test problems. The reference is the rationale with `<<…>>` calculator annotations and the `#### N` line removed.
- MATH-500 in Minerva 4-shot completion format (`EleutherAI/hendrycks_math@21a56338`). The existing MATH-500 benchmark has only a chat format. The reference is the solution with the final `\boxed{}` answer removed.

Hint methods, at H ∈ {0, 0.1, …, 1}, with the hint placed after `Answer:` or `Solution:`:
- truncation: the first H fraction of the reference, cut at a word boundary;
- masking: a random H fraction of the reference's words kept with a fixed per-problem seed, the rest replaced by `[MASK]`.

Trial counts: 64 at H=0 and 32 at H>0 for GSM8K; 32 and 16 for MATH-500. When four-shot MATH plus the H=1 hint exceeds 4K tokens, drop shots for that problem and record it.

Done when:
- References are pinned as a dataset and pass a blinded leakage audit of 100 references per task.
- Every sample records hint level, method, and reference ID, and per-H metrics are written through evalrecords.
- Tests show H=0 matches the plain protocol, truncation and masking produce the expected text, references contain no answers, and records round-trip.

- [`math.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/math.py#L35-L74) — pinned Hendrycks source and Minerva format.
- [`math.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/math.py#L185-L195) — MATH-500 chat source.
- [`spec.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/evaluation/spec.py#L243-L259) — fixed trial count per protocol.
- [`rollout_attempts.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/evalrecords/src/evalrecords/rollout_attempts.py#L20-L36) — stored attempt identity.

# Proposed Fix

1. Publish immutable reference corpora from the requested Hub commits. Take GSM8K test rows 0–255; match all 500 existing MATH-500 problems and answers one-to-one to `EleutherAI/hendrycks_math@21a56338`, failing publication on missing or ambiguous matches. Save source row IDs, revisions, and a corpus digest. Strip GSM8K calculator annotations and the `####` line; remove the final balanced `\boxed{...}` answer from each MATH solution. Before release, have a blinded reviewer inspect 100 randomly selected references per task with gold answers withheld, record the audit, and fix any leak.
2. Compile hints after the existing `Answer:` and Minerva `Solution:` prompts. For each H in 0, 0.1, …, 1, truncate at a word boundary or keep a seeded random fraction of words and replace the rest with `[MASK]`. Derive the mask seed from the reference ID, not run order. Use the H=1 Minerva prompt to choose a per-problem shot count that fits 4,096 tokenizer tokens, then keep that count across H and record it.
3. Register condition-specific completion variants in the curated catalog. Share a byte-identical no-hint baseline between methods: 64 trials per GSM8K question and 32 per MATH-500 question. Run 32 and 16 trials respectively for each nonzero H/method condition. Retain the existing GSM8K and Minerva graders and make the source IDs and protocol versions part of the corpus identity.
4. Carry hint method, H, reference ID, and effective shot count into typed per-sample/attempt records; reduce scores by H and method into evalrecords with scored and attempted counts. Test serialization and readback, including H=0's shared baseline.
5. Add behavioral tests for exact H=0 prompt parity, reference cleaning, deterministic truncation/masking, 4K shot fallback, and record round-trips. Run a small end-to-end evaluation and verify all condition counts and per-H metrics before running the full matrix (about 356,000 attempts when H=0 is shared).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The released GSM8K/Delphi grid has 34 checkpoints and 6,127,616 no-hint, masking, and truncation rollouts. [#11866](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11866) and [#11867](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11867) remain open, with no matching implementation PR found. The paper's 3.1 pp masking and 3.3 pp truncation values are Table 1 *in-sample fit* MAEs averaged across Delphi and four post-trained families; they are not Delphi forecast MAEs. The released GSM8K hints retain `<<…>>` calculator annotations and hint the five-shot exemplars, while #11866 specifies removing the annotations.

**Relevant code**
- [Delphi checkpoint inventory](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/reproducibility/delphi-seed-repeats.md) — published seeds and repository names.
- [Paper GSM8K prompt and grader](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/src/hinted/benchmarks/gsm8k_delphi.py) — exemplars, redaction, strict answer extraction.

- [Released result format](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/data/results/README.md) — problem-level outcomes and seeds.
- [Table 1 script](https://github.com/tatsu-lab/hinted-scaling-laws/blob/c0490e53ba8eae58bf5375f6b56956f0d57dad30/experiments/forecasting/table1.py) — pooled fit MAE calculation.

# Proposed Fix

1. Complete #11866 and #11867 with a paper-compatible GSM8K variant. Pin the paper data/code revision and each checkpoint revision. Compare generated prompts against the released prompts, including calculator annotations, hinted exemplars, answer redaction, five-shot completion format, and the H=0 prompt. Match the paper's strict `####` grader, 512-token limit, temperature 0.4, and top-k 1000 for H>0 (off at H=0).
2. Run the fit module on the paper's released outcomes without GPUs. Reproduce the pooled Table 1 values as a software check; separately record the Delphi-only fit MAE, fitted parameters, and held-out forecast errors. Those Delphi values are the relevant fit targets for this gate.
3. Smoke-test two problems, then run one checkpoint on all 256 problems at H=0, 0.5, and 1 to verify grading, output records, and measured H100 throughput. Re-estimate the issue's 25 H100-hour budget from that pilot before submitting the full grid.
4. Run all 34 checkpoints on the first 256 test problems: 64 rollouts at H=0 and 32 for each method at H=0.1–1.0. Store checkpoint revision, training seed, problem ID, method, H, prompt version, rollout, and grade. Average seeds within each compute budget, then compare every accuracy with the released per-problem outcomes using problem-bootstrap intervals. Publish the curves, pointwise differences, fit results, and any protocol or grading discrepancies.

The issue's 3.1/3.3 pp acceptance target should be replaced with Delphi-specific fit values from the released data. Report both the requested paper-only 95% intervals and a two-sample bootstrap comparison; requiring every one of 252 point estimates to fall in a separate 95% paper interval creates false failures even under a matching protocol. Keep [#11869](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11869) gated on this result.
