issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
The Iris controller rollout preflight passed on November 20 with the default Docker buildx builder selected and no GHCR push credentials. The rollout took a checkpoint, then its first image build failed because the selected Docker driver could not export a registry cache. A dedicated `docker-container` builder and a GHCR login with package write access were both needed before image publication succeeded.

Before taking a checkpoint, preflight should resolve the effective builder, including any `BUILDX_BUILDER` override, and check that it can export the registry cache used by the image build. It should also check GHCR push authorization for the configured image namespace or state explicitly when write access could not be verified. Docker reachability and a successful login alone do not establish both capabilities.

[Rollout preflight](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/scripts/iris/rollout_controllers.py#L721) · [Image build cache export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/build.py#L285)

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Preflight checks `docker info` and `docker buildx version`, but neither identifies the builder selected for the later build. The build exports a registry cache and pushes the image; a forward restart takes its checkpoint before that build. Docker documents that the `docker` driver supports registry cache export only with the containerd image store, and that `BUILDX_BUILDER` can override the selected builder. A successful Docker login does not establish write access to the image and cache packages.

**Relevant code**
- [`rollout_controllers.py#L367-L377`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/scripts/iris/rollout_controllers.py#L367-L377) — current Docker requirements
- [`rollout_controllers.py#L730-L757`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/scripts/iris/rollout_controllers.py#L730-L757) — preflight result gate
- [`build.py#L272-L292`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/build.py#L272-L292) — registry cache export
- [`cluster.py#L1392-L1404`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1392-L1404) — checkpoint precedes build
- [Docker build cache backends](https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/) — driver constraint

# Proposed Fix

1. Resolve the effective builder with `docker buildx inspect` under the same environment as the build. Check its driver; for `docker`, confirm the containerd image store through `docker info`. Fail preflight on an unsupported or indeterminate cache exporter, and name the builder and repair in the result.
2. Derive the GHCR image and cache repositories from the configured tags and the build path. Report push authorization for each as `verified` only if a safe registry check proves the granted push scope. Otherwise report `UNVERIFIED` explicitly, without treating Docker login or token presence as proof or exposing credentials.
3. Add behavior tests for the default builder, a `BUILDX_BUILDER` override, containerd enabled and disabled, malformed inspect output, and the GHCR authorization result. Update the rollout guidance so an operator sees the remaining authorization check before taking a checkpoint.

No open PR for #11878 or the buildx registry-cache check was found.

issues.title: [iris] Check buildx cache export and GHCR push access in preflight

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Symptom

At 18:34:34Z on 2026-11-20, the Iris hub's `federation-sync-cw-us-east-02a` thread crashed with `TransferBudgetExceeded` and stopped handing federated jobs to peer `cw-us-east-02a`. By 19:38–19:45Z, 47 pending jobs across 8 users were stuck on the hub in `"Awaiting acceptance by peer cw-us-east-02a"` (`PENDING_HANDOFF`, promoted on the hub but never acknowledged by `cw-us-east-02a` via `LaunchJob`), including small 8-H100 and 8-CPU jobs that fit on free cluster capacity. Direct submissions to the `cw-us-east-02a` regional controller continued to succeed. After a hub controller restart around 20:13:00Z on the same pre-fix image, the awaiting backlog drained to 0, leaving the hub exposed to recurrence.

Incident record: [Echo wiki 1035](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/1035).

## Cause evidence

- **Hub controller crash:** At 18:34:34,161Z on 2026-11-20 (`epoch_ms = 1795199674161`), hub thread `federation-sync-cw-us-east-02a` crashed with `rigging.filesystem.cross_region.TransferBudgetExceeded`: 10.00 GB already transferred plus a 13.4 MB bundle read from `gs://marin-us-central2/iris/marin/state/bundles/...` would bring the total to 10.01 GB, exceeding the 10 GB cross-region limit. No later controller log line naming `federation-sync-cw-us-east-02a` appeared up to the Finelog query time (~19:45Z).
- **Recurrence on pre-fix hub build:** This is the same crash stack as [Echo incident 982](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/982) (2026-11-13), whose fix in [PR 11399](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11399) (`aa68291f14`, merged 2026-11-17T15:42:06Z) closed [issue 11389](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11389). Hub `GetProcessStatus` (`process_info.provenance`) reports `base_commit = e9ae26899c` (2026-11-14T08:32:03Z, `tree_hash = 08b66dd6b2`, `branch = main`, `dirty = false`) — three days before [PR 11399](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11399) merged — confirming that the fix is not deployed on the running hub.

## Live observations (2026-11-20)

- **During stall (19:38–19:45Z, read-only):**
  - **Hub pending queue (all 104 pending jobs paged):** **47 jobs** across 8 distinct users showed `"Awaiting acceptance by peer cw-us-east-02a"`. The oldest awaiting job was an 8-H100 job submitted at 17:45:07Z (~2 hours pending); next oldest was submitted at 18:36:34Z, followed by a burst starting at 18:50:52Z. An 8-CPU CPU-only job submitted at 19:19:54Z was also stuck in the same state. Separately, **5 jobs** (all 64-H100 jobs) showed `"Queued for peer cw-us-east-02a to report free capacity"`.
  - **Regional controller on `cw-us-east-02a` (newest 40 root jobs inspected; timestamps are regional `submitted_at`, not accept timestamps):** The newest hub-forwarded root job (present on the hub with `peer_status = SYNCED`) was submitted at 18:33:36Z; hub-forwarded jobs were accepted from 17:45Z up to ~18:34Z, and no hub-forwarded root job submitted after ~18:34Z appeared among the newest 40 root jobs. Direct regional submission still worked (newest root job overall submitted at 19:26:36Z with no hub record).
  - **Available capacity on `cw-us-east-02a` (`kubectl`, schedulable `Ready` nodes):** **12 free H100 GPUs** across three Ready nodes (8, 3, and 1 free H100 respectively), **~1,360 free CPUs** on GPU nodes, and **~450 free CPUs** across 4 CPU-only nodes. Both the awaiting 8-H100 job and the awaiting 8-CPU job fit in idle capacity.
- **Post-restart recovery (20:19–20:21Z, read-only):**
  - Hub `GetProcessStatus` reported uptime 434.6 s at ~20:20:15Z (process started ~20:13:00Z), still on the same pre-[PR 11399](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11399) build (`e9ae26899c` / `08b66dd6b2`). Hub jobs showing `"Awaiting acceptance by peer cw-us-east-02a"` dropped from **47** to **0** (out of 61 pending total; 8 jobs showed `"Queued for peer cw-us-east-02a to report free capacity"`), with the earliest post-restart task start on `cw-us-east-02a` among the formerly stuck jobs at 20:13:19Z (no direct accept timestamp is stored; regional `submitted_at` carries hub submit time).
  - Of the 47 formerly stuck jobs, **43** appeared on `cw-us-east-02a` (22 running, 7 succeeded, 12 killed, 2 failed) and **4** were absent on `cw-us-east-02a` with hub state `KILLED` (`"Cancelled (peer reported the job gone)"`). At least **2** of the 43 (the 8-H100 and 8-CPU jobs above) were cancelled on the hub and resubmitted directly to `cw-us-east-02a` at 19:54:07Z / 19:53:35Z; the remaining **41** on `cw-us-east-02a` cannot be split between post-restart hub hand-offs and direct resubmissions from read-only controller state alone.

## Code path (checked at `main` `a9ebf7ceb0`)

- `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/jobs.py:232-244` (`_federated_pending_reason`): `HandoffState.QUEUED_HANDOFF` renders `"Queued for peer {cluster} to report free capacity"`, whereas `PEER_STATUS_PENDING_SCHEDULING` (for a promoted `PENDING_HANDOFF` job) renders `"Awaiting acceptance by peer {cluster}"`.
- `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/store.py:39`: `PENDING_HANDOFF = 0` means persisted locally on the hub while the peer has not yet acknowledged `LaunchJob`.
- `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/writes.py:838-864` (`promote_queued_handoff`): compare-and-set transition that promotes a job from `QUEUED_HANDOFF` to `PENDING_HANDOFF` for the chosen peer.
- `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/availability.py:270-336` (`assign_queued`, specifically lines 279, 288–289, and 335–336) and `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/manager.py:67` (`DEFAULT_MAX_HANDOFFS_PER_CYCLE = 8`): queue assignment walks candidates in priority-then-age order and skips jobs that do not fit, ruling out head-of-line queue blocking.

## Requested action

Deploy a hub controller image that includes [PR 11399](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11399) (`aa68291f14`) so bundle reads use `unbudgeted_url_to_fs` and one failed bundle read cannot kill a per-peer federation sync thread. Restarting the same pre-[PR 11399](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11399) image (`e9ae26899c` / `08b66dd6b2`) only resets the 10 GB process-wide cross-region transfer budget and leaves the hub exposed to the same recurrence once another 10 GB of cross-region bundle reads accumulate.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Deploying the marin Iris hub controller needs a specific set of GCP permissions, but no role names that set. Operators get it ad hoc, and a new operator finds out what is missing only when a deploy fails partway.

On November 20 a controller rollout built and pushed images, then failed at two steps:

- writing the controller VM's startup metadata (`compute.instances.setMetadata` denied);
- SSH as the `iris-controller` service account (`iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` on the VM's default Compute service account denied).

The existing operators can deploy only because they hold broad roles such as `roles/editor` or `roles/owner`. PR 11875 fixed this for one operator by copying four deploy-relevant grants:

- `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`
- `roles/compute.osAdminLogin`
- `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor`
- `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the default Compute service account

Define one `marin-infra` grant set (custom role ID `marinInfra`) in `infra/pulumi/src/iac/gcp/iam_data.yaml` (a custom role, or one documented group of bindings), and grant operators that set instead of individual roles. Include the permissions the rollout needs end to end: image push, Token Creator on `iris-controller`, metadata write, SSH and IAP. Prefer the narrowest permissions that work, and test them with a real rollout.

Done when:

- `iam_data.yaml` has the `marinInfra` role, and the current operators hold it;
- the controller rollout reference and `lib/iris/OPS.md` name that role as the deploy prerequisite;
- an operator who holds only that role and `marindev` completes a checkpointed controller rollout.

## Research

[PR #11875](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11875) added separate deploy grants for one operator. Current `main` has no `marinInfra` role. Iris pushes images to GHCR; GCP IAM does not provide that push credential.

**Relevant code**
- [`iam_data.yaml` custom roles](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dca3b9c0eb486986f49d8407dfc09efe1590f486/infra/pulumi/src/iac/gcp/iam_data.yaml#L107) — project role declarations.

- [`iam.py` bindings](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dca3b9c0eb486986f49d8407dfc09efe1590f486/infra/pulumi/src/iac/gcp/iam.py#L375) — role-authoritative project bindings.
- [`cluster.py` image build](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dca3b9c0eb486986f49d8407dfc09efe1590f486/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L194) — GHCR push path.
- [Controller rollout procedure](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dca3b9c0eb486986f49d8407dfc09efe1590f486/.agents/skills/use-iris/references/controller-rollout.md#L8) — checkpoint, restart, and verification gates.

## Proposed Fix

1. Inventory the current controller operators by encrypted principal ID and their effective grants. Define `marinInfra` in `iam_data.yaml` with the smallest [testable custom-role permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-custom-roles) for VM metadata, OS Login, and IAP tunnel access. Bind VM permissions to the hub instances where IAM conditions support that scope. Keep Token Creator on `iris-controller` and Service Account User on the hub VM's default Compute service account as resource-scoped parts of the documented grant set; preserve the controller service account's existing grant.
2. Grant that set to the current operators, then review the `marin` stack's authoritative IAM diff for unintended removals. Have a grant reviewer apply it. Record the existing `marindev` project-wide `actAs` privilege explicitly; narrowing that shared role needs a separate impact review.
3. Update `lib/iris/OPS.md` and the controller rollout procedure with the `marinInfra` prerequisite, the two service-account bindings, and the separate GHCR push login requirement.
4. After IAM review and an explicitly scoped rollout authorization, test on `marin-dev` with an operator lacking `editor`, `owner`, and broad Compute roles. Run plan, preflight, baseline snapshot, checkpointed controller restart, smoke job, and the full five-minute verify. Record effective grants and any denied permission, then tighten the grant set before calling the issue done.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

PR #10984 adds the original [GenomeQA benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05774) to TaskCompendium. Models answer 5,200 binary-choice and multiple-choice questions across six biological subtasks, using the [pinned Hugging Face dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa/tree/e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943) and the authors’ fixed prompt, without tools or retrieval.

### Why

A model can describe a splice site in words. Can it also recognize one when given a DNA sequence? GenomeQA lets us test that distinction with sequence-based questions about regulatory elements, splice sites, species, histone marks, transcription-factor binding sites, and motifs. The six subtask scores show where a model can select the correct biological label from the sequence and where it struggles. That gives us a way to compare checkpoints and track which sequence tasks improve as training changes.

Hugging Face’s biology team used a modified multiple-choice version of GenomeQA to evaluate [Carbon-X](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceBio/Carbon-X). Its taxonomy task differs from the original, which limits direct score comparisons.

### Validation

All 5,200 Hugging Face rows match the authors’ release on the evaluation fields. The runs used the fixed prompt and sampling settings from the released runner (temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95).

All six native runs are complete: **5,200/5,200 graded per run**. They use the same questions, prompt, sampling, and total output cap. GPT-OSS reasons at both settings: low/medium is not off/on. These are single-seed comparisons, not claims of statistical superiority. [Validation launch scripts and per-model configurations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/928e45d65c81fb7bd88040d40309a3685fdd2eca/experiments/evaluation/genomeqa_validation).

| Measure | Gemma off | Gemma on | Qwen off | Qwen on | GPT-OSS low | GPT-OSS medium |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enhancer/promoter | 38.60% | 36.30% | 47.20% | 50.40% | 48.90% | 50.00% |
| Splice sites | 37.30% | 23.40% | 29.70% | 32.00% | 37.70% | 35.00% |
| Species classification | 47.10% | 34.90% | 50.00% | 50.20% | 49.90% | 49.40% |
| Histone marks | 40.70% | 31.70% | 40.40% | 38.80% | 39.70% | 40.20% |
| TF binding sites | 41.80% | 39.40% | 41.80% | 42.60% | 46.30% | 45.70% |
| Motifs | 59.00% | 69.00% | 57.00% | 59.50% | 60.00% | 60.00% |
| BCQ, mean across six subtasks | 54.43% | 49.47% | 51.87% | 54.03% | 53.77% | 54.73% |
| MCQ, mean across six subtasks | 33.73% | 28.77% | 36.83% | 37.13% | 40.40% | 38.70% |
| **Overall macro** | **44.08%** | **39.12%** | **44.35%** | **45.58%** | **47.08%** | **46.72%** |
| Truncations / 5,200 | 12 | 1341 | 318 | 393 | 34 | 42 |

Gemma thinking falls **4.97 points**, with 25.79% truncation; Qwen thinking rises **1.23 points**; GPT-OSS medium falls **0.37 points**. All non-length-stopped responses in these runs parsed successfully. All 2,140 length-stopped responses remain in the denominator. Of those, 353 had nonempty final text and none contained a parseable answer. Grading available final content at the cap changes none of the six scores. Truncations materially limit interpretation of Gemma’s thinking-on result.

- **Paper comparison.** Rescoring Maverick’s 5,200 saved responses with the shared parser gives 50.58% macro (2,467 correct, seven unanswered). The prior Marin grader scored 50.60%. Running the authors’ extractor on the same final responses gives 50.62%, versus 49.07% derived from their published tables.
- **Replay.** We verified the prompts, generation settings, and weights for 31,200 saved responses. Replaying them through the corrected grader at `b706dbdc87` reproduced every native extracted answer and metric. All 26 grader/importer tests passed.
- **Shared parser replay.** Selecting the last `### Answer` section before applying the shared MCQ parser recovers 1,324 choices across the six native runs, including 1,050 on Qwen thinking-off. This reproduces all 31,200 choices of the prior Marin grader. The authors’ permissive fallback selected a letter on 306 additional native responses, all length-stopped, of which 99 matched the reference.
- **Blinded spot check.** A single Codex reviewer labeled 24 saved responses before seeing the references or grades. All 24 agreed on extraction and score: seven correct, eleven wrong, and six truncated. The sample included one truncation per run.

### Cost

**The six native runs consumed 30.03 H100-hours** including serving and recovery. Worker time sums the durations of started worker attempts. Elapsed time spans the first worker start to the last worker stop, including recovery gaps and excluding the initial queue wait.

| Scope | H100s per worker | Worker time (min) | Elapsed (min) | H100-hours |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Gemma off and on, including recovery | 2 | 399 | 5,310 | 13.29 |
| Qwen off | 4 | 91 | 91 | 6.04 |
| Qwen on | 4 | 118 | 118 | 7.86 |
| GPT-OSS low | 1 | 95 | 226 | 1.58 |
| GPT-OSS medium | 1 | 76 | 76 | 1.26 |

<details>
<summary>Model pins, usage, replay evidence, and recovery details</summary>

Current-main validation (2026-11-17, `5e07ba7498`): **23 focused tests and lint pass; all applicable CI checks are green**. The PR reuses main’s `final_only` implementation; its custom shared-code addition is removed. All six advisory lanes completed; fixes reuse the existing Parquet reader and centralize repeated constants. The compact grader and source-row dictionaries were retained because splitting this linear grading operation or wrapping boundary rows would add little value.

At `5e07ba7498`, the November 17 audit established: **all 31,200 saved answers across six runs match**, with zero source-row, prompt, generation-setting, extracted-answer, metric, or weight differences. All expected cell populations and latest graded attempts were verified. The upstream `final_only` change alters none of these results; no saved message combines a refusal field with nonempty content. Follow-up constant cleanup is semantically identical, and the shared Parquet reader preserves all 5,200 source hashes. The CPU-only audit succeeded within its one-hour cap, with **zero new model calls**.

Private EvalDash ingestion reproduces all six macros, all six subtask and twelve cell metrics, and full 5,200-item coverage. The macro remains continuous, with weighted uncertainty and no fabricated integer correct count. **A shared reporting gap remains:** `coverage.n_unanswered` is not populated by the native reader, although the saved `unanswered` metric is correct. No public records were ingested; this verifies backend reduction and measurement projection, not browser rendering.

Historical paper comparison: Maverick’s complete 5,200-question run scored **50.60%**, versus **49.07%** derived from the paper’s BCQ/MCQ table. Replaying it through TaskCompendium reproduced every per-item metric and all 120 grouped metrics with identical prompts. A separate two-question live native smoke also passed.

Review fixes in `b706dbdc87` reject `B1` and `B or (C)`, identify renamed pinned input files by digest, and independently test wrong answers and cell populations. All 26 grader/importer tests and changed-file lint passed. CI passed. A CPU-only replay of all 31,200 native final answers on the corrected grader found zero changes to extracted answers or metrics. Rechecking all 5,200 historical Maverick responses changed one histone MCQ from unparseable to a valid wrong answer (B, gold A). Its parse failures fall from six to five and the macro stays 50.60%.

**Blinded spot check at `b706dbdc87`.** A single Codex reviewer inspected 24 saved responses, four per run and 12 per format, and recorded the final choices before seeing the answer key or grader verdicts. All 24 extracted answers and grades agreed: seven correct, eleven wrong, and six length-truncated. Four truncations had empty final content and two had partial text; all six scored zero. Sampling deliberately included one truncation per run. This checks grading against the pinned answers, without estimating a population error rate or assessing the biological validity of the answer key.

Unlike the [merged SimpleQA Verified example (#11393)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11393)’s 2,048/16,384 off/on allowances, these comparisons keep the output cap equal to avoid changing both thinking and budget.

The declaration now follows the [add-eval guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8eca4ffc4b5bc9b63de1db08c3c77c8763e0b4f6/docs/tutorials/add-evaluation.md). Its curation source ID is `Eval:genomeqa`, its recipe name is `eval-genomeqa`, and its protocol benchmark key is `genomeqa`. The recipe pairs converter version `2026.11.18` with the grader hash. The publication and output-budget test passed using this declaration. The six archived model runs below used the earlier declaration.

All native inference used runtime `fe813e34c2a0d047f10a1604a12da35f162031cd`. Gemma: `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` at `4d7ae4984b7db7de8f8457170b3f1a419ee76d52`, two H100s. Qwen: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` at `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`, four H100s (TP2 × DP2). GPT-OSS: `openai/gpt-oss-20b` at `6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee`, one H100. Compilation and CUDA graphs remained enabled. Template checks and saved request options verify the selected thinking/effort controls. Other settings retain checkpoint/server defaults; these are fixed GenomeQA-protocol runs, not each model’s full recommended sampling recipe.

| Run | Input tokens | Output tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| gemma-off | 7,298,523 | 1,436,334 |
| gemma-on | 7,288,123 | 47,058,415 |
| qwen-off | 7,654,474 | 13,909,197 |
| qwen-on | 7,644,074 | 28,897,134 |
| gptoss-low | 7,812,272 | 8,041,128 |
| gptoss-medium | 7,812,272 | 8,005,514 |

Usage covers final graded attempts only; output includes reasoning and final answers without a separately measured split. Qwen thinking uses 2.08× output tokens; GPT-OSS medium uses 0.44% fewer than low. Failed-attempt usage is not included.

This is historical worker runtime, including serving overhead, not billing or a sum of authorization caps. Queue-only attempts have no start timestamp and contribute zero. Gemma’s paired/recovery workers span both modes, so their time is not falsely split. GPT-OSS low includes the preempted worker and successful recovery; its capacity-blocked recovery obtained no GPU. All inference workers are stopped. The subsequent audit is CPU-only and makes no model calls.

Native retries retained successful answers. Gemma’s final one-question recovery preserved all 5,199 prior responses; GPT-OSS low recovery preserved all 5,058. Qwen on recovered 28 first-pass infrastructure failures; GPT-OSS medium recovered 126 across two further native passes. Successful grades were not resampled. Earlier queue, connection, and preemption failures are operational history, not additional scored model failures.

Private audit evidence: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/audit-merged-main-20261117/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Faudit-merged-main-20261117%2F). Includes per-item hashes, aggregate audits, ingestion projections, worker timestamps, and the prior detailed issue record.

Native result roots: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/gemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fgemma-paired-fe813e34-20261112%2F), and `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/genomeqa/cohort-fe813e34-20261116/` · [Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fexperiments%2Fgenomeqa%2Fcohort-fe813e34-20261116%2F). Original questions/responses remain controlled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Pinned assets, parser details, and historical parity</summary>

Data: [HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa/tree/e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943), revision `e655e415fa30681dddbaf4acc182bcbd8ac41943`; only `binary/train-00000-of-00001.parquet` and `mcq/train-00000-of-00001.parquet`. The `train` split is used for evaluation. Evaluation fields match the author release; metadata equivalence was not checked.

Binary SHA-256: `0ef4c3d33541980e3fded9a5b23a952296ce3c51cb0415b42c0299a61c21938a`; MCQ: `c1cbb51449eb8a5241890337c88dc1bc0a58974b8eb4cb8bc49f310b12faeb75`.

Prompt: authors’ [run.py](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/run.py), revision `7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d`. Parse the literal without executing upstream code. Prompt-development-set disjointness has not been established. The paper’s CC BY Figure 8 differs from the runner; it is not substituted. Code/data availability statements do not establish reuse terms for the assembled dataset or runner prompt.

For each subtask, average its BCQ and MCQ accuracies; overall is the mean of those six values. Reversing the two equal-weight averaging steps gives the same result. `genomeqa_macro` uses weight 5 for the 100-question motif cells and 1 for each 500-question cell; ordinary accuracy remains unweighted. Format macros follow the authors’ [aggregation](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/collect_res.py).

The grader receives final content only. When the released prompt’s `### Answer` heading is present, it grades the text following the last heading. It accepts the last explicit option recognized by VerifyIt’s MCQ parser or a standalone option letter. A missing or out-of-range choice scores zero and counts as unanswered. The authors’ runner also scans prose for a standalone letter as a fallback. Validation reports use archived model turns to count length and content-filter stops.

Maverick (2026-11-06, historical Evalchemy path): macro 50.60%, BCQ 57.43%, MCQ 43.77%, unweighted 47.46% (2,468/5,200); paper-derived macro 49.07%. Six parse failures, no truncations or separately classified refusals. Four failures were splice-site MCQ, one histone MCQ, one TFBS MCQ. Natural-language declarations such as “The answer is X” would recover one additional correct answer: macro 50.6167%. Those counterfactual scores were not adopted. Reported API cost was $3.08, conservative accounting bound $3.93, excluding CPU hosting and connectivity pilot.

The first complete motif-MCQ cell scored 64/100 versus the paper’s 65/100; its temporary integration code was retired after the full run. The initial native replay reproduced the six historical extraction failures. The November 17 replay at `b706dbdc87` left five: one histone MCQ yielded a valid wrong answer. Both versions scored 2,468/5,200 correct. The two-question native smoke used 1,982 input and 348 output tokens ($0.0010417 API cost); it validates execution, not performance. Its provider request included seed/thinking kwargs absent from the historical run, without proving provider enforcement.

</details>

### Initial implementation

- **Protocol.** Use the authors’ fixed prompt, including its short explanation, and enable thinking wherever supported for the main comparison. Marin used a 16,384-token output cap for validation. The released runner leaves that limit to the provider. [Paper §4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05774v1#S4.SS1) · [Released runner](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/blob/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/run.py)
- **Scores.** Report the six biological subtasks first, averaging binary-choice (BCQ) and multiple-choice (MCQ) accuracy equally within each. Report BCQ and MCQ separately, giving each subtask equal weight within each format. The mean of the six subtask scores is a secondary summary.
- **Use.** Proceed with internal evaluation, including internal EvalDash review, and report aggregate results. We found no explicit reuse license for the original questions, their Hugging Face copy, or the released prompt. See the [upstream license request](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/issues/1). If a public report will include per-example traces, ask the authors for permission first. [Original questions](https://github.com/ai4nucleome/GenomeQA/tree/7ccc230e734fc11a365fd1963b593b5fd11e834d/benchmark) · [Hugging Face dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceBio/genomeqa) · [Chris’s comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10981#issuecomment-6991338723)

### Follow-ups

- **Thinking and explanations.** Our hypothesis is that all six subtasks primarily probe recognition of learned sequence patterns, such as motifs or patterns associated with phylogeny. If a model has learned those patterns, extended reasoning or a written explanation may add little to its accuracy. First, use the existing paired runs to see how accuracy changes by subtask when thinking is turned down or off while the authors’ prompt stays fixed. Then explore an answer-only prompt at that same lower setting. This second comparison would tell us whether asking for an explanation affects accuracy even at the lower setting.
- **Output caps.** Choose a routine cap for each model once we know which thinking setting and response format we want to use. A model generating extended reasoning and a visible explanation may need a different allowance from one returning only an option. When comparing settings, check truncation alongside accuracy. At the same 16,384-token cap, Gemma hit the limit on 1,341 of 5,200 questions with thinking on and 12 with it off.
- **Lower-cost checkpoint evaluation.** Test a fixed subset stratified by biological subtask and question format for routine checkpoint comparisons. issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
During the November 20 `marin` hub rollout, the CLI took a checkpoint and wrote a pending deploy record. The GCE bootstrap then failed at VM metadata and SSH authorization before it could run the restart script. The automatic rollback also failed at SSH, after writing `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED`.

The original controller was still serving on the original image. Leaving that record active meant its next boot could restore the pre-deploy checkpoint over the current database and discard newer hub state.

Distinguish a bootstrap failure before the VM changes from a failure after the new controller may have started. For a confirmed pre-bootstrap failure, keep the active image recorded and leave the checkpoint available without arming a restore. Preserve automatic rollback when the new image may have changed the database. Add regression coverage for both paths.

[Restart and automatic rollback](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1394) · [Startup restore](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/main.py#L51)

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`controller_restart()` writes `PENDING`, then treats every provider restart error as a post-restart failure. The GCE handle updates startup metadata and then runs the script over SSH; an authorization failure before the script runs currently sends the CLI through `_auto_rollback()`, which writes `ROLLBACK_REQUESTED` for the next boot to consume.

**Relevant code**
- [`cluster.py#L1407-L1425`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cli/cluster.py#L1407-L1425) - failure enters automatic rollback
- [`vm_lifecycle.py#L425-L437`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/vm_lifecycle.py#L425-L437) - VM restart sequence
- [`handles.py#L175-L181`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/gcp/handles.py#L175-L181) - metadata precedes SSH
- [`main.py#L51-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/56625db1dff04453f80f90a12599ad219f43dd26/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/main.py#L51-L79) - next boot restores checkpoint

# Proposed Fix

Before `vm.bootstrap()`, run a nonmutating SSH command and raise a typed restart-not-started error if it fails. On that error, restore the prior rollout record (or record the original image as committed when none existed), leaving the new checkpoint in storage; keep automatic rollback for failures after the probe. Add regressions for the persisted rollout state in both paths.

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
### What

Implement Olympiad and Research as separate single-turn evaluations in TaskCompendium. On Olympiad, the judge checks whether the written answer is equivalent to the reference answer. On Research, it scores the solution against the item’s 10-point rubric. The pilot uses one answer per released row on each track. [Paper, §§2–3](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21165v1) · [Pinned dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/tree/25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30)

### Why

Can a model explain *how* it reached a scientific conclusion well enough to earn credit for the intermediate steps? GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro already test whether Marin can select the right answer. Olympiad adds short-answer physics, chemistry, and biology questions. FrontierScience-Research gives each written solution up to 10 rubric points, so we can see partial progress even when few answers reach the passing threshold. ByteDance used both pass rate and mean rubric points to compare Axion checkpoints during training. [Marin eval policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) · [Axion technical report](https://axion1-0.github.io/paper/axion.pdf)

### Decisions for review

| Decision | OpenAI’s published evaluation | Marin pilot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Population | The gold set has 100 Olympiad and 60 Research rows. The paper does not say how its runner handled the duplicate Research problem. | Use all released rows. Report Research pass rate over 60 rows as primary. Also report the rate after excluding the second duplicate (row 12) and the percentage-point difference. |
| Trials | OpenAI averaged accuracy over 20 independent trials per Olympiad question and 30 per Research question. | Generate one response per row. Report a standard error across problems for each track, preserving subject mix and grouping the duplicate Research rows during resampling. One draw per row cannot measure run-to-run variation on the fixed release. |
| Solver | Reasoning models used high effort, except GPT-5.2 at xhigh. Browsing was disabled. We found no numeric solver output cap in the release. | Send the released problem in one user turn, with thinking enabled and no tools or retrieval. Qwen’s thinking switch has no established equivalence to OpenAI’s effort levels. |
| Judge and scores | GPT-5 at high effort checked answer equivalence for Olympiad and awarded rubric points for Research. Research passes at **7/10 or above**. | Use GPT-OSS-120B at high effort with the published Appendix B prompts. Give the judge the problem, visible final answer, and reference answer or rubric. Report Olympiad accuracy and Research pass rate separately. Also retain decimal rubric points and report their mean. |

For the full Qwen3.6-35B-A3B run, set the output cap to **81,920 tokens**, shared between reasoning and the final answer. Qwen recommends this cap for highly complex benchmarks independently of thinking mode. The SU-01 evaluation setup lists 131K tokens for Olympiad and 256K for Research. Record length stops by track so reviewers can judge whether the cap affected scores. [Qwen guidance](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B#best-practices) · [SU-01 evaluation settings](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.13301v1)

Use Qwen’s general-task thinking preset on both full tracks: `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, `presence_penalty=1.5`, and `repetition_penalty=1.0`. Equivalence to OpenAI’s original sampling settings is unverified. [Qwen model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B#best-practices)

For a solver length stop, grade the visible final-answer text. A correct Olympiad answer can earn full credit. A partial Research solution earns the rubric points it satisfies and passes at 7/10. Score zero if the solver produces no final-answer text. Keep length stops in the denominator and report them separately. Marin’s ID OlympiadBench scorer provides precedent for accepting a complete extractable answer when generation reaches its limit. Final-only extraction and partial Research rubric credit are explicit FrontierScience pilot choices. [ID policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) · [Pinned OlympiadBench scorer](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/c1d5c62cdc3939b42f64411af44fd50716b53454/eval/chat_benchmarks/OlympiadBench/eval_instruct.py#L568-L581)

Set `EvaluationItem.groups["subject"]` from the source row so the run records contain both track headline scores and six subject scores, one for each track and subject. Compute each headline across the released rows to preserve the published subject mix. In the validation PR, link the run records and show the correct or passing count, graded count, and expected population alongside each score. Verify coverage with `cli scores`. [Subject reporting, Figure 7](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21165v1#S3.SS1) · [Marin subgroup reporting](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/139b752890/docs/tutorials/add-evaluation.md#L130-L138)

See [published settings and aggregation, §3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21165v1#S3.SS1) · [judge prompt, Appendix B](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/2fcd284c-b468-4c21-8ee0-7a783933efcc/frontierscience-paper.pdf) · [dataset discussion of the duplicate](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/discussions/3).

### Validation

**Source checked.** The dataset card lists Apache-2.0. At revision `25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30`, Olympiad contains 50 physics, 40 chemistry, and 10 biology rows. [Pinned Olympiad file](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/blob/25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30/olympiad/test.jsonl)

Research contains 20 rows per subject, 59 distinct problem texts, and 59 distinct source task IDs. Physics rows 7 and 12 (one-based) match in every field. Assign a stable execution ID to each track and row, retaining the original task ID for provenance. Verify that both rows are sampled independently, that cached results cannot substitute one for the other, and that resuming preserves each row’s own response and grade. The 59-problem sensitivity score reuses these grades. [Pinned Research file](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/frontierscience/blob/25ed67db7da8f4591484e764008ff585544f5a30/research/test.jsonl)

**Implementation and runs are pending.** Check the compiled populations against the source counts and test Olympiad equivalence verdicts. Verify the compiled solver prompts against the pinned rows and the judge prompts against Appendix B. Check the full-run solver request payloads against the agreed sampling preset, thinking flag, and output cap. Verify that the outgoing judge request selects GPT-OSS-120B with high effort. Record the returned model identity and judge output budget. Test scores below, exactly at, and above 7 and distinguish malformed judge output from a scientific answer earning zero.

1. Smoke-test 50 rows from each track with Qwen3-0.6B. Confirm that all selected rows receive a grade and resolve infrastructure failures.
2. Run Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on both full tracks with one response per row. Reuse the external Qwen checkpoint that [Marin evaluated alongside Snowball](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/139b752890/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/model-configs/Qwen-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.yaml), `995ad96eacd98c81ed38be0c5b274b04031597b0`. Prefer item-level agreement. If only aggregate scores are available, report each track’s score and uncertainty alongside the reference, naming differences in judge, trials, and solver settings. Record expected and graded counts, truncations, and judge failures.
3. Inspect at least 20 graded responses and every unparseable case. For the grader audit, freeze a sample from both tracks and have two reviewers independently grade the same saved answers, blinded to the pilot verdict and each other. Include randomly selected responses as well as equivalent Olympiad answers and Research scores near 7. Record sampling strata and weights, disagreement on passes, and differences in rubric points. Report malformed judge outputs as grading failures. [Add-eval workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.agents/skills/add-eval/SKILL.md) · [Grader audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.agents/skills/audit-grader/SKILL.md)

Two teams published scores for the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B baseline. Neither team's exact weights revision has been verified against Marin’s pin.

| Source | Olympiad | Research | How the team reported the score |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [SU-01, Tables 1–2](https://huggingface.co/Simplified-Reasoning/SU-01#evaluation) | 65.0% | 5.0% | Olympiad averages four runs. SU-01 describes rule-based checks followed by GPT-OSS-120B for unresolved Olympiad answers, and GPT-5-high for Research. Research repeat count is unverified. [Grading details, Appendix G](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.13301v1#A7) |
| [ByteDance Axion, §4.1 and Table 2](https://axion1-0.github.io/paper/axion.pdf) | 71.0% | 26.7% | Best complete run of three. The harness supports tools under benchmark-specific restrictions. Qwen’s actual tool use on these tracks is unverified. |

The 21.7-point gap on Research makes either aggregate a weak test of grader correctness. Where reference grades are available, compare verdicts on the same saved answers.

### Cost

The full one-trial run produces **100 Olympiad and 60 Research responses**, with one grade per row. At the chosen cap, that permits up to 13,107,200 solver output tokens across the full run. The published repeat counts imply **2,000 Olympiad and 1,800 Research responses** per model at the released track sizes. The separate Qwen smoke adds 50 responses and grades per track, bringing the planned total to 260 solver responses and 260 row grades before retries or audit regrading. Empty final answers can receive zero without a judge call. Runtime and spend remain unmeasured.

### Remaining scope

Configure the serving context to fit the longest rendered prompt plus 81,920 output tokens. The earlier Marin comparison run used a 73,728-token total context. Consider EvalDash presentation when reviewing the benchmark for ID policy admission.

issues.author: hrl20
issues.body:
Finelog pins DataFusion 53 (`lib/finelog/rust/Cargo.toml`). DataFusion 53.1 and 54.2 rewrite a prefix or wildcard-free `LIKE` into min/max comparisons against `Utf8` literals (`build_like_match` in `datafusion-pruning`). Finelog types string columns as `Utf8View`, so the rewritten predicate fails to evaluate with `Invalid comparison operation: Utf8View <= Utf8`. DataFusion 55.0.0 builds the bounds with the column type.

The bug has two effects in Finelog.

Segment planning failed the whole query after #11184. #11857 works around this by building the segment pruning predicate only from conjuncts that read Int64 columns alone (`int_bounds_predicate` in `lib/finelog/rust/src/query/provider.rs`). The workaround costs integer-bounds pruning for a conjunct that mixes a string column with an integer one, such as `key LIKE 'a%' OR epoch_ms > N`.

The parquet scan hits the same error and swallows it. With a prefix `LIKE` in the filter, row-group statistics pruning is dropped for the full predicate, the time conjunct included. Results are correct, but queries of the form `key LIKE '/job/%' AND epoch_ms > N` on `log` read row groups that the time filter could skip. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the test table from #11857, as reported in [this review comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11857#discussion_r4647690138):

| Filter | `predicate_evaluation_errors` | `row_groups_pruned_statistics` |
|---|---|---|
| `timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 0 | 2 total |
| `worker_id >= 'w-' AND worker_id < 'w.' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 0 | 2 total |
| `worker_id LIKE '%-2' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 0 | 2 total |
| `worker_id LIKE 'w-%' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 8 | 0 total |

`starts_with(col, 'x')` is affected in both places because the optimizer turns it into `col LIKE 'x%'`.

Done when:
- Finelog builds against DataFusion 55 or later, including the `datafusion-datasource` and `datafusion-datasource-parquet` pins.
- The Int64-only conjunct filter from #11857 is removed, and `string_filters_run_beside_time_pruning` still passes.
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of `worker_id LIKE 'w-%' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` on that test table reports 0 `predicate_evaluation_errors` and prunes row groups by statistics.

Related to #11172.

comments.body:
🤖 Archived the description before automated prose cleanup.
<!-- marin-prose-cleanup-archive:1bb983fec662a64c2acdb50f8aea624e01b1cd94d4dff4f27f978793b0e58b98 -->

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
🤖 Finelog pins DataFusion 53 (`lib/finelog/rust/Cargo.toml`). DataFusion 53.1 and 54.2 rewrite a prefix or wildcard-free `LIKE` into min/max comparisons against `Utf8` literals (`build_like_match` in `datafusion-pruning`). Finelog types string columns as `Utf8View`, so the rewritten predicate fails to evaluate with `Invalid comparison operation: Utf8View <= Utf8`. DataFusion 55.0.0 builds the bounds with the column type.

The bug has two effects in Finelog.

Segment planning failed the whole query after #11184. #11857 works around this by building the segment pruning predicate only from conjuncts that read Int64 columns alone (`int_bounds_predicate` in `lib/finelog/rust/src/query/provider.rs`). The workaround costs integer-bounds pruning for a conjunct that mixes a string column with an integer one, such as `key LIKE 'a%' OR epoch_ms > N`.

The parquet scan hits the same error and swallows it. With a prefix `LIKE` in the filter, row-group statistics pruning is dropped for the full predicate, the time conjunct included. Results are correct, but queries of the form `key LIKE '/job/%' AND epoch_ms > N` on `log` read row groups that the time filter could skip. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the test table from #11857, as reported in [this review comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11857#discussion_r4647690138):

| Filter | `predicate_evaluation_errors` | `row_groups_pruned_statistics` |
|---|---|---|
| `timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 0 | 2 total |
| `worker_id >= 'w-' AND worker_id < 'w.' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 0 | 2 total |
| `worker_id LIKE '%-2' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 0 | 2 total |
| `worker_id LIKE 'w-%' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` | 8 | 0 total |

`starts_with(col, 'x')` is affected in both places because the optimizer turns it into `col LIKE 'x%'`.

Done when:
- Finelog builds against DataFusion 55 or later, including the `datafusion-datasource` and `datafusion-datasource-parquet` pins.
- The Int64-only conjunct filter from #11857 is removed, and `string_filters_run_beside_time_pruning` still passes.
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of `worker_id LIKE 'w-%' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000` on that test table reports 0 `predicate_evaluation_errors` and prunes row groups by statistics.

Related to #11172.

```

</details>

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Finelog pins DataFusion 53 and Arrow/Parquet 58. A prefix `LIKE` on a `Utf8View` column makes DataFusion 53's pruning comparison use an incompatible `Utf8` bound. PR #11857 limits segment pruning to Int64-only conjuncts, but the parquet scan still drops statistics pruning when that comparison fails. This upgrade also crosses DataFusion API changes used by Finelog's custom table provider, extension planners, and execution plans; [DataFusion 55's upgrade guide](https://datafusion.apache.org/versions/55.0.0/library-user-guide/upgrading/55.0.0.html) documents the changed signatures and required method.

**Relevant code**
- [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/20f92312dbb293f3789bb16535c7f5036913a2d9/lib/finelog/rust/Cargo.toml#L124-L142) — coupled dependency pins.
- [provider.rs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b493b8dc5847393e2dae39069899f9c06c9f8b7a/lib/finelog/rust/src/query/provider.rs#L406-L440) — PR #11857's temporary conjunct filter.
- [store.rs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/b493b8dc5847393e2dae39069899f9c06c9f8b7a/lib/finelog/rust/src/store/store.rs#L5674-L5693) — prefix `LIKE` regression fixture.
- [exact_aggregate.rs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/20f92312dbb293f3789bb16535c7f5036913a2d9/lib/finelog/rust/src/query/exact_aggregate.rs#L270-L335) — custom planner and execution plan.
- [group_extrema.rs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/20f92312dbb293f3789bb16535c7f5036913a2d9/lib/finelog/rust/src/query/group_extrema.rs#L258-L336) — second custom planner and plan.

# Proposed Fix

1. Base the work on #11857 once it lands, or stack on that branch while it remains open. Pin DataFusion, `datafusion-datasource`, and `datafusion-datasource-parquet` to 55; align Arrow/Parquet with [DataFusion 55's 59.2.0 pins](https://github.com/apache/datafusion/blob/55.0.0/Cargo.toml); regenerate `Cargo.lock` and check for duplicate DataFusion/Arrow versions.
2. Port `TableProvider::scan` to the slice projection, both extension planners to `PhysicalPlanningContext`, and both custom execution plans to `apply_expressions`. Compile the Rust workspace and address any additional API changes exposed by the compiler.
3. Remove #11857's Int64-only conjunct filter. Keep the Int64 bounds implementation returning no statistics for unsupported columns, and check that mixed string/time predicates retain segment pruning where valid.
4. Extend `string_filters_run_beside_time_pruning` to run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on `worker_id LIKE 'w-%' AND timestamp_ms >= 2000`: require zero `predicate_evaluation_errors` and positive `row_groups_pruned_statistics`, alongside the existing result checks. Run the Finelog Rust tests and repository lint/review gates, then open a PR with `Fixes #11890`.
