issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
## Full Qwen panel, November 20

**102 tasks inventoried; 101 planned per knowledge condition (202 Qwen trials).** Task 78 covers mutation-specific protein stability prediction and includes a toxin in its held-out examples. Its inventory entry is retained, with both knowledge conditions marked unrun and no score assigned. Report coverage against the official 102-task inventory. Once all eligible tasks are graded, each headline score has a denominator of 101. EvalDash submitted both conditions on November 20 at 16:15 UTC. The first 13 knowledge-on grades were verified in the official archive, each with positive Qwen completion tokens. Knowledge-off had 29 admitted trials and zero grades after an infrastructure interruption. Its three unused judge reservations were reconciled against a complete sandbox audit, with zero visual grader launches in the interruption window. The knowledge-off retry will reuse the original run identity and budget. [Submitted runs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7044520121) The earlier 204-trial preflight and the single-task pilot are historical checkpoints. [Implementation PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11599)

**Task 41 stays in both conditions at the released threshold of 0.73.** Flag its reference failure beside the headline results and also report each condition’s aggregate with task 41 excluded. Anika Liu and coauthors supplied the underlying study. The ScienceAgentBench team published the KNN adaptation, reference program and grader. We measured mean F1 of 0.70433 for the released reference on the released inputs with scikit-learn 1.7.2, 1.5.2 and 1.4.2. Each replay earned zero. The origin of the published threshold remains unresolved. [Original study code](https://github.com/anikaliu/CAMDA-DILI/blob/master/Machine_Learning/code/models_MD.py) · [ScienceAgentBench Verified release](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench#updates)

**Visual reference failures stay in the headline results.** Use the published task thresholds and missing-marker rule in both knowledge conditions. Task 59’s publisher plot averaged 0 (all three replies hit the output limit without a score marker). Task 96’s averaged 36.67. Both have a threshold of 60. Freeze the list of reference failures before inspecting Qwen outcomes. For each condition report the headline score and denominator, the task-41-only exclusion, and the score and denominator after excluding all flagged reference failures. List each excluded ID and its reason. Track incomplete reference checks and infrastructure failures separately.

### Publisher reference results for the 101 eligible tasks

| Outcome | Tasks | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Passed a deterministic evaluator | 29 | Task 97 used an extended diagnostic allowance. Its pass within the official 900-second clean replay limit is unverified. |
| Passed visual grading | 58 | The last recovered plot, task 52, averaged 73 against a threshold of 60. |
| Produced an output below the published threshold | 4 | Tasks 41, 59, 96 and 102. These four define the threshold-failure sensitivity analysis. |
| No completed output comparison | 10 | Tasks 11, 12, 13, 15, 70, 72, 75 and 90 encountered replay failures or timeouts. Task 17's publisher program required Kaleido for plot export. Task 49's judge request was interrupted. |

The four groups count each eligible task once. The visual ledger has 61 completed figure comparisons for 60 tasks because task 63 has two figures. The reference flags were frozen before Qwen inference began. Tasks 53 and 58 have a separate sensitivity analysis for answer exposure. [Reference results and thresholds](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11592#issuecomment-7045716068)

## Task 66 pilot result, November 19

**Qwen received 0/1 on task 66 with expert knowledge off.** The official EvalDash run used Pi 0.87.0 with a 65,536-token context and a 16,384-token reply cap. A fresh sandbox staged the task CSV after startup from the pinned release. The submitted program exited successfully in clean replay. Three independent MiniMax M3 comparisons scored its plot 45, 30 and 55. Their mean of 43.33 fell below the published threshold of 60. The judge calls cost $0.00314458. [Official shared-image run](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261119-194500-qwen3.6-35b-a3b-9d050394062043259c60bdafbc0db1dd-scienceagentbench-verified-66-knowledge-off-08d3fc592fd85680ac9670b7ab000efe)

An earlier integration run on the same case also received 0/1. It used an image containing the CSV. Its three scores were 45, 0 and 35. One completion hit its output limit without a score marker and received zero under the published rule. The matched and mismatched plot controls averaged 96 and 25. Both runs used OpenRouter with DeepInfra FP8 and fallback disabled. Equivalence to the self-hosted MXFP8 checkpoint remains unverified. [Earlier integration run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fexedev%2Fsab66-official-openrouter-1119e)

| Evidence | November 19 checkpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Official Qwen pilot | One distinct knowledge-off case, reward 0, on the earlier 1 GiB allocation |
| Full Qwen cohort panel | 204 cases prepared on 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk. Zero solver starts and zero grades |
| Publisher reference controls | 73 of 102 task IDs exercised across shared-image revisions. Nineteen distinct deterministic references passed. Visual output checks and judge verdicts are recorded separately |
| Visual-judge budget | Up to 390 candidate calls for both conditions. Up to 195 additional reference-control calls were approved under the same aggregate $5 ceiling |

## Summary

Implement [ScienceAgentBench Verified](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench)
with Pi through the native TaskSpec and EvalDash route and collect evidence for inclusion in
[Marin's ID evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197).
The proposed outcome is a reproducible implementation, complete runs on selected
cohort models through the official EvalDash path, and a documented admission
recommendation. Policy inclusion remains a separate decision.

Execution order: implement and validate the 101 eligible reference solutions, run the
202-trial Qwen panel through the official evaluation path, review its outcomes,
run the remaining cohort, and present the admission recommendation.

The task 66 pilot exercised the native agentic path end to end. The remaining admission evidence depends on validating the publisher references and running the cohort. Harbor’s existing adapter provides the comparison for the original release.

The benchmark tests scientific Python programming with supplied data across
bioinformatics, computational chemistry, geographical information science, and
psychology/cognitive science. The inclusion case will document the measured
capabilities, trustworthy grading, cohort results, reproducibility, and
operational cost. An incremental-coverage or overlap assessment against existing
ID evaluations is outside this issue's scope.

## Evidence standard

[SimpleQA Verified PR #11393](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11393)
provides an example of the evidence package for a new evaluation:

- What capability is measured and why it belongs in the evaluation set.
- Pinned data, implementation, prompts, models, and explicit protocol deviations.
- Complete baseline runs with EvalDash links and comparison to published results.
- Grading audits, failures, and limitations.
- End-to-end runtime, accelerator use, and judge cost.

Registration, full execution, verified dashboard ingestion, and policy admission
are separate milestones. An EvalDash entry alone does not establish policy approval.

## Source findings

### Verified modifies the original task population

It is a modification of the same 102 task IDs, not a smaller subset.

<details>
<summary>Annotation comparison: 41 of 102 rows changed</summary>

A direct comparison of the public annotation files at Hugging Face revision
`9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7` found:

| Comparison | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original annotation rows | 102 |
| Verified annotation rows | 102 |
| Added or removed instance IDs | None |
| Rows with at least one changed field | 41 |
| Task instruction changes | 9 tasks |
| Domain knowledge changes | 4 tasks |
| Dataset preview changes | 18 tasks |
| Source file/path changes | 15 tasks |

Field counts overlap. The comparison normalized null and empty values to the same
empty string and compared other values as strings; it is an annotation comparison,
not an audit of the underlying datasets or grading artifacts.

Changed task instructions: 12, 26, 29, 31, 32, 34, 35, 67, 92.
Changed domain knowledge: 5, 9, 79, 80.

Sources:
[original CSV](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/blob/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7/ScienceAgentBench.csv),
[Verified annotations](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/blob/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7/data/verified-00000-of-00001.parquet).

</details>

Upstream describes Verified as a release to reduce false negatives and requires
both the Verified annotations and `benchmark_verified.zip`. The November 17
artifact audit below establishes its inventory and selected grading structure.
The historical artifact link returns HTTP 404, so exact legacy-to-Verified
evaluator, reference-output, input-data, and dependency changes remain unresolved.
Do not describe this as a grading-only fix.

### Verified artifact audit — November 17, 2026

The archive linked by the current upstream README is 1,769,478,786 bytes;
streamed SHA-256: `46e715d3b2196d459d2dff52aa487f506a95ec44b44262e82208d086ea879610`.
Its 955 entries total 4,071,815,117 uncompressed bytes. Ranged reads retrieved
only the small program/rubric files for static inspection; restricted source
files remain private and were not committed or redistributed.

- All 102 annotation-referenced evaluators and reference programs are present.
  There are 110 Python files in the evaluator directory; only the annotation
  mapping defines the evaluation population.
- The selected evaluators comprise 38 deterministic and 64 visual tasks.
  Sixty-three visual tasks make one figure comparison. Task 63 makes two;
  each figure's mean judge score must be at least 60 for the task to pass.
  The single-figure visual evaluators also use the threshold of 60.
- Task 63 requires both figure outputs. Capturing only each annotation's
  `output_fname` would omit its second output; capture the required output set
  from clean replay before grading.
- Task 22 calls `pandas.read_pickle` on candidate output. Its deserialization
  requires an additional isolation boundary or an explicitly validated safe
  representation; moving program execution out of the grader is insufficient
  to isolate that task's untrusted output.
- The largest dataset directory is approximately 863.28 MiB. This is input-data
  size, not prepared image size or peak disk usage, and does not yet prove that
  every task fits the selected 10 GiB allocation.

This audit is static evidence. Reference execution, full data/dependency
validation, and the original-versus-Verified artifact comparison remain pending.

### Harbor generation is unpinned and targets the legacy split

There are two separate issues:

1. **Reproducibility:** the generator calls `load_dataset` without a revision.
   Regenerating tasks can therefore change when upstream changes. This is a
   reproducibility defect for a canonical evaluation, though it does not prove
   already-generated, separately pinned Harbor tasks are mutable.
2. **Current loader compatibility:** the generator loads the default configuration
   and indexes `['validation']`. The current HF default configuration exposes
   `verified`; the legacy `validation` split lives in a separate configuration
   named `validation`. The existing code is therefore expected to fail on a fresh
   current load with a missing-split error. This is a source-level finding; the
   adapter has not been executed here.

For Verified, explicitly select `split="verified"` and a full HF revision, paired
with the matching artifact checksum. Reproducing the legacy benchmark requires an
explicit legacy config/revision and its matching artifacts. Neither choice should
silently replace the other.

Sources: [adapter.py](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/adapter.py),
[run_adapter.py](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/run_adapter.py),
[HF configuration](https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/ScienceAgentBench/blob/9c6e96c9e74572e979b0930ee735041cef528cb7/README.md).

## Existing implementation and evidence

- [Harbor PR #630](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/pull/630) merged on
  April 18, 2026. [Upstream](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench)
  announced Verified on April 30, 2026.
- Harbor documents 102 legacy tasks: 38 deterministic and 64 visual-judge tasks.
  Recheck this classification against Verified artifacts.
- Historical parity used Claude Code 2.1.63 with Claude Haiku 4.5, five runs per
  framework: Harbor 31.76% ± 1.18 percentage points SEM; patched upstream harness
  33.72% ± 0.91. The upstream harness had output-path and dependency fixes. These
  are legacy parity results, not Verified or Marin results.
- The current README reports 95/102 CPU oracle passes, with failures attributed
  to resource needs and stochastic variation. The PR description reports 100/102;
  that discrepancy needs reconciliation rather than selecting the stronger claim.
- Earlier Marin research in [issue #9160](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9160)
  prioritized a deterministic bioinformatics subset for readiness checks. That is
  a different scope from full Verified evaluation.

Historical evidence: [README](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/README.md),
[parity record](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/parity_experiment.json).

## Grading concerns to resolve

The [Harbor verifier](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/template/tests/test.sh)
turns missing or unreadable evaluation results into zero rewards. Infrastructure
failures must remain distinguishable from valid model failures.

The verifier also copies gold references into the execution filesystem before
rerunning submitted code. Although they are hidden during agent generation, they
are accessible during that later execution. Separate submitted-program execution
from grading, including reference files and judge credentials. This is a static
boundary finding, not an observed exploitation result.

The upstream visual judge uses GPT-4o-2024-05-13, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, 1,000 output
tokens, and three completions per request (`n=3`). Missing score markers become
zero in both inspected upstream and Harbor implementations. Decide and document
whether to preserve that behavior for parity or use an explicitly versioned
failure-aware protocol. Do not silently change grading semantics. Extract, pin, and test Verified's
exact task-success calculation, including aggregation across multiple figures
and mixed checks, pass thresholds, and missing candidate-output rules. Keep
malformed judge responses separate from valid negative judgments.

Sources: [upstream judge](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/gpt4_visual_judge.py),
[Harbor judge](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/llm_visual_judge.py).

## Execution route

The development pilot ran through the official EvalDash launcher with TaskSpec, Pi 0.87.0, and Daytona. TaskSpec describes the task, files, environment and grader. Pi runs the interactive coding session. A fresh sandbox replays the submitted program, then a separate grader receives its outputs and the publisher’s grading material. The shared-image task 66 record shows this path working end to end.

The initial plan followed BixBench’s Harbor adapter because the new-eval guide at the time covered non-agentic tasks. Harbor remains the comparison for the legacy ScienceAgentBench release, and BixBench provides the Pi and cohort settings. The native route now has a graded pilot in EvalDash. [Implementation PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11599) · [Historical non-agentic guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2dd5aa45254641ef3c2977afa49cdc2afa34c1e6/docs/tutorials/add-evaluation.md)

### Implementation responsibilities

| SAB component | TaskSpec / runtime responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned task instruction and supplied knowledge | TaskSpec context, with explicit knowledge protocol |
| Input datasets and scientific software | Share a pinned software image across tasks. Before Pi starts, stage that task’s official files in its fresh private sandbox and verify their hashes. Repeat staging in clean replay. |
| Interactive coding and debugging | RolloutEngine agent harness and native Shellbox execution |
| Submitted Python program | Explicit declared file submission; keep program identity and evidence |
| Clean replay of submitted program | Reference-free execution stage with its own limits and pinned dependencies |
| Deterministic checks and visual judging | Separate grading stage using upstream Verified assets; judge credentials only here |
| Population, repeats, sampling, metrics | EvaluationProtocol and immutable corpus |
| Raw attempts and dashboard presentation | Shared evaluation runner, FineStore archive, and verified EvalDash ingestion |

The full-panel launch still depends on reference validation against the shared software, including replay-to-grader transfer of the actual outputs. The pilot establishes the launcher, archive and dashboard path for one visual task. The reference evidence below records deterministic passes, output-only checks, discrepancies and infrastructure failures separately. Cohort scores must identify the changed judge and the two known answer exposures.

## Proposed implementation decisions

| Decision | Proposal / unresolved work |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Separately versioned `scienceagentbench-verified`; pin annotations, artifacts, code, images, and task manifest. |
| Population | 102 inventoried, 101 eligible per condition. Report domain and grading-method breakdowns. Any subset receives a separate identity. |
| Answer exposure in official inputs | Keep the published files and include tasks 53 and 58 in the headline denominator in both knowledge conditions. Flag both task scores in the results. SHA-256 comparison confirmed that the agent can read byte-identical copies of both target rasters for task 53 and the target CSV for task 58. A passing score on either task cannot establish that the agent independently computed the answer. |
| Implementation home | Canonical TaskSpec implementation in TaskCompendium; shared RolloutEngine execution. Extend/validate the official agentic evaluation integration before cohort runs. Harbor is reference/parity material. |
| Agent | Pi 0.87.0, matching the inspected BixBench policy pin, across all models and both knowledge conditions. Validate TaskSpec/EvalDash integration before execution. Version upgrades require an explicit protocol decision. |
| Inputs | Selected: report knowledge-on and knowledge-off separately for each selected model. Hold task population, agent, budgets, and other settings fixed across the pair; do not pool the scores. Knowledge-off must omit supplied expert text from all actor-visible prompts, files, annotations, and metadata while preserving task instructions and data. |
| Context | 65,536 tokens total, capped at each model's supported maximum; record any model-specific reduction explicitly. |
| Output | Maximum 16,384 generated tokens per model turn, within the available context budget. |
| Agent setup | 360 seconds (6 minutes), separate from solving and image building. A setup timeout is a retryable infrastructure failure under the selected retry policy. Prepare dependencies before execution. |
| Agent time | 3,600 seconds (60 minutes) per task for the Pi solving session, including its model/tool interactions; separate from subsequent clean execution and grading. |
| Clean execution | 900 seconds (15 minutes) to run the submitted program without gold references or judge credentials, within the total verifier budget. Execution and grading remain isolated stages. |
| Verifier time | 1,800 seconds (30 minutes) total after the agent session, covering preparation, clean execution, and grading. The 900-second execution cap is nested within this budget. |
| Infrastructure retries | Up to 10 retries per logical trial for applicable, explicitly classified infrastructure failures, selected to match BixBench. Preserve every attempt and completed evidence; do not retry scored model failures. Exponential backoff with multiplier 2 and waits bounded to 1–60 seconds, selected. Map relevant error categories to TaskSpec before execution. |
| Network | Match BixBench's effective network policy, selected subject to verification of inherited task/backend settings. Freeze the resolved policy identically across knowledge conditions; document benchmark-specific download requirements and any proposed deviations before execution. |
| Build timeout | Match BixBench's preparation behavior without a benchmark-specific timeout override, selected. Verify and record the effective preparation timeout before building; absence of a campaign override does not imply unlimited build time. |
| Other budgets | Detailed recovery behavior remains to be finalized. |
| Solver sampling | Reuse the selected model's existing Marin cohort sampling configuration. Verify and persist resolved temperature, top-p, top-k and other applicable parameters before execution; keep them identical across knowledge conditions. |
| Thinking | Reuse each model's existing Marin cohort thinking/reasoning configuration, selected. Verify and freeze the actual provider request settings; keep them identical across knowledge conditions. |
| Execution/grading | Separate candidate execution from gold references and judge credentials; retain failure taxonomy. |
| Agent limit handling | On agent time or context exhaustion, preserve the work and verify any valid submitted program. Do not assign zero solely for hitting the limit or retry the solver for a better score. Distinguish missing/invalid submissions from verifier infrastructure failures. |
| Visual judge | OpenRouter `minimax/minimax-m3` routed exclusively to DeepInfra FP8 with two-image input enabled, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, maximum 1,000 output tokens per completion, three completions averaged per figure comparison. Preserve the official zero score for a returned response without a parseable `[FINAL SCORE]` marker. API errors, timeouts, and missing completions are ungraded infrastructure failures. Report the judge substitution alongside visual-task results. Agreement with upstream is unmeasured. |
| Metric / coverage | Selected: single-trial success = successful tasks / validly scored tasks; coverage = validly scored tasks / 102. Target 100% coverage; allow reporting at ≥90% (at least 92/102), independently for each model/knowledge condition. Below this threshold, withhold the canonical headline score. Keep infrastructure outcomes ungraded and adjust uncertainty under the policy. Upstream's per-task best-of-three procedure requires a separate comparison. |
| Image preparation | Start with one pinned Pi and scientific software recipe for actor and replay. Add a shared software environment only when reference runs demonstrate a dependency conflict or a disk constraint. Stage task data separately before the solver clock starts. Keep gold references and judge credentials in the private grading environment. |
| Resources | Match the completed BixBench trial with 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk. Set all three explicitly in the native episode. Three publisher references failed at the native 1 GiB RAM default and finished at 8 GiB. |
| Distribution | Keep restricted artifacts private. Upstream prohibits redistributing extracted data online. |
| Models | Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, openai/gpt-oss-20b, and google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, all present in the existing cohort campaign. Pin exact revisions before execution. |

Upstream's [metric calculation](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/calculate_metrics.py)
selects the best trajectory separately for each task, using success, program
validity, CodeBERTScore, then cost to break ties. Its reported cost averages the
selected trajectories. Our operational cost report must count all attempts,
retries, and judge calls, including trajectories that were not selected.

The official [inference instructions](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/README.md#direct-prompting-and-self-debug)
expose `--use_knowledge` as an option, and the
[native agent](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/agent.py)
defaults to `use_knowledge=False`. Including the supplied knowledge is a supported
benchmark variant. Here the repository agent means the authors' direct-prompting
and self-debug implementation, not a uniquely canonical agent protocol.
[Paper Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#S4.T3) reports both with-knowledge
and without-knowledge results for direct prompting, OpenHands CodeAct, and
self-debug. The code default does not establish a preferred paper setting.
These paper results predate Verified. Comparisons must match the knowledge
setting as well as the benchmark version. The selected plan is two separately
reported conditions for each of the three models: six model-condition cells.
One trial per task per model per knowledge condition is selected: 612 planned
solver trials, excluding validation and separately accounted infrastructure
retries. This protocol decision does not authorize execution or spending.

### Protocol comparison: paper, Harbor SAB, BixBench policy, and proposal

Paper settings refer to the original benchmark. Harbor entries distinguish adapter
defaults from the documented parity experiment. BixBench is the current Marin
policy reference, not a SAB result. Proposed results use Verified;
these protocols must not be presented as interchangeable leaderboard runs.

| Setting | Original paper / authors' code | Harbor implementation | BixBench in Marin policy | Proposed Marin evaluation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Benchmark | Original 102 tasks | Legacy 102 tasks | 205 BixBench CLI corrections v3 tasks | Verified 102-task inventory, 101 planned per condition |
| Agent | Direct prompting, self-debug, OpenHands CodeAct v1.9 | Parity: Claude Code 2.1.63 with Haiku 4.5 | Harbor / Pi 0.87.0 (policy pin) | Pi 0.87.0 with selected Qwen, GPT-OSS, and Gemma models |
| Knowledge | Both on and off | Adapter includes it when present | No analogous paired SAB knowledge condition | Separate on/off results, selected |
| Agent setup deadline | No equivalent setup timeout established | No separate agent-setup override in adapter template | 360 seconds; timeout is an infrastructure failure | 360 seconds, selected; separate from solving and image building |
| Agent deadline | No overall wall-clock limit identified in paper; self-debug code allows up to 10 iterations | Template: 3,600 seconds | 1,800 seconds; setup separately capped at 360 seconds | 3,600 seconds (60 minutes), selected |
| Program execution | Paper task-selection criterion: programs within 10 minutes; authors' code cap: 900 seconds | 900 seconds inside verifier | No analogous standalone submitted-program replay cap established here | 900 seconds within verifier budget, reference-free execution stage |
| Verifier deadline | Docker evaluation code defaults to 1,800 seconds per instance's tests; not a paper-stated agent deadline | Template: 1,800 seconds including preparation, replay, and grading | 300 seconds (5 minutes) | 1,800 seconds (30 minutes) total including preparation, clean execution, and grading, selected |
| Context / per-turn output | Not established in this comparison | Not specified in inspected adapter or parity summary | 65,536 / 16,384 tokens | 65,536 / 16,384 tokens, selected; context capped at supported model maximum |
| Solver sampling | Paper: temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95 except o1 defaults | Not established from parity summary | Cohort model configuration | Reuse each model's Marin cohort sampling settings, selected; resolve and freeze exact values before execution |
| Thinking / reasoning | No equivalent modern configuration for the selected cohort models; o1 used defaults | No explicit thinking budget established from the parity summary | Model default; no benchmark override | Reuse each model's cohort configuration, selected; verify actual request semantics |
| Repetitions / aggregation | Three runs; best trajectory per task; mean/SD also reported | Five full parity runs, reported mean and SEM | One trial per task; mean scored reward, with policy coverage rules | One trial per task per model per knowledge condition, selected: 612 planned solver trials; no best-of selection |
| Visual judge | GPT-4o; authors' code pins 2024-05-13, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, 1,000 output tokens, three completions | Same named model and sampling settings | Not visual: co-hosted MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 answer-equivalence judge; 1,024 output tokens, boolean schema, service sampling defaults | MiniMax M3 via OpenRouter, DeepInfra FP8 only, with two-image input and three independent calls using the original prompt and sampling settings |
| CPU / RAM / disk | Not established in this comparison | Template requests 2 CPUs, 8–16 GiB RAM and 20 GiB disk | The pinned comparison task declares 2 CPUs and 8 GiB RAM. The campaign overrides disk to 10 GiB. | Explicit 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk for both knowledge conditions. The earlier task 66 integration pilots used the native RAM default. |
| Image preparation | Paper does not establish a uniform prebuild strategy here | Dockerfile recipes can be built ahead of trials | The inspected campaign uses a pinned Harbor task Dockerfile with the scientific data downloaded at build time. | Private Daytona snapshots from pinned software recipes. Stage the selected dataset after startup in fresh actor and replay sandboxes. Stage evaluator and gold files in the separate grader. |
| Build timeout | Not established in this comparison | Template: 1,800 seconds | No explicit build timeout in inspected campaign YAML | Match BixBench preparation behavior; no benchmark-specific override, selected; verify effective timeout before building |
| Network during solving | Restrictions not established in this comparison | Effective restrictions not yet verified | No explicit network override in campaign YAML; inherited behavior requires verification | Match BixBench's verified effective policy, selected; identical across knowledge conditions |
| Infrastructure retries | No explicit retry limit established; three runs are independent repetitions | Transient-infrastructure retries mentioned, count unspecified | Up to 10 retries for an explicit exception allowlist; exponential backoff, multiplier 2, wait 1–60 seconds | Up to 10 infrastructure retries; multiplier 2, waits 1–60 seconds, selected; map applicable error categories and finalize recovery behavior |
| Partial-run admission | Not established in this comparison | Not established from parity summary | At least 90% valid scored trials; remaining infrastructure failures excluded from scored coverage; uncertainty adjusted | Target 100%; permit reporting at ≥90% (92/102) per model/knowledge condition, selected; success denominator is validly scored tasks, with policy-adjusted uncertainty |
| Agent time/context exhaustion | No equivalent Pi rule established | Handling depends on Harbor runtime; adapter sets limits and verifier | Preserve work and verify; no automatic zero or solver retry | Same behavior, selected |

Sources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3),
[Harbor task template](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/template/task.toml),
[Harbor verifier](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/template/tests/test.sh).
BixBench sources: [policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197),
[campaign configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/harbor-configs/bixbench-pi.yaml),
rechecked against main on November 16, 2026.

**Policy change required:** #10197 currently applies a 30-minute agent and
5-minute verifier timeout to every Harbor benchmark, with no benchmark-specific
exceptions. The selected SAB proposal of 60 and 30 minutes must be approved as
an explicit policy exception or revision before being described as policy-compliant.
The existing SAB Harbor template is not a Marin policy exception. This proposal
requests an explicit policy revision permitting a 60-minute agent limit and a
30-minute verifier limit for ScienceAgentBench Verified. Policy admission remains
pending approval of that revision; selecting these limits does not itself grant
an exception.

Under the Harbor policy, agent timeout and context exhaustion preserve the work
and proceed to verification; they are not opportunities to rerun the solver for
an improved score, nor automatic zeroes. Retryable infrastructure errors are a
separate category. BixBench's retry limit is a trial-level rule; model-request,
judge-request, and judge-only recovery retries need separate accounting. Map the
applicable exception categories to TaskSpec rather than copying unrelated
benchmark-specific exceptions verbatim. Other inspected campaign configs use 10
retries for BFCL, DS-1000, SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, TBLite, and tau3; SOTOPIA uses 3.

Author-code timing references follow below. This table should accompany the results,
with proposed values replaced by the verified realized run settings.

The [parity record](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/blob/e5a08396fce7bc230b2f023bbb568dbfa86b3ee8/adapters/scienceagentbench/parity_experiment.json)
reports Claude Code 2.1.63 with Claude Haiku 4.5 (2025-10-01), five full runs,
Modal execution, concurrency 16, and transient-infrastructure retries. These
settings do not establish exact realized deadlines or undocumented solver
sampling/context settings. Generated task defaults and actual run overrides must
be distinguished when reproducing the historical experiment.

The upstream visual judge uses GPT-4o-2024-05-13 with temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95,
1,000 output tokens per completion, and three completions averaged per comparison.
Those are judge parameters, not solver parameters. Its request timeout is 120
seconds, with additional rate-limit retry/backoff logic, still subject to the
outer verifier deadline. The 30-minute verifier limit is therefore not a precedent
for allowing 30 minutes of grading after a separate 15-minute replay.

### Image preparation strategy (selected)

Selected: prepare and validate images before scored trials, then use immutable image digests
across models, knowledge conditions, and retries. This is compatible with the
TaskSpec image route, which requires resolving Docker build recipes before
execution. A fresh container per trial still preserves isolation; reusing an image
must never reuse a model's modified workspace.

BixBench and BFCL campaign configurations explicitly require preparing selected
task images with Pi before launch. Policy #10197 describes DS-1000 images built
from pinned Dockerfiles; that statement does not establish whether builds occur
for every trial or whether caches are reused. There is no single image-preparation
procedure established here for every policy evaluation.

A completed November 5 BixBench Pi run provides a narrower historical check:
its saved job configuration and 205-trial lock select the pinned Dockerfile-based
task repository, without a prepared-image override. A sampled trial completed
grading without an infrastructure exception. Those artifacts do not identify a
final prepared-image registry or digest, so they do not establish that the
current campaign's preparation requirement was followed in that run.

SAB's Harbor adapter provides Dockerfile recipes with scientific dependencies and
task input data. Those recipes can be built ahead of time. For the proposed
Verified implementation, invoke Pi only during the actor stage, keep clean replay
free of gold references and judge credentials, and expose private grading assets
only to the grading stage. Actor and replay use the same prepared scientific
environment; the replay stage runs the submitted Python program directly.

The pinned upstream container harness builds task dependencies from imports in
the submitted program using `pipreqs`, followed by task-specific installation
rules. It uses Python 3.10 and several version ranges rather than a complete lock.
That harness was released after the paper; it is not evidence of the paper's exact
environment. Fixed prepared images therefore change dependency provisioning.
Record the resolved package lock, system dependencies, base-image digests and recipe identity. Validate every reference program before scored use.

The shared software recipe pins the runtime across both knowledge conditions. Each fresh sandbox receives only the files for its task. Record disk use and staging time independently of solver time. A changed dependency requires a new recipe version and reference validation.

The image-build deadline governs preparation work, separately from the six-minute
agent setup, 60-minute solving, and 30-minute verifier budgets. Match BixBench's
preparation behavior without a benchmark-specific timeout override. Verify and
record the effective timeout in the preparation path before building; no explicit
campaign override does not imply unlimited build time. Harbor's 30-minute SAB
template allowance is comparison evidence, not the selected preparation limit.

### Timing evidence for the protocol decision

The [paper introduction](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#S1) says agents can
usually produce a meaningful program draft within 10 minutes. This is a broad
observation, not a reported end-to-end runtime distribution or agent deadline.
[Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v3#A1) says task collection was
restricted to programs that complete within 10 minutes; this concerns program
execution, not the entire agent session.

In upstream code at `c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d`,
[agent.py](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/agent.py)
allows up to 10 self-debug iterations and 900 seconds per program execution.
[run_eval.py](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/run_eval.py)
also uses 900 seconds for submitted-program execution. The
[Docker evaluation CLI](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench/blob/c26e151ed601ba109dc4d35e057ff8e73fec469d/evaluation/harness/run_evaluation.py)
defaults to 1,800 seconds for tests per instance. These are distinct limits.
The selected Pi agent budget is 60 minutes per task, matching the Harbor adapter
default. The selected verifier budget is 30 minutes total, including clean
execution capped at 900 seconds. These are Marin protocol choices, not
paper-specified agent deadlines.

## Alternatives considered

The choices below explain the proposed protocol. Selection does not establish
runtime readiness or policy approval; the validation gates still apply.

| Choice | Alternative considered | Rationale and tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official Verified release, preserving all 102 task IDs | Reuse the legacy Harbor dataset unchanged | Verified includes upstream corrections. It requires auditing updated artifacts and graders; legacy Harbor results remain historical comparisons, not Verified evidence. |
| Retain and flag the exposed answers in tasks 53 and 58 | Remove the three matching files for those tasks only | Keeping the published inputs preserves comparability. Removing them would create a corrected-input variant. |
| TaskSpec benchmark representation with Pi | Patch only the existing Harbor adapter, or use Marin's built-in ShellHarness | TaskSpec provides the target task contract; Pi matches the selected BixBench harness. A Harbor-only update could reuse more existing wiring, while TaskSpec plus Pi requires proving the shared runner integration. ShellHarness would change the selected agent. |
| One pinned modern harness: Pi 0.87.0 | Reproduce all three paper agent approaches or reuse Harbor's Claude Code parity harness | A single harness keeps the cohort comparison consistent with BixBench. This does not reproduce the paper's harness-dependent scores. |
| Separate knowledge-on and knowledge-off results | Choose only one condition or pool both | Both conditions are supported upstream. Separate reporting exposes the effect of supplied expert knowledge, at twice the solver workload of one condition. |
| One trial per task and condition | Paper-style per-task best of three, or Harbor-style repeated full runs | Matches the selected cohort protocol and limits execution cost. It provides less repeatability evidence than repeated runs and is not directly equivalent to best-of-three results. |
| Shared pinned software and per-task input staging | Bake each dataset into its own image, or install dependencies during solver time | The shared recipe allows both conditions to reuse the same software. Each task requires a separate transfer and checksum check before Pi starts. |
| Request 60-minute agent / 30-minute verifier limits | Adopt BixBench's 30-minute / 5-minute limits | Uses Harbor SAB's configured allowances for this scientific-programming workload. Longer limits increase potential cost and require an explicit policy revision; they are not yet an approved policy exception. |
| Qwen panel: 101 eligible tasks in each condition | A two-task model pilot before the full panel | The 202-trial panel measures benchmark-wide coverage, failures, runtime, and cost and can contribute directly to final results. It exposes more compute to integration failures, so full reference validation precedes it. |
| Official launcher, retained artifacts, and EvalDash | A standalone runner with manually reported scores | Follows the evidence path exemplified by SimpleQA Verified. It requires completing shared integration rather than treating standalone execution as an official result. |
| Preserve official inputs within the initial 10 GiB allocation | Reduce data or exclude oversized tasks | First remove redundant packaging and caches without changing task semantics. Input reductions or exclusions remain contingent alternatives requiring an explicitly identified variant or subset and revised counts. |

## Work plan and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit original and Verified artifact bundles, recording evaluator, reference,
  input-data, and dependency changes alongside annotation revisions and checksums.
- [ ] Complete the implementation checks below, resolve remaining protocol decisions,
  and record a frozen configuration.
- [ ] Implement population-preserving TaskSpec conversion for all 102 Verified tasks.
- [ ] Establish the supported interactive evaluation route, including clean program
  replay, separate grading, failure classification, and resource requirements.
- [ ] Use the official cohort launch workflow and its resource controls for
  preparation, validation, and the full Qwen panel. Record resolved allocations
  and cost accounting; escalate any requirements outside that workflow.
- [ ] Verify knowledge-off isolation across all actor-visible inputs and test
  the pinned task-success aggregation, thresholds, and missing-output rules.
- [ ] Validate all oracles and representative negative controls through the supported
  validation workflow; investigate stochastic failures and reference isolation
  without silently changing thresholds. Reference-solution validation for all
  102 Verified tasks is a required gate before the Qwen panel; unresolved
  reference failures must be resolved or receive an explicit protocol decision.
- [ ] Run the full official-path panel with the cohort's `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`,
  using its frozen cohort revision and settings: 101 eligible Verified tasks in each of the two
  knowledge conditions, 202 logical solver trials total, selected. Validate the
  official launcher, retained evidence, and EvalDash. Check displayed coverage
  and grades against raw archives, and separately exercise infrastructure-failure
  handling. These results count toward the final 612-trial cohort panel if the
  frozen protocol remains unchanged and reporting gates are met; no duplicate
  Qwen run is required. Review Qwen outcomes before proceeding to GPT-OSS and
  Gemma. Execution remains contingent on implementation and validation readiness.
- [ ] Complete full runs for the selected cohort models under frozen settings.
  Link EvalDash runs and durable evidence; report coverage, uncertainty, failure
  counts, runtime, accelerator/sandbox use, judge costs, and retry accounting.
  Retain all 102 task IDs and report planned trials, attempted trials, validly
  graded trials, and successes; retain ungraded outcomes separately.
- [ ] Audit grading and compare with upstream Verified or an explicitly matched
  reference protocol. Keep legacy results and protocol deviations separately labeled.
- [ ] Present the ID-admission recommendation: measured scientific-programming
  capabilities, paired model outcomes, grading reliability, reproducibility,
  operational cost, and limitations. No incremental-coverage or overlap study
  against BixBench/DS-1000 is required.

Completion requires a reviewable evidence package and an explicit admission
recommendation. Implementation or dashboard registration alone does not satisfy
this issue. A small model panel provides initial comparative evidence, not a
robust correlation study.

## Implementation checks and remaining approvals

The protocol choices above are selected. The following are implementation work
and review dependencies, rather than prerequisites for filing this proposal.

### Implementation checks

- Resolve and freeze the existing cohort revisions for Qwen, GPT-OSS, and Gemma.
- Verify and freeze BixBench's effective network policy, including inherited
  task/backend settings, for reuse across both knowledge conditions. Document
  benchmark-specific download requirements; any deviation needs an explicit
  protocol decision.
- Verify BixBench's effective preparation timeout and reuse its behavior without
  a benchmark-specific override. With the infrastructure retry
  limit fixed at 10 and backoff fixed at multiplier 2 / 1–60 seconds, finalize applicable
  error categories and stage-specific
  recovery behavior without rerunning successfully completed stages unnecessarily.
- Confirm whether 10 GiB is a required disk ceiling or a campaign allocation.
  If a Verified task exceeds the adopted ceiling, first remove redundant caches
  and packaging overhead without changing task inputs or grading. Reducing data
  or excluding tasks requires an explicit protocol decision and a separately
  identified modified variant or subset, with an exclusion manifest and revised
  task counts. Such exclusions are not infrastructure missingness under the
  90% reporting gate; the full 102-task protocol remains the target meanwhile.
- Use the selected MiniMax visual judge with three independent calls per comparison. The completed controls and routing deviation are recorded below. Agreement with the upstream GPT-4o judge remains unmeasured.

### Remaining protocol and ownership decisions

- Agree on comparison evidence required for externally reported scores. The
  selected reporting gate is ≥90% valid scored coverage per model/knowledge
  condition; preserve all 102 task IDs and apply the policy uncertainty adjustment.
- Who owns the shared agentic evaluation-runner changes and policy admission review?
- Obtain policy-owner approval of the requested ScienceAgentBench Verified
  revision permitting 60-minute agent / 30-minute verifier limits. Requesting
  this revision is selected; approval remains outstanding against the existing
  30-minute / 5-minute limits.

## Official path and current state

The task 66 pilot used the native TaskSpec path through the official launcher. The remaining full-panel work includes reference validation and grading recovery. [Launcher documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/246f795749166285a864e891e56facfbcf9127e7/experiments/evaluation/README.md) · [Implementation PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11599)

### Visual-judge decision (November 17)

Marin uses the BixBench MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 checkpoint with vision enabled. Each
comparison sends the candidate plot first and the gold plot second, with the
original prompt, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, and a 1,000-token output limit.
Average three separate single-completion requests. A response without a matching
score marker contributes zero. A failed call or missing completion leaves the
comparison ungraded.

Both the model substitution and the change from one three-completion request
are deviations from upstream. In a six-call synthetic control, MiniMax scored
identical charts 100/100/100 and a reversed data trend 25/25/25. This checks
image-pair handling and basic discrimination at task 66’s threshold of 60.
Agreement with the upstream judge has not been measured.

Task 66’s saved reference-program plot received three scores of 100/100 from the Marin-hosted MiniMax judge. The pinned task evaluator returned reward 1 at its threshold of 60. This checks the saved reference output. Task 92 separately passed through the Harbor verifier. At that checkpoint, official Qwen solver starts and grades were 0/204.

### Shared environments and paired corpus, November 19

The curated pipeline built and reloaded all **204 rows** across the two knowledge conditions. Each condition has 102 task IDs, 64 visual evaluators and 38 deterministic evaluators. Expert knowledge changes the prompt for 98 tasks. Four tasks have identical prompts in both conditions. These are corpus counts. The 64 visual tasks contain 65 figure comparisons. Three judge calls per comparison imply up to 390 candidate calls across both knowledge conditions. Visual reference validation would add up to 195 calls, approved under the same aggregate $5 ceiling. The full 2-CPU, 8-GiB Qwen panel has 0/204 graded trials. Official pilot evidence covers one distinct task/condition. The initial implementation and the shared-software validation both scored 0 on task 66, knowledge off. Treat them as two integration runs on the same case.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Actor and clean replay | Fresh sandboxes reuse a pinned Pi/scientific software snapshot. The runner stages each task’s selected files after startup. The 405 selected files across 71 directories match the published release digests. Tasks 53 and 58 keep the documented answer-file exposures in both conditions. |
| Largest input | Three files totaling 905,216,384 bytes passed in-sandbox SHA-256 checks in 138.2 seconds with 10 GiB disk. A prior range-based attempt lost its publisher connection. Fetching the pinned archive once and extracting on the runner succeeded. |
| Offline plotting | Some climate references call Cartopy for a public coastline or land layer. The runner stages the same checksummed Natural Earth files before actor and replay startup for tasks 48, 49, 56 and 86 in both knowledge conditions. Their sandboxes keep network access disabled. Native clean replay produced all six tested plots (48, 49, 55, 56, 66 and 86), and task 66 still matched its previously graded reference output byte for byte. |
| Private grading inputs | The corpus identifies the 102 published evaluators and required gold members by path, size and checksum. The task 66 software-only grader started empty and passed both its evaluator and target-figure checksums after staging. No judge call was needed for this check. |
| Shared scientific dependencies | Tasks 29, 34, 35 and 92 also passed the native clean-replay and separate-grader path with replay exit 0 and reward 1 each. Task 66 reproduced its previously graded plot byte for byte. Adding the missing runtime library let task 32 produce its figure. Output creation alone provides no visual grade. |
| CPU and memory | Native Daytona defaults gave these reference sandboxes 1 GiB of RAM. Tasks 14, 21 and 23 each exited 137 with a recorded out-of-memory kill. The completed BixBench comparison trial requested 2 CPUs and 8 GiB of RAM through its [pinned task](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/blob/454d04b5427fd90de78d7bec9dfe57561a21ff03/datasets/bixbench-cli-marin-corrections-1/bix-1-q1/task.toml), and the campaign set disk to 10 GiB. With those BixBench requests, all three references finished with no out-of-memory kills. Task 21 received reward 1. Tasks 14 and 23 produced plots. Their peak memory ranged from 1.07 to 1.45 GiB. The full-panel recipe now requests 2 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk explicitly. |

At the November 19 checkpoint, CPU diagnostics had exercised 73 of the 102 publisher reference programs across shared-image revisions. Nineteen distinct deterministic references received reward 1, including ten through native clean replay and a separate grader (16, 18, 19, 21, 29, 34, 35, 40, 53 and 92). Task 41’s publisher program exited successfully twice and received reward 0 both times. The released evaluator (eval_MD_KNN.py) sets the mean F1 threshold at 0.73 across three prediction files. Our measured mean F1 was 0.70433. The Verified annotation credits Anika Liu and coauthors’ [CAMDA-DILI source study](https://github.com/anikaliu/CAMDA-DILI). Its linked models_MD.py uses random forests and SVMs. The benchmark authors distributed the KNN adaptation (MD_KNN.py) and its scorer in their [Verified release](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench#updates). The original study pinned scikit-learn 0.21.2 and Python 3.6.7. The benchmark harness installs scikit-learn without an exact version. The shared image uses scikit-learn 1.7.2. Separate replays with scikit-learn 1.5.2 and 1.4.2 produced the same mean F1 as 1.7.2, to all recorded digits. These checks leave the origin of the 0.73 threshold unresolved. Task 90 received zero because its reference failed during clean replay with the 900-second limit. Its saved diagnostic omits the exit reason, so timeout attribution is unconfirmed. Tasks 21 and 53 encountered network failures on two native grading attempts each. Both recovered after adding a fallback from interrupted range reads to the full digest-verified release. Their publisher references passed native grading with reward 1. Task 53 retains its documented answer exposure. All of these are environment and scoring controls, separate from Qwen results.

The 29 references still unattempted at that checkpoint included three glacier tasks that import OGGM (64, 65 and 74), two materials tasks that import MODNet (101 and 102), and two EEG tasks that import PyTorch (71 and 72). The new image includes CPU PyTorch. These import checks identify the next validation work. They do not establish that any reference runs successfully.

Three additional references identified gaps in the shared dependency lock. Task 30 expects an older Phonopy API, task 36 requires a BioPsyKit release with MuseDataset, and task 69 requires scikit-misc. The BioPsyKit versions exposing MuseDataset depend transitively on docopt, which has no compatible wheel on the selected index. A lock pinning docopt 0.6.2 built successfully in a single private image with BioPsyKit 0.11.0, Phonopy 2.38.2, scikit-misc 0.5.3 and the CPU-only PyTorch wheel. The new private shared image produced the expected plots for tasks 30 and 36. Fourteen additional references finished, including a deterministic pass on task 44 and output plots on the other thirteen. Task 69 progressed to execution but exceeded the short 180-second diagnostic allowance. With the configured 900-second allowance, native clean replay finished successfully on task 69 and produced its 97,885-byte plot. Task 66’s reference plot remained byte-identical after the image change. Neither replay called a judge.

Two initial official staged-input attempts failed during Daytona startup. A subsequent snapshot-backed attempt was preempted and hit its single-attempt cap on recovery. Its archive contained a start record and no completed response or grade. At that checkpoint, reference controls were pending for the original 204-trial plan. The [official shared-software task 66 run](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261119-194500-qwen3.6-35b-a3b-9d050394062043259c60bdafbc0db1dd-scienceagentbench-verified-66-knowledge-off-08d3fc592fd85680ac9670b7ab000efe) finished successfully. Clean replay exited 0. The three visual grades were 45, 30 and 55, for a mean of 43.33 against the task threshold of 60 and a binary reward of 0. The run used 34,368 prompt tokens and 2,459 completion tokens. The three judge calls cost $0.00314458 in total. It used the earlier 1 GiB pilot allocation.

The pilot capped each trial at one attempt. The native runner checks its attempt cap on resume, and skips completed grades, submission failures and invalid tasks. For agent episodes it can rerun the solver after a grading infrastructure failure. The full-panel launch needs an explicit mapping for the selected ten infrastructure retries, recovery of saved submissions where possible, and accounting that enforces the aggregate judge budget across retries.

On November 19, the approved OpenRouter/DeepInfra FP8 reference check on task 66 scored 100 in all three completions. The publisher reference passed its threshold of 60 at a cost of $0.001097144. This is a reference control. The official Qwen candidate grade remains 0/1.

On November 20, visual reference replay covered all 64 visual tasks. Fifty-three produced plots and eleven failed before judging (9, 17, 38, 39, 52, 64, 65, 70, 74, 75, 98). The Qwen panel has no separate wall-clock cutoff. Per-task limits and the aggregate visual-judge budget still apply.

comments.body:
🤖 Triage: #11592 spans benchmark conversion, shared evaluation support, validation, and an ID-policy decision. The issue records no ScienceAgentBench implementation or runs, and no matching open PR is present. The [current launcher](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/README.md#agentic-benchmarks-harbor) documents Harbor agentic evaluations; the proposed TaskSpec route still needs an interactive harness, isolated replay and grading, and verified EvalDash ingestion.

Plan:

issues.author: alioramuss
issues.body:
Hi, I'd like to add an eval and wanted to check it's wanted before sending a PR.

**What:** TUMLU-mini, from *TUMLU: A Unified and Native Language Understanding Benchmark for Turkic Languages* (Isbarov et al., ACL 2025 main conference). These are school-level multiple-choice questions written natively in each language, not translated from English. The dataset is `jafarisbarov/TUMLU-mini` on Hugging Face, CC BY 4.0, with a 35-row dev split and a 700-row test split per language across seven subjects.

**Why, given INCLUDE is already there:** `INCLUDE_44_TASKS` covers Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Turkish and Uzbek. TUMLU adds Tatar, Crimean Tatar, Karakalpak and Uyghur, which aren't covered anywhere in Marin as far as I can see. For the overlapping languages it gives a second, school-curriculum view (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Maths, Geography, History, Native Language and Literature), so you could check whether INCLUDE results hold up on a different native source.

**Plan:**
* Follow the pattern from the LEXam change (#11778): a benchmark file in `experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/`, an importer and scorer in `taskcompendium`, a catalog entry and tests
* Pin the Hugging Face revision and set the expected population per language, the way LEXam does
* Add it to the eval list in `prepare_eval_corpus.py` so decontamination covers it
* I'm a native Azerbaijani speaker, so I'd start with Azerbaijani, check the prompt and extraction by hand, and then add the other languages

**Questions:**
1. Should this go in the new `experiments/evaluation` setup like LEXam, or as a 5-shot task next to INCLUDE in `task_configs.py`?
2. One benchmark per language, or one with a language parameter?

I've also proposed this to HELM (stanford-crfm/helm#4385), but since HELM is in maintenance mode, Marin seems like the better home. Happy to do the work either way.

Ali (@alioramuss)

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
Passing an `s3://` (or `gs://`) URI to `TrainerConfig.log_dir` or `dump_grug_state_sharding_run_artifact(..., path_override=...)` coerces it through `pathlib.Path`, collapsing `s3://bucket/...` into the relative local path `s3:/bucket/...`. Downstream `StoragePath(str(path))` calls then see no `://` scheme and write to `./s3:/...` on ephemeral pod disk without error, so files such as `state-sharding.json` and log-dir artifacts (`split_step_after_grad.json`, `split_step_after_opt.json`) silently never reach object storage. In a 64-GPU diagnostic run, these diagnostic and sharding outputs were lost on pod exit (only the tracker-uploaded `grug_sharding_spec` survived).

Reproduce:
1. Configure `trainer.trainer.log_dir` to `"s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/logs"` or `sharding_dump_path` (`path_override`) to `"s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/state-sharding.json"`.
2. Decode `TrainerConfig` (`lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py:890` coerces `log_dir` to `PosixPath("s3:/...")`) or invoke `dump_grug_state_sharding_run_artifact` (`experiments/grug/sharding_dump.py:51`).
3. Observe `StoragePath(str(path))` writing to local relative `./s3:/...` and the configured `s3://` URI returning `FileNotFoundError` on readback.

Expected: Remote URLs (`s3://`, `gs://`, etc.) are kept as `str` / `StoragePath` and opened through `fsspec` (`StoragePath`), or rejected with a loud error where only a local filesystem path is supported.

## Where (verified on `main` `eecb397a0c`)

- `lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py:890`: `log_dir: Path = Path("logs/")` coerces remote URIs at config decode time. Downstream sites: `:677` (`str(self.config.log_dir / self.run_id / "profiler")`), `:823-835` (`Trainer.write_artifact` calls `os.makedirs(dir, exist_ok=True)` and `StoragePath(str(artifact_path))` on the already-mangled path), and `:1039` (`levanter.utils.logging.init_logging(self.log_dir, f"{id}.log")`). `lib/levanter/src/levanter/utils/profile_dirs.py:89` also passes `log_dir` into `StoragePath(log_dir)`.
- `experiments/grug/sharding_dump.py:30-56, 80-83`: `Path(path_override)` (`L51`) and `Path(log_dir) / run_id / "artifacts" / GRUG_SHARDING_DUMP_FILENAME` (`L56`) collapse `s3://` to `s3:/` right before `StoragePath(str(path)).write_text(...)` (`L35`) and `StoragePath(str(path)).parent.mkdirs()` (`L81-83`).
- `lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem/storage_path.py:53`: `StoragePath` detects remote schemes via `if "://" in value:`, so `s3:/...` silently parses as a local relative path.
- Note for fixing `TrainerConfig.log_dir`: `lib/levanter/src/levanter/utils/logging.py:29-31, 42` uses `Path(log_dir).mkdir(...)` and `logging.FileHandler(path)` (local-only), so preserving remote `log_dir` URIs needs explicit handling in `init_logging` (local log directory fallback or loud error) rather than crashing `FileHandler`.

## Observed evidence (2026-11-20, 64-GPU run)

- Configured valid `s3://` URIs for `trainer.trainer.log_dir` and `trainer.sharding_dump_path`.
- Rank-0 `levanter.json_logger` (`2026-11-20T22:17:04Z`) emitted `"path": "s3:/marin-us-east-02a/.../state-sharding.json"` (single slash), and `diagnostic-summary.json` recorded `"s3:/.../artifacts/split_step_after_grad.json"` and `split_step_after_opt.json` (diagnostic artifacts derived from `str(trainer.log_dir)`).
- Live S3 readback of the run prefix (`69` objects) found `consumed-config.json`, `diagnostic-summary.json`, and `timing/native-sft/rank-*.jsonl`, while `state-sharding.json`, `logs/`, `split_step_after_grad.json`, and `split_step_after_opt.json` were all absent (`FileNotFoundError`).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research
`TrainerConfig.log_dir` is decoded as `Path`, so `s3://...` becomes `s3:/...` before artifact writes reach `StoragePath`; Grug repeats the conversion for `path_override`. `init_logging` and tracker artifact staging require local files, so accepting a remote trainer log directory needs a broader storage contract.

**Relevant code**
- [`trainer.py#L890`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L890) — config path coercion
- [`trainer.py#L823-L835`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L823-L835) — artifact write and tracker call
- [`sharding_dump.py#L30-L56`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/experiments/grug/sharding_dump.py#L30-L56) — override conversion
- [`logging.py#L29-L42`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/lib/levanter/src/levanter/utils/logging.py#L29-L42) — local file handler
- [`background.py#L67-L75`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tracker/background.py#L67-L75) — local artifact staging

# Proposed Fix
1. Keep `TrainerConfig.log_dir` as a scheme-preserving string until validation. Reject URL schemes at config construction, then route local consumers through one validated `Path` accessor. This makes a remote `log_dir` fail before it creates `./s3:/...` or starts training.
2. Parse Grug `path_override` with `StoragePath` and write its JSON through that type. For remote destinations, pass a local staged copy to trackers so the existing `grug_sharding_spec` upload still works.
3. Add config-decode and local-path controls plus a `memory://` dump readback regression; then run the touched package tests, pyrefly, pre-commit, and PR lint review before a `Fixes #11896` PR. Full remote `log_dir` support needs a separate contract for file logs and profiler captures, which require local paths today.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
On 64 H100 (CoreWeave cw-us-east-02a, JAX 0.11.1, Snowball e12 FP32 SFT, 8x8 mesh, `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`), the same `jit_train_step` executable runs at about 122 s/step in the process that compiled it, and at about 45 s/step in a fresh process that loads it from the persistent JAX compilation cache. The cause is not known.

**Evidence**

| Run | Cache | Steady step |
|---|---|---:|
| Controlled pre-job (3 updates, empty cache) | miss, compile 14.2 s | 125.7, 122.5 s |
| Same config, next job, same cache URI | hit, 2.6 s | 49.4, 41.7, 44.4, 46.8 s |
| Distillation arm A, alpha 0 (compiled in-process; cache entry `jit_train_step-a19e8a54…`) | miss | 122 s (MFU 6.9%) |
| Same code and config, new job | hit on `a19e8a54…` (no new entry written) | 44.6, 41.2, 42.4, 47.4, 47.0, 38.1 s |

- The controlled test used one cache key, `jit_train_step-61378ece…`, in both stages. The executable fingerprint and compiled-text SHA256 match.
- The slow process is GPU-bound: ~350 of 411 s of a 3-step trace is on the compute stream, and ~100 s/step is in Triton GEMM fusions with small tiles (block 64, 768 B shared memory).
- Ruled out: autotune level (the fast program was also compiled at level 0, and the cached copy is the same executable), the per-fusion autotune cache (the cached autotune sets for the slow and fast trees match on 131,051 of 131,072 sampled keys), checkpointing, row content, and code version.
- Autotune level 4 was tried once: the compile finished in 41 s, but no step completed in 2.5 h (separate hang, not diagnosed).
- Compile records:
  - miss: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/base-start-fp32-redo-20261119/mochi-5cb/control-compile-prejob/compile-record.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Flong-loop-436%2Fbase-start-fp32-redo-20261119%2Fmochi-5cb%2Fcontrol-compile-prejob%2Fcompile-record.json))
  - hit: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/long-loop-436/base-start-fp32-redo-20261119/mochi-5cb/control/compile-record.json` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Flong-loop-436%2Fbase-start-fp32-redo-20261119%2Fmochi-5cb%2Fcontrol%2Fcompile-record.json))
- Profile trace of the slow process: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/xprof/task504-distill-b-soft-20261119-profile/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxprof%2Ftask504-distill-b-soft-20261119-profile%2F))

**Why it matters**

The first run of any new config (code change, new schedule, new data shapes) compiles its own step and runs ~3x slower for its whole length. A config that differs from a warmed template looks 3x slower without anyone noticing why.

**Workaround**

Run a short warm-up job first: the same config, stopped after 3 updates, on the same `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR`. Then start the real run and check that no new `jit_train_step` entry is written, or look for `Persistent compilation cache hit for 'jit_train_step'`.

**Open question**

What differs between the compiling process and a loading process? Candidates include a kernel choice made at compile time and then replaced on load, memory placement or allocator state left by compilation, and leftover autotuning buffers. A profile of both processes on the same executable would show which kernels differ.

Found by duiker (controlled test) and otter (task 504). Related: PR 11732.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The controlled cache miss and hit use the same `jit_train_step` cache key and executable fingerprint, yet steady steps take about 122 and 42–49 seconds. The available device trace covers only the slow process, so it cannot show whether the fast process runs different kernels or runs the same kernels faster. The Long Loop step is one donated JIT call; related slow steps in #11646 do not establish a shared cause.

**Relevant code**
- [`train.py#L1264-L1280`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/454902f11d08aaaf89bb8b177896a533aabb6db5/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/train.py#L1264-L1280) — donated JIT step.
- [`train.py#L1743-L1771`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/454902f11d08aaaf89bb8b177896a533aabb6db5/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/train.py#L1743-L1771) — optional AOT compile before dispatch.
- [`launch_arms.py#L61-L86`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/454902f11d08aaaf89bb8b177896a533aabb6db5/experiments/post_training/teacher_distill/launch_arms.py#L61-L86) — shared remote cache setup.
- [`launch_arms.py#L112-L119`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/454902f11d08aaaf89bb8b177896a533aabb6db5/experiments/post_training/teacher_distill/launch_arms.py#L112-L119) — bounded profile and warm-up runs.

# Proposed Fix

1. On the same 8×8 H100 geometry, run a short cache-miss job followed by a cache-hit job with pinned source, image, `XLA_FLAGS`, input shapes, and cache URI. Record at least three unprofiled steady steps in each. Verify the cache key, executable fingerprint, and optimized HLO match before interpreting timing.
2. Capture two or three steady XPlane steps from each process at the same relative update. Compare kernel names, launch counts, GEMM tile choices, per-kernel duration, compute/collective time, and idle gaps with `profile_summary.py`. Confirm profiling preserves the slow/fast ordering; the existing slow-only trace cannot make this comparison.
3. If kernel choices differ, inspect XLA compile/load and autotune decisions. If choices match but runtimes differ, compare `cuda_async` allocator state, scratch availability, module-load activity, and direct compiled-executable versus stock JIT dispatch. Keep the executable and workload fixed while changing one runtime condition at a time.
4. Patch the isolated cause in Marin or report a minimal JAX/XLA replay upstream. Qualify a fix with repeated short miss/hit pairs, finite losses, no new cache entry on hits, and a steady-step gap below 10%.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 A second, separate slowdown seen in the same runs: the first-step host rebind (`rebind_first_state` in `experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/state_rebind.py`) is sometimes slow enough to kill the job.

The rebind snapshots the train state to host memory (12,802,939,936 bytes on each rank), deletes the device buffers, and restores them. The bytes and memory figures are the same in every run below, but the time varies widely:

| Run (64 H100, cw-us-east-02a) | Rank 0 rebind | Outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| 8 h e12 FP32 template, 2026-11-18 | 7 s | ran |
| 1 h distill arm A (cache hit), 2026-11-19 23:30 | 7 min 54 s (slowest rank done ~10 min after start) | ran |
| 8 h distill A warm-up, 2026-11-20 01:06 | 11 min 48 s | **died** |
| 8 h distill B warm-up, 2026-11-20 01:06 | 8 min 6 s | ran |
| 8 h distill A warm-up, 2026-11-20 11:55 | 7 s (slowest rank 2 min 33 s) | ran |
| 8 h distill B warm-up, 2026-11-20 11:56 | 2 min 32 s | ran |

- How it kills the job: ranks that finish the rebind enter step 1 and wait for the NCCL clique ID from process 0. If process 0 is still rebinding after `--xla_gpu_nccl_termination_timeout_seconds` (600 s in the e12 runtime profile), they fail with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: GetKeyValue() timed out with key: cuda:root_process: 0`.
- For example, process 0's 12.8 GB snapshot took 11 min 48 s, about 18 MB/s.
- Workaround used in PR 11732: raise that flag to 1800 s. Note that this flag is part of the JAX compile cache key, so changing it needs a new warm-up (see above).
- Cause unknown. It does not depend on whether the process compiled or loaded the step program: the slow 1 h case was a cache hit. Host memory before the rebind was similar in fast and slow runs (rank RSS ~19 GB, cgroup 142-155 GB of 687 GB).

spillover_issues.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
spillover_issues.body:
A Daytona connection reset while a task machine runs a model command or the grader ends the rollout, and the quick loop masks it from training. In a Quick RL Loop run on 164 Linux and shell-simulator forge tasks (3 updates, 512 rollouts each), resets caused 2 of the 7 masked rollouts:

```
Task d13.stormwater.flood_risk/23 interrupted during advance: TaskMachineError (DaytonaConnectionError: Failed to execute command: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer)
Task d09.traffic_operations_control/17 interrupted during grade: TaskMachineError (DaytonaConnectionError: Failed to execute command: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer)
```

#11762 restarts a non-Harbor rollout only when the reset happens at `RolloutOperation.START`, before the model has run. A reset during `ADVANCE` or `GRADE` loses the turns already generated.

A third rollout in the same run failed with no cause in the log:

```
Task d40.animation.three_d.deforming_character_rig/14 interrupted during advance: TaskMachineError
```

`_failed_rollout` in `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py` appends the cause only when it is a `DaytonaError`, so any other cause of a `TaskMachineError` is not logged.

Done when:
- A connection reset during a command or during grading no longer discards the rollout when the command can be safely re-run or the rollout continued on a new machine.
- Every `TaskMachineError` warning names its underlying cause, redacted.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

One `Machine.run` on Daytona sends several provider requests: create the command directory, upload the script, run the script, measure and download the output, and remove the files ([`DaytonaMachine.run`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6484db037/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/daytona/machine.py#L348-L465)). A `DaytonaConnectionError` from any of them leaves `run` unhandled. `_OwnedMachine.run` wraps it in a `TaskMachineError` ([machines.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6484db037/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/machines.py#L40-L45)), and the task worker masks the rollout.

All of these requests except the one that runs the script give the same result when they run twice. The request that runs the script is different: the provider can start the command before the connection drops.

The warning has no cause for the third rollout because `_failed_rollout` appends the cause only when it is a `DaytonaError` ([task_worker.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f6484db037/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py#L323-L327)).

## Proposed Fix

1. The Daytona machine repeats a repeatable request that lost its connection, up to three times with backoff. `upload` and `download` restart as a whole.
2. The command script claims its private directory before it runs, and the exit trap records the exit code. After a lost connection the machine repeats the request, which starts the command only if the first request did not. The machine then reads the exit code from the sandbox until the command's timeout. The rollout keeps its turns and its machine.
3. `_failed_rollout` names the redacted cause of every `TaskMachineError`.

A connection that stays lost still masks the rollout. This change does not restart a rollout on a new machine after the model has run; #11762 does that only for a reset at machine start.
